_about: Standalone teachings from the public channel (t.me/HouseOfWews2) that the export never captured, screened from a full read of the channel. Each is filed under its doctrine topics and shown on the chapters it teaches on. Edit titles/topics freely, then rerun tools/clean_studies.py.

teachings.title: Biblical fundamentalism and the Trinity
teachings.summary: Says the fundamentalist stops where scripture presents mystery, as with 1 John 5:7 and Colossians 2:1-4, rather than supplying philosophical machinery to explain the Godhead.
teachings.text:
Seeing people debate the various vain philosophy of men used to explain the position of the Father, the godhood of the incarnate Jesus, the Trinity, the person of the Spirit and the unity of it all, in the fallible and weakness of men's terms. 

Biblical fundamentalism is superior to theology. Heresy answered with heresy is not how we find the truth. 

It is by the revelation of scripture and understanding that some things our finite brain cannot comprehend. And accepting those things by faith.

Where the text of scripture presents mystery, “*great is the mystery of godliness*, ” the fundamentalist stops, where the philosopher and the theologian continue, pressing on in their vain imagination. 

The fundamentalist does not feel obligated to supply the missing metaphysical machinery that finite minds invent to close the gap. And we don't need to take sides in the back-and-forth debates of differing heretical schools of thought. 

Way too many Christians, saved, bible-believing Christians at that, see an answer to a clear heresy that is closer to the truth, and accept that doctrine as solid. They lean on the understanding of traditions. The consensus of the crowd. 

Fundamentalists should never accept presuppositions and systematics that require us to adopt a set of beliefs that come prepackaged, regurgitating apologetics because others before us accepted them whole cloth. 

Always search the scripture to see if it is so. And if you cannot draw a clear, direct understanding of a doctrine or view from plain language and context, then it is ok and in fact wise, to leave it to faith and admit your ignorance as fallible, finite man.

The fundamentalist rejects the theologian's "Sola scriptura," for pure Bible. They use the logic of men, the writings of church fathers and reformers and past generations of men to claim the Bible should be the final arbiter of doctrine. That sliver of daylight given to the authority of tradition and man's philosophy, invites error just as much as the other attempts to answer bad doctrine. 

Taking scripture compared to scripture as the only means of finding truth, and allowing the Bible to be the only authority for matters if faith and practice, avoids these traps. 

And the general understanding of Romans 14, that on secondary matters, men may disagree and be persuaded themselves, without judging another man's servent, makes fundamentalism the way. Primary doctrine is clear. God is not the author of confusion. But where we see through a glass darkly there is room for brotherly disagreement.

**1 John 5:7**
*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

The Bible does not demand that we figure out the metaphysical mechanics of how three can be one. It simply states the fact of their heavenly record and their absolute unity, leaving no room for human rationalization. 

Scripture doesn't get into the mode,  essence or hypostatic union or the filoque or any other nonsense used to debate endlessly the vain wisdom of man. 

It identifies them by their revealed biblical names: Father, Word, and Holy Ghost, and the undeniable fact that these three are one. 

The Bible does not demand that you figure out the metaphysical mechanics of how three can be one. It simply states the fact of their heavenly record and their absolute unity, leaving no room for human rationalization.

1 John 5:6 
*This is he that came by water and blood, even Jesus Christ; not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.*

God anchors the reality of Jesus Christ to historical facts, He was born of water, the incarnation, and he came by blood, the death and resurrection. And the person of the Spirit bears witness to Christ's factual existence and the truth of the gospel. 

There is no need to explain what we know is true. It is just true. 

Verse 9, *If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.*

The theologian and the seminarian and the other "experts," seek to gain our confidence in them. In their arguments and their theories and their jargon. 

But the witness of God is greater. 

Verse 10 *He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.*

We have the Spirit of truth, Who teaches us all things. Who does not speak of Himself, but the good things of God. 

**1 Corinthians 2:12–13**
*Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.*

What more do we need? And this truth speaks expressly of the truth we have known and the gift of eternal life that we may know Him. The truth that is the true God.

**1 John 5:20**
*And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.*

So don't let theologians and men wise in their own conceits tell you that you need to be "educated" as they are to know the truth. 

God Himself testifies with us the truth of His Son. Amen.

**Colossians 2:1–4**
*For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh; That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ; In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. 

And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.*

The beguiling men with enticing words seek to lead us from the truth. Paul in the Spirit is giving prophecy that applies to Christians today as much as it did the Colossians and the Laodiceans. 

Our hearts may be comforted with the assurance of full understanding, even as we acknowledge the mystery of God. Of the Father and of Christ and ALL of the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. 

**Colossians 2:6–9**
*As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving. Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.*

We have received Christ, sealed by the Spirit in Jesus, we are rooted in Him. We are called to walk in Him, and because we are established in the faith, secure in our knowledge of the truth, we can never deny Him, but we can be spoiled by deceivers. Led away by vain traditions of men, following the ways of the world, the logic of men. Following the theology and theory and disputations of denomination and schools of thought, instead of Christ. 

The fulness of the Godhead is stated as a fact, *in* Christ. The scripture does not seek to define His "essence," substance, or the mechanics of that fulness. God's word simply declares it, its truth, and then warns against the very methods that later generations of men would use to elaborate it. Their philosophy, traditions of men, and the rudimentary or elementary principles of the world. The natural man view. 

The vain and puffed up philosophy, groups of men with creeds and confessions that add to and take away the things of Christ, teaching for commandments the doctrines of men. 

**Colossians 2:16–18**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind*

These are the tip of the iceberg, the various ways false teachers use their own imagination to invent how we should live, what we should do, and condemning those of us who place our trust entirely with Christ and His word.

teachings.title: Soul winning is an act of faith and love
teachings.summary: Says door-to-door soul winning is not about pride or bragging rights but an act of faith and love, which is why it needs encouraging.
teachings.text:
If door to door soul-winning was about bragging rights, pride, being holier than thou...Then far more professing Christians would be out doing it. 

It is sometimes difficult to get everyone on board with, and encouraging them to get with the program is needed precisely because it is an act of faith, done of love of Christ and duty, with worldly rewards out competing that love. 

Any efforts to discourage it are wicked. 

Go soul-winning!

teachings.title: Wise as serpents, harmless as doves
teachings.summary: Uses Matthew 10:16, Matthew 18:16-17 and 2 Timothy 2:16-18 to say grace without discernment is a vulnerability wolves exploit.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 10:16**
*Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.*

Many Christians often fall into the trap of being harmless as doves, while failing to be wise as serpents. 

We tend to feel the need to show Grace and to try to bridge peace and avoid conflict in every situation. To be as sheep in both mind and spirit. 

But the wolves take advantage of this. 

Jesus says to be as wise as serpents. To understand the context and nature of those who come into our lives and exert a negative influence. 

Part of the problem is that we don't attempt to discern the intents of the heart of the person who we are dealing with. Sometimes they'll say something that has a grain of truth, and in the interest of fairness and to seem reasonable, we will validate their premise. But their premise may be in bad faith. They may not be seeking a dialogue and to come to an understanding. Their intent is to throw bombs. Sow discord. To validate slander in the interest of promoting their own agenda. 

Even those who come in, in error, weak in the faith, maybe confused or wrong on some doctrinal point, or turned around by something they've heard that you know is wrong, we are warned against giving them space to stay in error and to spread it. 

**Romans 14:1**
*Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.*

Yes we should cater to those who are ignorant, or convicted about something that isn't explicitly taught in the Bible, and we should attempt to correct them in love. 

But when they come in with doubtful disputations, that is creating turmoil and breaking the unity of the brotherhood of saints? Him we should not receive. 

Part of the problem often stems from the fact that we can't imagine how evil people might behave. We cut them slack. We give them grace based on our own conscience's sake, and show them kindness and mercy that only encourages and emboldens them. 

If they're simply in error, and too prideful or ignorant to accept rebuke, after you've admonished them kindly, shake the dust. 

**Titus 3:10**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;*

This is especially true at the door when you are out soul winning. It does no one any good to get bogged down in the doubtful disputation. 

Defending yourself against a false accusation built on bad faith premises does nothing but legitimize the other person's point. 

If someone accused you of being incestuous with your mother, your reaction should not be "I am not!" it should be "You're wicked!" You don't defend yourself from slander by reasoning with the slanderer. You identify them for what they're doing, and rebuke them. 

But the issue becomes entertaining these sowers of division in a house of God or in a space of fellowship. Not throwing them out at the first sign of their behavior. 

What that does is allow their contention to grow, and to draw others in to deal with it. 

Further you encourage those sheep who aren't as wise as serpents, to compromise with the truth in order to bring peace to the situation. To try to smooth things over. To debate the slander as a point with merit. 

This only encourages wolves and keeps the confused and weak-in-the-faith brother, in error. 

God hates those who sow division. 

**Proverbs 6:14–19**
*Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord. Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy. These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

We as Christians have absolutely no obligation to give them a platform to do the things that God hates, but rather to expel them and turn them over to Satan. 

If they are saved believers, God will deal with it. But the Bible says we are to treat them as heathen.

**Matthew 18:16–17**
*But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican*.

You should not allow someone free rein to spew lies and indignities, to overthrow the faith of some.

Grace without discernment isn't biblical peace; it is a vulnerability that wolves exploit. 

**2 Timothy 2:16–18**
*But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.*

It doesn't matter if the vain babblings are denying the future resurrection of saints, slandering men of God and their works, discouraging the first love of the faith, soul-winning, or teaching a false gospel that says men are made elect by their genealogy. 

It increases ungodliness among the brethren and overthrows the faith of some.

teachings.title: Watch
teachings.summary: Sets the warning of Proverbs 7:18-20 beside the call to watch in Matthew 24:42-44 and Mark 13.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 7:18–20**
*Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves. For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed.*

**Matthew 24:42–44**
*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.*

Christians are called to watch for the return of Christ, being good and faithful servants, and not letting the delay of His return lull us into sin.

**Matthew 24:46–51**
*Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

This is why we preach separation unto the Gospel, being a holy people and working to do the will of the Lord, so that when we are found approved in that day. 

But the evil servant is like the foolish woman, calling others to sin. 

**Mark 13:33–37**
*Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is. For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch. Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.*

teachings.title: Tradition against the commandment of God
teachings.summary: Quotes Matthew 15:3-8 and says Jesus supported the death penalty for cursing father or mother.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 15:3–8**
*But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.*

If you're against the death penalty for murders while Jesus was for it for those that curse their parents, you ain't right.

teachings.title: The peace of God keeps the heart
teachings.summary: Gathers Colossians 3:15-17, Philippians 4:6-7 and Isaiah 26:2-3 on the peace of God as a promise to those who trust Him.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 3:15–17**
*And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.*

**Philippians 4:6–7**
*Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. **And the peace of God,** which passeth all understanding **shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.***

**Isaiah 26:2–3**
*Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in. **Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.***

The Lord keeps those whose mind stays on Him, Whom they have trusted. God keeps your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. 

No matter what you call this, it is a promise of God. Let God be true and every man a liar!

teachings.title: Reasonable service and unseen rewards
teachings.summary: Says keeping the law and loving others is the bare minimum, as Luke 17:7-10 shows, and that Matthew 25:35-40 shows rewards for things done unknowingly.
teachings.text:
Side note. When we don't sin and we follow the law to the best of our human ability and we love our neighbors and our brothers and sisters in Christ, and we forgive others, we are doing the bare minimum. It's our reasonable service. 

**Luke 17:7–10**
*But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat? And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink? Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not. So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.*

Of course we're going to receive rewards that have been promised to us for doing great works for Christ. 

And while I don't know exactly, I would imagine some of the things that we were commanded to do will produce rewards. Crowns in the next life. 

But the things that we're commanded to do are the bare minimum. I suppose it's the heart behind the things that we do, rather than the simple obedience that God looks at and rewards. I think God gives credit for effort, context and the spirit it was done in. 

I think Paul's warning about the wood, wood and stubble getting burnt up and suffering loss, is because there will be things that we absolutely expect to receive a reward for that ultimately were just our reasonable service. 

And we are going to receive crowns of Glory for acts that we didn't even consider were reward-worthy at the time. Things that Jesus looks at and says this was precious stones, silver or gold. Things where He will say well done my good and faithful servant, that we don't remember doing.

**Matthew 25:35–40**
*For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.*

While we are promised rewards, and it's often discussed the nature of them and how they are earned and what qualifies as precious stone or silver or gold, it's the little acts of love where Christ's light shines through us and others glorify God, where his mercy and his grace is magnified through the acts that we do simply because we are children of God, without any thought for ourselves. 

In fact, it's very likely that the things we expect a reward for will be burned and we will suffer loss, but it will be the times we unknowingly entertained angels, offered comfort and gave hospitality to the hopeless that will be judged worthy, on that day.

teachings.title: The Bema seat and wood, hay and stubble
teachings.summary: Explains that bad works at the Bema seat means worthless works for the kingdom, not a list of confessed or covered sins.
teachings.text:
At the Bema Seat, "bad" or wood, hay and stubble, does not mean God pulls out a list of your confessed or covered sins to punish you for them. It means he evaluates the things you did that were worthless for the Kingdom. Things like time wasted (arguing online**👀**), fleshly ambitions (popularity), or religious works done for the praise of men. 

Those works are burned up, resulting in a loss of reward, not a infliction of punishment.

teachings.title: The angel of the LORD and Sennacherib
teachings.summary: Reads 2 Kings 19:35-36 on God's deliverance, noting that He sometimes responds to prayer out of His own pleasure and plans.
teachings.text:
**2 Kings 19:35–36**
*And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses. So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.*

When Jerusalem was surrounded and under siege, is likely when **Psalm 44** was written and sung. 

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. **For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.***

It is always interesting to see that it was the preservation of Jerusalem itself and the promise made to David that motivated God to act. 

King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah tore their clothes, humbled themselves, and cried out to God in intense prayer for deliverance. The sons of Korah wrote and sang Psalms. The people lamented and prayed. 

But, what seems to have motivated Him wasn't necessarily His people. God considered His pleasure, promises and plans, and relented, confounding and destroying the army before the gates. 

It pleased Him to defend the city, to save it, for His own sake, and the promise He had made. 

Many times, our effectual and fervent prayers are answered, and God delivers us out of mercy and grace. But sometimes, it is His pleasure, promises and plans that He responds to. 

It is something to keep in mind as we look to do His will and take joy in it being done.

teachings.title: Believers cannot apostasize, continued
teachings.summary: Sums up that believers cannot apostasize and apostates cannot believe, with Hebrews 6:7-9, and urges comparing scripture with scripture.
teachings.text:
TL:DR - Believers cannot apostasize and apostates cannot believe

**Hebrews 6:7–9**
*For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned. But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.*

Here, the Bible gives us the parable to explain the apostasy verses that came before it. 

The same rains and earth are given to both the dressed fields that bring forth herbs also brings forth thorns and briers, rejected and cast into the fire. 

This directly applies to those that tasted of the truth, but did not consume, who see the power of the Spirit but never trusted the truth. They are the thorns and briers. The saved are the herbs meet for the dresser (the fruit of those who won them to Christ). The ground that bears thorns isn't good soil that "lost" its status; it is bad ground whose true nature was finally exposed by the rain.

The parable explains the concept beautifully. 

It does not say the herbs become thorns, let alone that briers eventually are turned to fruit. 

And so Paul, having explained this concept, reassures the believers he is writing to. 

**Hebrews 6:9**
*But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.*

The fundamental problem is that people accept things without actually comparing scripture with scripture, to see if the thing they are being told is so. 

They don't have enough Bible knowledge to do anything but to regurgitate proof texts that they were given, that they accepted at face value. And worse, when presented with context of their proofs, that show that the cherry-picked eisegesis is wrong, and why, they just dig in their heels and act like fools. 

Clowns.

teachings.title: Believers cannot apostasize
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 1, 1 John 2 and Hebrews 6 that the saved cannot fall away or believe a strong delusion, and that apostates never believed.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18–23**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

That which may be known of God is made manifest by His wrath revealed from Heaven. Man has no excuse. 

Many have this understanding, the law written in their hearts and the conviction of the Spirit, and the wonder of creation and even the example of mercy towards the saved believer...and still don't repent towards the gospel, perishing in their sins. 

But these people being described know the truth of God and hold it in unrighteousness. They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They reject the truth for a lie. They worship themselves and the created over the Creator. And God gives them up to a reprobate (rejected) mind. 

For those that not only had the manifest truth of God, but a clear articulation of the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ Jesus, understand it, and even profess to assent to it, and then reject it? They are worse off than those that simply never hear or consider it. 
These have forsaken the right way;

**2 Peter 2:17**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.*

The apostates are reprobate, twice-dead. Not only dead and hellbound in the next world, but conscience seared and accursed in this one. 
**2 Peter 2:21**
*For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.*

But we who have trusted the truth in our hearts have a more sure hope. We have the Spirit of truth to defend us from the spirit of error. Jesus said it is impossible to fool the elect. 

But for the fallen away, God gives them strong delusions as punishment for their rejection of the truth. 

2 **Thessalonians 2:10–12**
*And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness*.

But praise God this is not possible for a believer. We are kept from falling by the power of God. By the witness of the Spirit. By the perfect work of Christ, knowing we have not believed in vain. 

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

Regarding the lie that those who are saved CAN fall away, can believe a strong delusion, can be fooled, the Bible teaches this is not possible.

**1 John 2:18–27**
*Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time. **They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us**. **But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things. I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth, but because ye know it,** and that no lie is of the truth. 

Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son. Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also. 

Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning. **If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father**. And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life. These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you. **But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie**, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.*

John continues;

**1 John 4:1–6**
*Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. **Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.** They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and **the world heareth them**. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** **Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.***

This is the unction of the holy Spirit. This Spirit of truth. That we hear those of God and reject those heard of the world by their false teaching. 

**John 10:1–5**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out. And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. *

***And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.***

We who are saved WILL NOT FOLLOW the stranger. We hear Jesus' voice. This is the promise of God.

**John 10:26–30**
*But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand. I and my Father are one.*

It is impossible for a saved child of God to fall away into apostasy. The trust in a false way, after knowing and assenting to the truth in their hearts. And it is impossible for an apostate to ever be saved once they've rejected the truth.

**Hebrews 6:4–6**
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

Anyone teaching that saved believers can reject the truth, believe a lie, have strong delusion, and apostasize, is wrong. It's heresy. It is not possible. 

Just as it is not possible for one who went out from us, who held the truth in unrighteousness and didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge, to ever come to the knowledge of the truth.

The Bible warns repeatedly against false prophets, false teachers who try to lead away people with itching ears by their vain jangling. Creeping unawares in order to spy out our liberty, and to make merchandise of us. 

Just like Satan, they try to make you doubt God's word in order to get you to sin. Or to believe foolishness. A saved believer can be led away into believing some heresies that are couched in the truth. 

These heresies are not necessarily apostasy. In order for it to be apostasy, it has to change the truth of God into a lie. 

Not all heresies are damnable. Not all heresies force someone to become apostates by their adopting them as a school of thought or a systematic that they apply to or over their existing faith. 

Nor does a heart that is no longer perfect towards God, but has added other elements of worship into their true faith, make someone an apostate. Yes they are not right and yes they are backslidden and yes they will face the chastening of God, but they have not lost their salvation. Theologians call adding falsehoods or heresies to true faith syncretism.

Solomon was guilty of this. He never rejected the Lord God or the temple he was given to build or the covenant and sacrifices that represented the Christ to come. But his heart was turned away to other gods by the love of his wives, partaking in their idolatry in addition to the truth he held in his heart. 

This applies to saved believers who use terms like repent of your sins, or who believe in some of the elements of Calvinism and predestination. Or who get caught up in other false doctrines, or never fully abandon the religion that they were won out of.

It may apply to someone who trusted in Christ at the door when a soul winner came and presented the gospel to them, but out of habit and loyalty and family ties they continue on going to a Catholic Church for example. 

Naaman was a Syrian general who asked the Lord for forgiveness for entering an idol's temple with his king, after believing on the truth of God. 

**2 Kings 5:18**
*In this thing the LORD pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the LORD pardon thy servant in this thing.*

He had full knowledge of what he was doing and understood that it was wrong. I would assume Solomon did too, knowing the punishment he received through his son and the divided Kingdom for his spiritual adultery. 

But there are thousands and thousands of saved believers who after trusting in God, and the blood of Christ, neglect to walk in the Spirit, and read the Bible and learn God's ways. Those who simply went back to their Catholic church or their Mormon church or whatever apostate cult they were in, and while it may prick them in the heart they might not recognize why. 

But what they'll never do is trust in the false gospel of that church. Just as Naaman never trusted in the false gods of his people ever again.

And I think it's curious that this current heresy - that a saved believer could apostasize and could believe a false gospel in their heart, or reject the truth of God utterly, has been creeping up over the past few years. 

It's a twist on Arianism, which holds that a saved believer can become apostate and lose salvation. By adding the assurance of salvation to it, it allows them to lead away babes in Christ or people who aren't fully trusting the truth, and give them cover to chase after delusions. 

A believer they lead away with this vein jangling won't lose their salvation obviously. They also won't come to believe a lie ultimately because they can't. But they'll introduce doubt and they'll give a bad testimony and when the false teacher can get baby Christians to slander men of God, soul-winning efforts, the teaching of Truth, they ultimately hurt the cause of Christ.

But a nominal Christian, someone who has not fully believed unto salvation, it allows them to continue in whatever lie they are holding on to to avoid repentance. 

And it softens them up to be led away by whatever other strange doctrine the false teacher decides to impart upon their proselytes. He makes them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves.

These false teachers are attempting to have it both ways. They use the comforting banner of "Once Saved, Always Saved" as a Trojan horse to smuggle in a license for total apostasy, claiming a person can completely deny Christ, turn to paganism, or become an atheist, and that God will simply override their will and force them to believe in the end.

This teaching collapses under the weight of Scripture for several critical reasons. 

It redefines Faith as a meaningless past transaction, that purchased salvation, Rather than treating belief as a state of being. It becomes a transient action in their minds, rather than the reality their heart would live in if they believe the truth. 

Of course we reject Calvinism, so there is no forcing of faith or salvation onto someone who has utterly rejected it. The Bible says they're ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Jesus says depart for me I never knew you. 

It invents a class of people that the Bible doesn't say exists. There is a binary of those who believe and those who are condemned already because they have not believed. There is no third option. 

They purposefully overlook the power of the Holy Spirit and His purpose, to seal the believer, guide us to all truth and show the spirit of error. 

While that doesn't rise to the level of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, in my opinion, it sure does come close.

teachings.title: The mind of Christ and humility
teachings.summary: Reads Philippians 2:5-8 to urge believers to be humble as Christ humbled Himself, condescending to men of low estate that they may be saved.
teachings.text:
**Philippians 2:5–8**
*Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.*

Jesus being God and knowing he was God still condescended to become man. God humbled himself to take on mortality for the whole world. 

Let this mind be in you. Be humble. Be humble to others. Condescend to men of low estate that they may be saved.

teachings.title: Prayer for the lost and going soul winning
teachings.summary: Says a prayer for the lost is also a call for the believer to go and show them the gospel, and urges members to support the church's children's services and soul winning.
teachings.text:
Everyone wants children's services, no one wants to work them. 

If you want more out of your church than you're willing to put in and then backbite and complain, instead of supporting your pastor and helping out (and taking care of your unruly children is bare minimum BTW), you have a bad spirit and aren't right with God. 

You can be 3-to-thrive, and still not be right with Jesus, if the spirit you have is wrong. 

If you aren't volunteering to help and your kids are a nightmare, you need to be rebuked and convicted. Not coddled and catered to.

This goes doubly for soul-winning. 

There are people who ask that their family and friends be added to the prayers for the lost that folks at Wendsay night prayer service gladly pray for, when the people asking never darken the door of the church outside of Sunday morning, and never show up for door knocking. 

There are Christians in the lives of those strangers we minister the gospel to, praying that their loved ones get saved, too. 

If you want soulwinners to bring the truth of Christ to your loved ones, but can't be bothered to go out and warn who you can, don't be surprised when your prayers go unanswered in that regard. 

**Romans 10:13–17**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. **How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!** But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report? So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

Every prayer for the lost is a prayer that the Spirit not only softens the heart of the unsaved, but that He also brings soulwinners into their lives to show them the gospel from scripture. 

The Spirit not only is convicting the lost loved one, but should be convicting you as a saved believer to go out into the highways and hedges, bringing that gospel of peace to whoever you can.  To be an ambassador for Christ in the ministry of reconciliation. 

**2 Corinthians 5:17–20**
*Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation; To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.*

teachings.title: What worship means in scripture
teachings.summary: Shows from the Hebrew shachah, translated worship, bow and obeisance, that Catholics change the meaning of worship to excuse idolatry.
teachings.text:
When a Catholic tells you you don't understand what "worship means" they are actually changing the meaning of the word to obfuscate their idolatry. 

The Hebrew term (שָׁחָה / shachah) is used 172 times in the Old Testament - translated as “worship” 99 times, “bow” 31, “bow down” 18, “obeisance” 9, “reverence” 5, “fall down” 3.

Defined as to depress/prostrate oneself (especially in homage to a superior, royalty, or God) i.e., to bow, kneel, or fall down in respect and deference.

The primary Greek term (proskuneō) accounts for the great majority of NT occurrences of “worship” (60 times) and is defined as "to fall upon the knees, touch the ground with the forehead/kneel or prostrate oneself" in homage or obeisance (whether to express respect or make supplication).

**Exodus 20:4–5**
*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me*

The term is explicitly rendered as "bow" in the 2nd Commandment, and carries with it no qualifiers or anything indicating that the "level of honor" given when bowing and making supplication to an image or idol has any bearing when considering the commandment. 

There is no question that bowing before an image or idol, regardless of what it is meant to represent, is strictly forbidden. 

**Deuteronomy 5:7–10**
*Thou shalt have none other gods before me. Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.*

There is no mention of special religious worship for images of God, versus images of men, where it is allowed. 

Jeroboam created a new religion for Israel, with images of golden calves that were meant to represent the Lord God of Israel, and God destroyed them for it:

**1 Kings 12:28–32**
*Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan. And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Bethel, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.*

And because of this false religion of idolatry, God judged Israel 

**1 Kings 15:30**
*Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger.*

It is no wonder that every nation that becomes majority Catholic is judged by God, and is either wiped out with famine, war, disease or invasion and ethnic replacement.

teachings.title: Blessed when persecuted
teachings.summary: Quotes Matthew 5:10-12 and Mark 8:35 on being persecuted for righteousness and not saving one's life.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:10–12**
*Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.*

Professing Christians who express fear of the Tribulation, and persecution of the saints by the beast, saying they will flee and hide, are cowards and have little (if any) faith. 

It is wicked to be a "prepper" during the end times. Those who engage in this will be like the Jews who fled Jerusalem during the Babylonian captivity, seeking safety in Egypt. 

They were hunted down and slain. The prophet warned them;

**Jeremiah 42:19**
*The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day.*

Because they chose to rebel and hide like cowards, rather than trust God's plan, Jeremiah was instructed to prophesy that the Babylonians would invade Egypt and wipe them out, Even as the Jews forced Jeremiah and his scribe to go with them.

**Jeremiah 44:14,27**
*For none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah...Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.*

And the prophecy comes to pass. 

**Jeremiah 44:28–30**
*Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs. And this shall be a sign unto you, saith the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaohhophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.*

Secular history confirms that Pharaoh Hophra (Apries) was overthrown and killed during a bitter civil war and the subsequent Babylonian invasion which targeted the regions that the Jews fled to, fulfilling the exact sign God promised to prove the doom of the Jews who fled there. Jeremiah himself and his scribe Baruch, survived to preserve this record. 

Any Christian worth his salt should know that if they seek to save their life, they will lose it. 

**Mark 8:35**
*For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's, the same shall save it.*

teachings.title: Read it for yourself
teachings.summary: Warns that studying other people's theology and hermeneutics is easier than reading the text yourself, and that eschatology should be read from scripture rather than a prepackaged outline.
teachings.text:
Part of the problem is laziness. Too many Christians, including pastors and professors study to learn theology and hermeneutics, and to understand what other people have interpreted, because it is "easier" than just reading it for yourself. 

Eschatology can seem daunting, but if someone hands you a prepackaged outline and charts, you can just adopt it as your own. 

The same with soteriologies like Calvinism. (Although this is harder to pull off if a student is already saved and has a firm understanding of the gospel). 

In the end, many believers are no better off than Catholics who trust in a "magistrum" to interpret and tell them what the Bible says. 

*Prove all things; hold fast that which is good...Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. *

Search the scriptures to see if the things being taught are so. Don't blindly accept them because of authority or traditions.

teachings.title: Allegories, parables and dogmatic literalism
teachings.summary: Says a major source of heresy is taking allegories, parables and pictures in scripture and applying a dogmatic literalism to them.
teachings.text:
Probably the biggest source of heresy is the tendency to take allegories and parables and pictures of things given by God in His word that we can have better understanding, and applying a dogmatic literalism to them. Even conflicting images using similar terms about different topics become standardized to support a doctrine that is not necessarily being taught. 

This creates presuppositional terms that shut down thought. 

Terms like elect, repent, the church, the bride, the wedding supper, Abraham's bosom, Jacob's trouble, and others lead to a drastic misunderstanding at best and foolish heresy at worse. 

Rather than allowing the Bible to explain itself in the context, people plug in their own ideas and systematics, usually that they have learned from others and adopted unquestionably. 

Once they've been adopted, proof texting becomes a substitute for exegesis. And so every instance needs to be conformed to the pre-existing idea instead of just hearing what God's saying.

teachings.title: Two trees in Eden
teachings.summary: Reads Genesis 2:8-10 as God giving man two options from the beginning, the tree of knowledge of good and evil, the law, and the tree of life, which is by faith in God's word.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 2:8-10**
*And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed. And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.  And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.*

From the beginning God gave two options to the man He had created; the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the law, and the tree of life, which is by faith in the word of God.

teachings.title: Mary needed a Saviour too
teachings.summary: Applies Romans 4 to Mary, saying she was redeemed by her Lord and Saviour and that the Catholic view of a sinless Mary denies the gospel of justifying the ungodly.
teachings.text:
What shall we say then that Mary our sister in Christ, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Mary were justified by works, she hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

They don't believe the gospel. That Jesus justifies the ungodly, and His righteousness is given. A new man created by the baptism of the Spirit. And our sins and iniquity He remembers no more. 

So Mary has to be born sinless somehow, and fully obedient to the law her whole life, just as Jesus was. They can't comprehend Mary being redeemed by her Lord and Savior.

teachings.title: Forgiving and praying for others' sins
teachings.summary: Teaches from 1 John 5:16-17 and John 20:23 that believers should forgive others and ask God to forgive them.
teachings.text:
The New Testament explicitly teaches that we who are saved should forgive the trespasses of others against us. That we should pray to God to forgive them. 

**1 John 5:16-17**
*If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it. All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.*

**John 20:23**
*Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained"*

This is a duty of all believers. To say "forgive them Father, for they know not what they do."

teachings.title: Continue in the grace of God
teachings.summary: Shows from Acts 13:43 that converts were persuaded to continue in the grace of God, and that there was never a different plan of salvation, only grace by faith.
teachings.text:
**Acts 13:43**
*Now when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas: who, speaking to them, **persuaded** them to continue in the grace of God.*

These Jews and Gentile proselytes, or converts to the Hebrew religion of the Old Testament, were persuaded to *continue in the grace of God*. Not repent. Not leave the faith, but to continue in it, knowing Jesus was the Christ. The Messiah that the prophets all gave witness to. The Lord they'd called upon to to be saved. The Deliverer. Him that all them that looked for redemption, for the Savior.

They were persuaded by the scriptures and how they all pointed to Jesus, to continue in the grace of God.

There was never a different plan of salvation. It was always by faith in God's Christ. Paul preached the gospel, according to the scriptures. 

Not a new gospel. Not a different Dispensation. A new covenant that fulfils the old, replacing it with better promises and blessings. 

But it has always been grace entered into by faith.

teachings.title: The reprobate doctrine and the repent-of-sins gospel
teachings.summary: Says those who preach repent-of-your-sins make reprobates into saints, and asks who the dogs, swine, tares and goats in Christ's teaching are.
teachings.text:
If you don't understand what's being taught here, the process of hardening and eventually being given over to that hard heart, I don't know what to tell you. 

Your argument is with God.

People who preach a false "repent-of-your-sins" Gospel, always make Sodomites, who claim to have turned from their sin, into saints. They put them above all other men, because to them it's the ultimate proof of their false gospel. 

Their rationale "If turning from being a filthy sodomite, the worst sin, if that  doesn't get you saved, then nothing will!"

They'll claim it's evidence of the power of Christ to change lives. But it's really self-serving. They want to put their faith in the repentance of a homo, because it validates the faith they have in their own turning from sin. 

And no matter how many times it bites them in the ass, where the person they are putting up on a pedestal it turns out to be a false teacher, or a degenerate, or worse, They hold out hope for the next queer who makes merchandise of them by paying lip service to Jesus. 

And many of these vipers become false teachers, given authority over the faith. And they bring in damnable heresy, just as the Bible says they will. 

A large portion of the New Testament is devoted entirely to exposing this behavior and explaining it. 

Jesus teaches about false teachers. We encounter them in Acts. Paul writes against them repeatedly. Peter, Jude, and John talk about it. In the letters from Jesus to the seven local churches in Asia, he talks about it. In Revelation, in the end times, there's literally a false prophet leading a false religion in the name of the beast. 

We're told that they creep in unaware. Wolves and sheep's clothing. Leading away silly women and people with itching ears, bringing with them accursed false gospels. Reprobate concerning the faith. Ever learning and never coming to the knowledge of the truth. Impossible to bring them again to repentance to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. Because they believed in vain. Cuz they continued not in the sayings. They went out from us because they were not of us.

Jesus tells us to not give that which is Holy to dogs, not to cast pearls before swine... That they'll turn and rend you. 

Who do people think the dogs are? Who are the swine in this teaching of Christ? What do people who don't understand the reprobate doctrine and who don't think sodomites are accursed, what do they think this is talking about?

Who are the thistles and briars? Who are the tares? Who are those compassing sea and land to make their follows twofold more the child of Hell than themselves? Who are the goats? Who are the sheep who don't hear His voice? 

WHO DO PEOPLE THINK THESE TEACHINGS ARE ABOUT?

God's word: "Hey, there are false prophets who will try and infiltrate your churches, and lead away people, watch out for them. This is how they got that way, and this is what they do. Biblical fundamentalism is how you protect yourself from them. Love you." 

And people refuse to believe Him.

teachings.title: One gospel in all ages
teachings.summary: Says there has always been one gospel, salvation by calling on the Lord and believing His word by grace through faith, and quotes Galatians 1:8-9.
teachings.text:
There was, is and will always be one gospel. The same in all ages. Salvation by calling upon the name of the Lord, believing His Word. By grace through faith.

**Galatians 1:8-9**
*But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

teachings.title: Supporting preaching against sin
teachings.summary: Urges believers, even when struggling, to say Amen to preaching against sin and for the assembly and the great commission.
teachings.text:
You don't have to be perfect in all your ways, but if you aren't supportive of hard preaching against sin, ESPECIALLY YOUR OWN, even if you're struggling with it, even if you aren't where you ought to be...Then you're a fool. 

Standards and rules are for God's people, that it be well with them. That they go on to perfection. They are goals we should support out of love for one another. 

Stop making excuses and start edifying one another.

Even if you smoke, say "AMEN!" when the preacher speaks against it. 

Even if you're a drunk, say "AMEN!!" when the pastor preached against drunkenness. 

If you struggle to get up Sunday morning, don't go to Sunday night and didn't even realize there's a service on Wednesday, don't you dare sit silent. Say "AMEN!" when the preacher is telling you to not foresake the assembly. 

If you can't be bothered to take up the great commission, and don't go out to share the gospel in the ministry of reconciliation God has commanded us to do, don't you dare act offended when it comes up from the pulpit. 

Even if you're struggling to not have seconds and thirds (and fourths, and a little slice of pie, mmm pie), say "AMEN!!!" when the preacher teaches against gluttony.

If you cuss, if you gossip, if you can't help but share that meme you know you oughtn't.... whatever it is, don't you dare countersignal hard preaching. 

By all means get right, be convicted. But if you ain't right, at least be man enough to admit it is wrong and support the man of God who is calling out sin!

teachings.title: The ten commandments one by one
teachings.summary: Walks through the ten commandments to argue that they are generally easy to keep, if not perfectly.
teachings.text:
People make the 10 Commandments seem like this impossible list of things God asks for us. Sin is the transgression of the law, and these certainly are a cornerstone of the law. But they are genuinely easy to keep generally, if not perfectly.

1 - *I am the Lord thy God...*Thou* shalt have no other gods before me.*
2 - *Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image...Thou shalt not bow down to them or serve them*.
3 - *Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain...*
4 - *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy...Six days shalt thou labor, but the seventh is the sabbath.* (We rest in Christ, Who is our Sabbath)
5 - *Honour thy father and thy mother...That thy days may be long upon the land.*
6 - *Thou shalt not kill.*
7 - *Thou shalt not commit adultery.*
8 - *Thou shalt not steal.*
9 - *Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.*
10 - *Thou shalt not covet...Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, wife, or property*. 

It is easy to not place another god in your life or to avoid idols. It's easy to not take the Lord's name in vain. Christ is our rest. Honoring your parents isn't difficult. Neither is not being a murderer, an adulterer or a liar. It's kind of easy to not covet things that aren't yours and you don't deserve. 

Jesus upped the ante by making it the spirit of these things, holding it in your heart being as bad as acting on it.

teachings.title: Nephilim and serpent seed are not biblical
teachings.summary: Says Nephilim, serpent seed and similar teachings about angels and demons are not biblical and quotes Colossians 2:18.
teachings.text:
Reminder that "Nephilim," "serpent seed" and other false doctrines about angels and demons that men use to make merchandise of simple people are not Biblical, and hurt the cause of Christ. 

***Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind***

Ultimately, demon-human sex-stories are pornography for goofy people.

teachings.title: Soul winning guards against false teachers
teachings.summary: Says saved people who never go soul winning look for things to validate faith and are more open to false teachers, with 2 Peter 2:1-3.
teachings.text:
I think saved people who never go soul-winning tend to need something to validate their faith, because they don't see the power in the word in action. 

It makes them more likely to be taken advantage of.  

**2 Peter 2:1-3**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of. And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.*

Faith grows by obedience, not by paying influencers and "archeologists," or any number of "holy land" scams people get taken in by.

teachings.title: Calling upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Says calling on the Lord is admitting you are a sinner and confessing He is the Christ, not turning from sins, asking Jesus into your heart or giving your life to Him.
teachings.text:
Admitting that you're a sinner. Not "turning from your sins.

Calling upon the name of the Lord isn't "asking Jesus into your heart." It's confessing He is the Christ.

It's not giving your life to Jesus, it's knowing He gave His for you.

teachings.title: Baptist churches and apostolic lineage
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that Baptists have no tradition by tracing independent local churches to the New Testament churches, and says Catholics and Orthodox split from them.
teachings.text:
People say that Baptists have "no tradition," or Apostolic lineage. 

My church traces its doctrine directly back to the Apostles and church fathers. Who founded local independent churches, in Jerusalem, Antioch (Syria), Antioch (Pisidia), Athens, Berea, Caesarea, Cenchrea, Colossae, Corinth, Crete, Cyrene, Damascus, Derbe, Ephesus, Hierapolis, Iconium, Joppa, Laodicea, Lydda, Lystra, Pergamum, Philadelphia, Philippi, Puteoli, Rome, Sardis, Smyrna, Tarsus, Thessalonica, Thyatira, and Troas....

My pastor has been trained directly by the Apostles, to uphold the same traditions those first century churches held to, as God documents in His scriptures.

Catholics and Orthodox are modernist apostates. They split from the New Testament churches and the instruction of the Apostles. More and more over time. 

Because they're built on sinking sand rather than the solid rock of Christ on which we stand.

teachings.title: St. Patrick, an independent missionary
teachings.summary: Quotes Patrick's Confessio to show a 5th century missionary preaching grace by faith and soul winning, outside papal authority.
teachings.text:
St. Patrick was a Baptist missionary sent to Ireland by the independent church in Britain, to preach the gospel, which in Confessio 4, he quotes:

"...He poured out his Holy Spirit on us in abundance, the gift and pledge of immortality, which makes the believers and the obedient into sons of God and co-heirs of Christ who is revealed... Let every tongue confess that Jesus Christ, in whom we believe and whom we await to come back to us... is Lord and God. He is judge of the living and of the dead; he rewards every person according to their deeds."

Confessio 14–15:
"In the knowledge of this faith in the Trinity... it is right to make known the gift of God and his eternal consolation... I didn’t deserve at all that the Lord would grant such great grace, after hardships and troubles, after captivity, and after so many years among that people."

Patrick affirms that obedience to the gospel, and receiving the gift of eternal life and sonship, being co-heirs with Christ, is by the grace of God, and received by faith.

Confessio 3:
"Hence I cannot be silent... about the great benefits and the great grace which the Lord has deigned to bestow upon me in the land of my captivity... for this we can give to God in return after having been chastened by Him, to exalt and praise His wonders."

It's worth noting that while Patrick lived shortly after. Augustine and Pellagius, His isolation from them and Rome and there the introduction of determinism heresy that became Calvinism, he was notably silent on the matter of free will. Preaching a pure Gospel of grace received by faith. 

Confessio 38:
"I am very much God's debtor, who gave me such grace that many people were reborn in God through me and afterwards confirmed... for a people just coming to the faith, whom the Lord took from the utmost parts of the earth."

Patrick, saw the new birth (eternal life/regeneration) as coming by grace to those "coming to the faith"—faith as the response to the gospel call. 

In Confessio 12, Patrick echos the same amazement at the grace of God, that saves a wretch like me and you and him. 

"Before I was brought low, I was like a stone lying deep in the mud. Then he who is powerful came and in his mercy pulled me out, and lifted me up... That is why I must shout aloud in return to the Lord for such great good deeds of his... which the human mind cannot measure."

In Confessio 33, Brother Patrick wrote on his soul-winning mission:

"The Spirit was fervent within me... I pray to God to give me perseverance and to deign that I be a faithful witness to Him to the end of my life for my God." 

Is the same drive we should strive for today. Patrick was a great soul winner.  We should emulate him, and his passion for the gospel, rather than the drunken revelry and excess that Catholics despoil his legacy with. Green beer and bawdy behavior Is more fitting with the pagans he brought the gospel to those professing Christ. 

It was this love of God and the people of Ireland, that gave him innumerable souls won to the Lord. 

Confessio 41 (on the Irish converts):
"How has it lately come about in Ireland that those who never had any knowledge of God... have now been made a people of the Lord, and are called sons of God... How many have been reborn there so as to be of our kind, I do not know..."

Patrick's great success in winning people to Christ is why reclaiming his legacy from the Catholics matters. To be an inspiration to us today. That we don't faint in adversity or fall into the snares of the world. 

Confessio 16:
"The love of God and His fear came to me more and more, and my faith was strengthened. Faith grew, and my spirit was moved..."

Patrick's doctrine shines through his writings; eternal life is by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone.

Stripping away the invented Catholic  hagiography of St. Patrick to reveal the tremendous man of faith behind their legend also reveals that independent churches existed in the 4th and 5th century, with tenuous or no ties to Rome or papal authority. And that their understanding of the Gospel was the same biblical understanding used by Baptists today. 

Patrick, as an evangelical figure from a non-Roman British church tradition, independent of papal authority, does away with the common tropes and traditions Catholics claim always existed in the church. 

He relies on Scripture alone, emphasizing a believer's response to the gospel, and avoids entirely Catholic elements like intercession of saints, Mary,  purgatory, falling out of Grace, priestly confession, veneration of images and idols... All are absent from his writings which are entirely gospel focused. 

His Confessio shows no appeal to Rome for legitimacy, but a strong focus on personal faith and grace, and his mission as the first documented major "independent" missionary enterprise, post-apostles.

The most reputable biographies show that Patrick was British (born ~late 4th/early 5th century), enslaved in Ireland as a youth, escaped, then trained/ordained in Britain (likely as deacon/priest then bishop, possibly in the church his father and grandfather served as elders), and returned as a missionary around 432 AD. A third generation Christian, who potentially could trade by his patriarchal lineage, a direct line to first century Christianity. 

He describes his authority as being given by a divinely called mission, he appeals to no pope or hierarchy for validation, and his Confessio defends his mission against British critics who questioned his calling to Ireland and his burden for the same people who had enslaved him. 

Patrick does not describe or mention baby/infant baptism (paedobaptism) at any point in his writings. 

The two surviving documents universally accepted as genuinely from Patrick himself—his Confessio (Confession) and the Letter to the Soldiers of Coroticus (Epistola), contain several references to baptism, but all of them describe baptisms of converted believers, adults or those who have come to faith through hearing the Gospel, and confession of their faith. 

Patrick emphasizes baptism in the context of missionary preaching: teaching first, then baptizing those who believe, aligning with the Great Commission, which he quotes repeatedly in his writings. All water baptisms Patrick mentions are of converted believers who confirm their faith through response to the Gospel. No babies or infants are referenced.

The true gospel of eternal life and believer's baptism are all he knew, and all he related to others.

teachings.title: Dispensationalism and pre-trib as a shibboleth
teachings.summary: Says dispensationalism and the pre-trib rapture have become tests of orthodoxy in independent churches, but urges submitting to a sound pastor since the right gospel, Bible and soul winning matter most.
teachings.text:
The introduction of dispensationalism and the error of pre-trib rapture has become a defining shibboleth, making what are supposed to be Independent churches into a quasi-denomination through perverse incentives to enforce orthodoxy on these secondary doctrines.

This is how heresy becomes entrenched. It is how the early churches that broke off fellowship to do baby baptism eventually formed the Catholic denomination. Then Orthodox split over how the baptism was performed, not the error of it. Protestants split over corruption in the Roman Church, not the errors, and became their own denominations. 

The strength of the IFB should be their allegiance to Christ and the fundamentals of the word over networking and finances. But error needs to use perverse incentives to protect it, because it can't stand up to scriptural rebuke.

This shouldn't dissuade you from going to the best local, independent, fundamental Baptist Church you can find in your area. Pastor Awes is correct; What matters is the right gospel, the right Bible, soul-winning. A brother can be wrong on the timing of the gathering of the elect. We should submit to the pastor and not seek to sow discord among the brethren. 

But, we can also lovingly point out the hypocrisy of this system when appropriate.

teachings.title: Jesus' brothers and sisters
teachings.summary: Argues from the Greek adelphos that the KJV is correct in saying Jesus had siblings through Mary.
teachings.text:
The Greek ἀδελφός (adelphos, "brother") & ἀδελφή (adelphē, "sister") literally mean "from the same womb" (ἀ- + δελφύς "womb"). NT uses ἀνεψιός (anepsios) for "cousin" (Col 4:10).  God inspired the "same-womb" words deliberately for brothers & sisters, not cousins.

The KJV is correct. Jesus had siblings through Mary.

teachings.title: Acts 8:37 and the preserved text
teachings.summary: Defends Acts 8:37 as genuine scripture, pointing to early quotations of it, and says any Bible that omits it should be discarded in favor of the KJV.
teachings.text:
**Acts 8:37** is not "added" and the 2 "oldest manuscripts" remove a dozen verses, have 1000s of errors and discrepancies. Modern Bibles use these corrupt sources and critics of the preservation of scripture, claim it was added later. But it's not true. 

Irenaeus (d. 202 AD): In his work Against Heresies (180 AD), quotes it directly. 

Cyprian (d. 258 AD)(Treatise 12, Book 3, Section 43)references it in context of baptism requiring belief. 

Tertullian (d. 220 AD): Tertullian alludes to the verse in his writings on baptism, emphasizing the need for a confession of faith, though not a direct quote. His work On Baptism (around 200 AD) reflects similar language and theology.

Ambrosiaster, an anonymous Latin commentator cites Acts 8:37 in discussions of baptismal faith.

Pacian (d. 392 AD), Ambrose (d. 397 AD), and Augustine (d. 430 AD): All reference or quote the verse in their homilies and treatises. 

**Acts 8:37** is not an "addition." 

So beware Bibles that exclude it or call it into question!

Those who rely on "the oldest manuscripts" and call them more reliable, despite all of their errors and contradictions in themselves and with each other, all extra biblical,  sources, and the thousands of manuscripts that do contain these verses, are fools.
