Any Bible that excludes Acts 8:37 should be automatically discarded. Stick with the big boy Bible. The King James.

teachings.title: One way of salvation in every dispensation
teachings.summary: Says animal sacrifice was never a means of salvation and that dispensationalism errs in claiming a different means of salvation for ethnic Jews in the end times.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this but animal sacrifice never was a dispensation or ministration of salvation or grace or a means of justification. The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sin. 

There's only ever been one ministration given to save souls, and that's calling upon the name of the Lord and trusting in Him alone. We have a dispensation to administer the gospel to all men.

The biggest issue with "dispensationalism" isn't the past, it's the unbiblical claim that there will be a different means of salvation or a different dispensation in the end times, reserved for ethnic Jews.

teachings.title: Responsibility, not free will, against Calvinism
teachings.summary: Says the argument against Calvinism is responsibility, noting that God always provides an escape according to 1 Corinthians 10:13.
teachings.text:
Free will isn't the argument against Calvinism. Responsibility is.

No one has unlimited, absolutely free, will. Everyone is influenced and penned in by their past choices, other people's choices, trauma and bad habits and all the dark ripples of sin that all combine to make limited the number of choices we have. 

But God always provides an escape. 

**1 Corinthians 10:13** 
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

When we are tested, we have a choice to do the right thing, based on God's standards. And it's harder to do the right thing, because of sin. 

But we are responsible. And able to respond. So we have no excuse, except to deal with what's in front of you, in the Spirit. Even when it is hard.

It is by God's grace that He offered us His word, His commandments, His wisdom and prudence. We don't deserve a way out of the repercussions of sin. He not only forgives us, but provides us an escape. Both spiritually, in Christ but in this life, by His word. That's amazing grace.

teachings.title: Augustine, separated Christians and persecution
teachings.summary: Traces how separated, standards-keeping Christians were persecuted from the Cathars onward, blames Augustine's legacy for weakening responsibility, and quotes 2 Timothy 3:12 and Luke 6:22-23.
teachings.text:
Augustine’s legacy perverted the gospel and weakened responsibility which excused the excess and rationalized the evil done to separated Christians with standards; the faithful who keep trying to live Biblical lives and are persecuted for it. The pattern hasn’t changed.

The Bible says, *Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.* Jesus warns again and again that Christians will be hated for His name. That we will suffer persecution. Paul, Peter, John and Jude all write about scoffers, mockers, persecution for the faith, and the patience of the saints who endure it. 

We count ourselves blessed that in America, today, we aren't facing any real persecution. That we are free to worship, pray, read and own the Bible, go soul-winning...all without facing the same challenges our spiritual forefathers faced. Partly because our system of government was influenced by those fleeing persecution and sectarian violence. This gave us some protection against politically connected apostates coming against us for Godly living. 

But, another reason why Bible believing Christians today, including you and I, aren't facing the same level of persecution those 1st century NT Churches faced, or the various Christians throughout the last 2,000 years have faced, is because of our own lack of separation. Because we compromise. Because we shirk standards and give in to the flesh, and aren't as perfect, or mature, as we could be. Worldly. Carnal. 

Maybe we would have the crowns of glory given martyrs if we chose to live more like Christ and followed His example, the way these earlier Christians did.

**Luke 6:22-23**
*Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake. Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.*

teachings.title: The ten commandments are not impossible
teachings.summary: Says the ten commandments are generally easy to keep, with the Sabbath fulfilled as rest in Christ.
teachings.text:
Generally speaking, and understanding that we all fall short of the glory of God, and stipulated that the Sabbath is Christ Jesus, where saved believers rest forever, but the 10 Commandments are pretty easy to keep (mostly!) 

Having no other God, not making or bowing to idols, not taking His name in vain. Resting in Christ. Honoring your parents, even as adults. 

Not killing. Not commiting adultery (in practice if not in the heart). Not stealing. Not bearing false witness. Not coveting your neighbors things, or his wife, or anything he has. 

These bare minimum things are really not that difficult. Bare minimum stuff.

teachings.title: Original sin and babies
teachings.summary: Says original sin is not biblical and that the idea that babies are born guilty was created to keep people in the Roman Catholic church.
teachings.text:
Remember, original sin is not biblical. And the idea that babies are born guilty, and if they die they go to hell, was created to keep people going to the Roman Catholic apostate Church. 

Protestants continued to varying degrees supporting this. Even going so far to say that babies that die who aren't elect go to hell.

teachings.title: Peter's denial and ours
teachings.summary: Uses Luke 22:62, Galatians 2:11-14 and 2 Peter 2 to show that even mature believers can deny Christ under social pressure, yet Peter went on to preach boldly.
teachings.text:
**Luke 22:62**
*And Peter went out, and wept bitterly. *

There are times in every Christian's life where the story of Peter's betrayal of Christ hits hard. New Christians, who have just accepted the gospel and been saved, turn to their unsaved family and friends, and at the slightest pushback and mocking, get embarrassed and deny Jesus.

Older, more mature Christians even, will keep their faith hidden in social settings or in the workplace. 

We may miss opportunities to go soul winning with our brothers and sisters, in part because of the fear of judgment. That you will be accused by scoffers as Peter was, and so preemptively decline to go. 

We all have a regret of not sharing the gospel in a time and place where we are given the opportunity by God to proclaim the faith that saved us. 

We may weep bitterly by the hospital bed of someone close to us, incapable of knowing the truth because we never shared it. 

The Apostle Peter's story in the gospels is very real and relatable. But it doesn't end at the crowing of the cock that morning. 

The risen Christ appears to Peter again during the 40 days between Easter and the Ascension. Peter, unsure of his calling and, I think, ashamed of his betrayal before the Son of God, decided to go fishing.

**John 21:1-4**
*After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself. There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.*

And as Jesus prepares them food, and eats with them, He gives Peter, who denied Him 3 times, the opportunity to affirm his love of Jesus 3 times. 

**John 21:14-17**
*This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. *

Peter always loved Jesus, and trusted Him, but his shame for the denial of his Lord in His hour of death made him feel distant and alone. Jesus gave him the opportunity to work through that shame and realize his love for Christ is greater than his shame at letting Jesus down. 

And Jesus says at each affirmation, *feed My sheep*. Serve others. Win souls.  Care for the flock.

The answer to the shame we feel when we deny Christ or the opportunity to share Him with others, isn't to go fishing. To return to the world. But to return to the work of the ministry of reconciliation we all have. 

Soul-winning when you are down bad, and ashamed, when prayer feels a little empty, when Bible reading is falling off, when you know you gotta get right, even if you aren't backslidding, per se, is the way to show yourself the love of Jesus you have. It is restorative sharing with others the love He has for you, and them.

Peter's story doesn't end there, either. In Acts we see him boldly proclaiming Christ, calling Jews to repentance and faith towards God. Enduring beatings and imprisonment to preach the gospel. Of going to the Gentiles with the truth when called by God. 

And even then, Peter isn't perfect. Even as an elder of the faith, he still occasionally felt the pressure to conform to the world. Here, he is called out by Paul.

**Galatians 2:11-14**
*But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?*

It is something we can all fall into, even as older more mature Christians. 

That's why, when Peter writes his epistles, his encouraging message to believers to holdfast their faith, even when facing scoffers, mockers, false teachers, etc...to be like Christ when we are reviled for His sake - is so powerful. Like most good preaching, he is talking about his own struggles, to edify others. 

**1 Peter 2:21-23**
 *For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously*

Being ready to testify of the hope we have even as men falsely accused us, mocking and scoffing our faith, to have the mind of Christ:

**1 Peter 3:13-16** 
*And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

Even as Noah suffered the scoffers and blasphemers of the pre-flood world, as he prepared the ark, those spirits in Hell that Jesus went and preached to, showing those that trust the Lord shall not be ashamed;

Those *spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. *

Peter says the flood that destroyed those wicked people is a like figure to the baptism of the believer, showing the same faith and confidence Noah had to build the ark, saving his family.

*The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.*..

Our obedience in baptism, to publicly proclaim our faith, similarly shuts the mouths of those scoffers, that our conscience is clean in Christ. 

 **2 Peter 2:1-3**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.*

Verse 7-8, *how God delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Speaking of a believer who didn't share his faith, just Lot still was delivered from their filthy conversation, just as God promises to deliver us from the same mockers and unrighteous people.

*cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet.*

**2 Peter 3:3**
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.*..


And so let's learn from Peter's slip ups and mistakes, and take heart in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

**2 Peter 3:18-19**
*Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.*

I think many of us like to think of ourselves as Paul, but if we are honest, we are a lot more like Peter.

teachings.title: Reformed theology and unconditional election
teachings.summary: Argues that Calvinist election rests on a quality in the elect, contrary to the gospel of grace, and warns that Reformed teaching is creeping into Baptist churches.
teachings.text:
Notice that the underlying false gospel of the Reformed theology Calvinist, assumes they are selected based on God's will, because of a personal quality they possess. This is antithetical to the gospel of grace, which is the love of God for all men, manifest in the life, death and resurrection of His Son, Christ Jesus. 

It places a condition on their so-called "unconditional election." They say things like this in pride, trying to sound humble. 

They make themselves their own christs. Jesus isn't even necessary in the equation, because God would have chosen them anyway.

Reformed theology is the most dangerous apostasy creeping in to Baptist and evangelical churches today. It has been there, but is suddenly increasing in scope, with reports of solid IFB churches being subverted by online ministries and pastors creeping in, denying their doctrine is Reformed, while they sow seeds of it from the pulpit. 

Beware these wolves. They appeal to believer's pride to act as the soil their corrupt seed is planted in. The thorns and thistles these tares produce become the next generation in the church.

teachings.title: Equal unto the angels
teachings.summary: Explains Luke 20:36 in its context of the Sadducees and the resurrection, noting that Jesus is describing what believers will be: undying children of God.
teachings.text:
**Luke 20:36**
*Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.*

We know the context, that Jesus is talking to the Sadducees, and answering their foolish hypothetical about a woman married to 7 brothers under the law of Moses. They tried to paint a contradiction into the idea of the resurrection of believers, and Jesus responded by saying this. That we aren't taken in marriage in the glorified eternal life awaiting us. 

I want to point out that one, the resurrection on the day of redemption was understood as a concept, and something many Jews believed on, and trusted. Salvation was always by faith in the free gift of eternal life. Calling upon the name of the Lord to save you. 

But, more importantly, go back up and read the verse again. Jesus is describing us. What we will be like. Undying children of God. 

Amen.

teachings.title: Win souls until the day of Christ
teachings.summary: Quotes 2 Thessalonians 2 to show the falling away and the man of sin come first, so believers should win souls until then.
teachings.text:
*Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him, That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God. Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?

And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time. For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way. And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming*

The imminent return of Christ is true...after all these things come to pass. Until they do, win souls!

teachings.title: Predestination and free will
teachings.summary: Says people mix up free will and predestination from false definitions, and that the destination of adoption was predetermined for all who enter in through Christ.
teachings.text:
But that's not what predestination is. 

The destination of adoption was predetermined for all who enter in through Christ, not predetermining which people would step through the doorway.

People get really caught up in free will vs predestination, because they begin with fundamentally false premises, and wrong definitions of terms.

teachings.title: No Mid-Acts dispensation
teachings.summary: Uses Acts 15:8-11 to show Peter and Paul preached the same gospel, and that all men from Adam through today have been saved by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
**Acts 15:8-11**
*And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the *Lord* Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

"Mid-Acts" Dispensationalism holds that by chapter 15, a different gospel is made known unto Gentiles, that the Jews keeping the law of Moses still, despite believing, were under a dispensation of the law still. That the Gospel of Grace was given to Paul to preach to the Gentiles. That these verses "prove it."

A plain reading of the text shows that Peter held the same Gospel of Grace, and that it is not given by works of the law, but by the grace of the LORD (made distinct in the text, using the same capitalized distinction reserved for YHWH. A divine Lord, absolute authority, Greek is *Kyrios*).

*We believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they*. This sentence refutes any of the idea that Jews had a different gospel or standard, or that Peter's preaching to the circumcision was any different than Paul's ministry to the Gentiles. 

There is no "Mid-Acts Dispensation." All men, from Adam through today have been saved by the grace of God the Father, through faith in His deliverance, which is by His Son, Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Read scripture first for how it applies to Jesus
teachings.summary: Teaches that scripture should first be read as God telling us about God and the mind of Christ, not as a text written about the reader.
teachings.text:
Speaking of natural men, and not understanding the spiritual things of God that are spiritually discerned, it is incredibly important when reading scripture to look first at how it applies to Jesus. 

A lot of people read scripture, to read themselves into the text. To make it about them. 

"God's talking to me so why isn't it about me??"

God is telling us about God. To show us the mind of Christ that we may know it. And through it the Spirit which searches all things, even the deep things of God, reveals that mind of Christ. 

**John 16:13**
*Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.*

The only thing self-centered about our walk with God when we read scripture, is understanding His ways and His wisdom and then we can apply the implications to ourselves. But the primary text is about the Lord. 

Almost every heresy imaginable that is drawn from the Bible, comes from people making the focus themselves. 

As John the Baptist said, I must decrease that He may increase. You're going to learn so much more of the wisdom of God keeping that fear, that reverence, first and foremost in your mind.

teachings.title: Christmas decorations, Jeremiah 10 and Romans 14
teachings.summary: Says Jeremiah 10 does not condemn decorating a house with plants, and applies Romans 14 so that believers do not despise or judge one another over keeping the season.
teachings.text:
Annual reminder that **Jeremiah 10** does not condemn decorating your house with plants, and that God decorated His house, the Temple, with firs and box and pines. 

**Jeremiah 10**
*Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel:

2 Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.

3 For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe.

4 They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not.

5 They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.

6 Forasmuch as there is none like unto thee, O Lord; thou art great, and thy name is great in might.

7 Who would not fear thee, O King of nations? for to thee doth it appertain: forasmuch as among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like unto thee.

8 But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities.

9 Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning men.

10 But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation.

11 Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens.

12 He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.

13 When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.

14 Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

15 They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish*.

**Isaiah 60:13**
*The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.
*
The Bible doesn't teach against the use of plants as decoration. It shows us God uses evergreen trees to beautify His temple. 

A tree isn't a graven and decked image of a god. No one bows and serves a decorative house plant, they beautify their homes with them. No one worships a pine tree except pagan "druid" LARPers. 

Even the most secular reprobate consumerist, who strips Christ from Christmas and makes it entirely about snowmen and reindeer and coveting things, doesn't look at the plastic tree covered in lights and tinsel in the corner of their living room and thinks, "I shall worship this." They don't even "venerate" it. 

But that hasn't stopped some from judging believers in respect to holy days, and teaching doctrine of men for commandments. 

There are plenty of reasons to not want to participate in traditional Christmas trappings, especially as they have become in the modern, consumerist world of greed. The lie of Santa, the works-based system that you have to be good, "repent of your sins or you don't get a present!" The profane and the blasphemous way our Jewish-subverted culture has secularized it all. 

But most believing Christians see the season as simply a feast celebrating the miracle of the birth of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Most take the season to reflect on scripture, the great mystery that God was made flesh, to give thanksgiving to God the Father for His Son, to sing Psalms and hymns praising Him. And decorating their homes, eating special meals with family. And giving gifts to one another in the spirit of grace, just as God has given to each of us.

If you don't want to worship Jesus this way, and if you are convinced of yourself that it is a sin, then you should not do it. 

And regardless of your conviction, **Romans 14** should apply;

*1 Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.

2 For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs.

3 Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.

4 Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

6 He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it. He that eateth, eateth to the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth God thanks.

7 For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.

8 For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's.

9 For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.

10 But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

11 For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

12 So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

13 Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way.

14 I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.*

No one should judge someone who doesn't want to celebrate even the most faithful of Christmas celebrations, and no one should judge those who do. They certainly shouldn't abuse **Jeremiah 10** to justify their doctrines of men to level railing accusations against people who just think it's a nice thing to do, while keeping Christ as the center of their lives.

teachings.title: Romans on the Jew and the elect
teachings.summary: Quotes Romans 2, 5, 9, 10 and 11 and shows that Paul argues salvation is by faith, so Jews after the flesh are not the elect and dispensational promises to physical Israel do not follow.
teachings.text:
*Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God...Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid...

What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin; As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all

Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.*

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.

There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit....So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

 I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen. Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth. And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha. What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone;*

*As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me. But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.*

*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.(According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.

And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway. I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy. 

Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness? For I speak to you Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office: If by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them. For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.

For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

It's impossible to get any notion of dispensationalism or a promise to physical Israel being saved from this text. 

Paul creates an airtight argument that salvation is by faith, that the adoption and promises by faith are for the elect, and that Jews after the flesh are not the elect and have not obtained it.

teachings.title: Baptism for the dead in 1 Corinthians 15
teachings.summary: Explains that 1 Corinthians 15:29 is part of Paul's argument for the resurrection, not a recommendation of the Mormon practice of baptism for the dead.
teachings.text:
1 Corinthians 15:12-32 
***Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead**, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? **But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.** *

***Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.** **For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins. Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished**.

**If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable. But now is Christ risen from the dead,** and become the firstfruits of them that slept. **For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead**. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him. And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all. **Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?** And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily. If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, **what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.***

There is a wicked heresy among Mormons, especially, that there is a practice called "the baptism for the dead."

They take the verse *Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?* and create an entire ceremony where they go to graveyards, find names of people that weren't Mormon, and do an elaborate ritual where a member gets baptized in a pool in their Masonic temples, in the name of the dead person. They teach this will guarantee that spirit will enter the afterlife, and gives them points towards becoming gods. 

This is obviously wicked.

But many Christian denominations, even good Baptist pastors and preachers, misunderstand this verse, and while they will teach against the Mormon practice, they say it actually was some sort of pagan practice in Corinth that the church was caught up in. 

That's wrong. 

In this chapter, Paul is addressing the real problem among Corinthians, that they had some denying the resurrection. Not only the resurrection of believers, but of Christ Jesus. 

Paul then begins a series of rhetorical and logical arguments that lays out the hypothetical implications of the idea that Jesus didn't rise from the dead. 

If there be no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen. If Christ is not risen, then the preaching of the gospel is in vain. Their faith is in vain. Paul and other ministers of the Gospel are liars. We would still be in our sins of Christ didn't rise from the dead. Those who are dead in Christ, fallen asleep, are actually perished. 

We would be most miserable. 

Paul then explains the truth, that by Adam death came into the world, but in the resurrection, Christ conquered death. 

He then says *Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all?* If Jesus didn't rise up, He is dead. Why are we baptized in His name, an ordinance that pictures the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, in the name of a dead man?

Why would Paul stand in jeopardy every hour? Why risk his life to deliver the gospel? What advantage do we have as Christians if we do not have the resurrection? Eat drink and be merry, for tomorrow we die!

We see that, in context, it is an extension of the same argument. It isn't a recommendation for a practice invented in the fever dreams of Salt Lake City. It isn't a practice of the NT churches. It is not a pagan practice. 

It is simply the argument against those who doubt Jesus Christ rose from the dead, and the implications of that damned heresy.

While it's easy to laugh at the Mormons and profane idea of baptizing for the dead, which obviously has no efficacy or biblical support, it's important to note how evil this is. 

They will literally go and find relatives names or even total strangers and take it upon themselves to baptize in their name and claim that those people are now Mormons. It's as ghoulish as the Catholics trying to claim Charlie Kirk. 

It's a wicked process and evil minds come up with things like this. 

The LDS Church teaches that performing baptisms for the dead allows this "saving ordinance" to be offered on behalf of those who have died without accepting or knowing Jesus Christ or his teachings during their mortal lives.

Of course water baptism does not save anyone. But this is where that heresy leads. Believers baptism is the only biblical form of baptism that is taught. And it's an outward sign to others of what's in someone's heart.

teachings.title: Belief as a state of being
teachings.summary: Argues that believe is a stative verb, so one cannot stop believing the truth without repenting of it, and quotes 2 Peter 3 on the unlearned wresting scripture.
teachings.text:
"Believe" is often misunderstood as an action, but it's generally a state of being. Like other "be" verbs (is, am, are), it reflects an internal condition—holding something as true in your mind. 

For example, "I believe in kindness" describes a mental stance, not an act you perform. While it can seem active in some contexts, at its core, believing is a state of conviction. A state of being. 

"Believe" and "be" verbs (like is, am, are, was, were) are typically classified as stative verbs when describing a state of being. Stative verbs express a condition, state, or situation that exists, rather than an action.

They express things like mental states, emotions, senses, possession, or existence, and typically don’t involve physical activity or change. Unlike action (or dynamic) verbs, which show something happening (e.g., "run," "write"), stative verbs indicate a steady, ongoing state. 
 
Stative verbs are rarely used in continuous (progressive) tenses like "am believing" because states are seen as enduring, not temporary actions. Saying "I am knowing" sounds unnatural and stupid compared to "I know." 
 
Understanding stative verbs helps in using correct grammar, especially avoiding progressive forms with verbs that don’t typically take them. It also clarifies why "believe"is generally a state of being—an internal condition—rather than an action.

Repentance, understood as a change of mind, is the pivotal means of transforming belief because it involves a deliberate shift in one’s perspective or conviction. Belief, as a stative verb, represents an enduring mental state, a settled acceptance of something as true. Without repentance—actively rethinking or rejecting a prior belief—this state persists, as beliefs tend to remain fixed unless consciously challenged. By engaging in repentance, one reorients their mind, replacing old convictions with new ones, thus enabling a fundamental change in belief.

This is why when someone says "I stopped believing Jesus was real and that God gave His Son," or "I stopped believing the gospel was by faith alone and joined the Catholic Church," what they are saying is the repented of the truth, the big capital-T Truth, to believe a lie. 

The Bible says this is not possible. We have the Spirit of truth, cannot be deceived (it's not possible), and cannot reject it. But even if it were possible, it is IMPOSSIBLE for someone to be brought again to repentance. That's what **Hebrews 6** says and I believe it.

I figure if a mountain of scripture isn't sufficient for some people, a brief English lesson might be. 

...*even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are **unlearned and unstable wrest**, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.*

teachings.title: The disciples' doubts were not apostasy
teachings.summary: Shows from John 6, Luke 24 and John 20:9 that the disciples believed yet did not grasp the resurrection, and that doubt differs from repenting of saving faith.
teachings.text:
The Gospels repeatedly show the disciples failing to grasp the necessity of Jesus' death and resurrection, even though they believed in Him for eternal salvation.

**John 6:68-69**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God. 
*
Their faith in Jesus as the Messiah and Savior was genuine, but their understanding of the Scriptures regarding His suffering, death, and resurrection was incomplete until after the resurrection, when He "opened up the scriptures to them" as described in **Luke 24:45-46**.

Jesus first explicitly foretold His death and resurrection after Peter's confession of faith (**Matthew 16:16; Mark 8:29; Luke 9:20**). The disciples' reaction shows they did not comprehend or accept it;

**Matthew 16:21-23**
*From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee. But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

*Jesus explained to them, but they did not understand it. Peter's confession that Jesus was the Christ, shown to him by the Father according to Christ, the rock on which Jesus builds His church, was sufficient to save the apostle. Yet moments later Jesus calls him "Satan" rebuking Peter's offense at the idea of Jesus suffering death. 

**Mark 8:31-33**
*And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.*

Was Peter in unbelief? No. He just didn't understand the concept of what would soon follow. He was saved by faith in the things he knew, under the Old Testament. Without the indwelling and seal of the Spirit, they did not fully comprehend the gospel of the New Testament. 

**Luke 9:44-45**
*Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.*

As they approached Jerusalem, Jesus detailed His fate again, but the disciples could not fully understand.

**Luke 18:31-34**
*Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again. And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.

***John 12:16**
*These things understood not his disciples at the first: **but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him**, and that they had done these things unto him.

*It is a key point, raised again and again that they simply did not have it given them to understand.

**John 20:9**
*For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.*

And so, after the resurrection, you have scenes like the two pilgrims on the road to Emmaus (**Luke 24:13-32**). They didn't believe He had risen from the dead. They didn't know this was Jesus who spoke to them. Jesus says "*Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?"* and explains to them they should believe the prophets and expounded the Scriptures unto them, showing how His suffering and resurrection were foretold from Moses onward (**Genesis 3:15; Deuteronomy 18:15; Isaiah 53; Psalm 22:16-18; 16:10**).

They were believers, under the OT, who trusted that Jesus was the Christ but didn't understand the totality of what that meant, until it was given to them to understand. 

The same with the apostles who didn't believe Mary Magdalene's report. Not that they stopped believing Jesus was Christ, or stopped believing the word of God they knew and understood unto salvation. 

They just didn't believe a woman's story. Same as Thomas didn't believe them. He still knew Jesus was the Messiah, but he didn't trust their accounts that He had risen from the dead, because none of them really could understand that aspect without Jesus' instruction and the Spirit that then came and sealed them. 

These passages demonstrate that the disciples' faith for salvation was present early, but full insight into the Scriptures' prophecies about the Messiah's suffering and resurrection required Jesus' post-resurrection teaching.

People, who err not knowing scripture, will often take a verse out of context, or use a word that doesn't mean what they think it does in the situation, and apply it in isolation as a proof text for heresy and nonsense. 

We should search the scriptures to see if something is so. Rightly dividing the word of God. And ask more mature Christians if what you think something means, does, or has a larger context you might be missing.

And it shouldn't have to be said that the doubting Thomases among the disciples of Christ during that 3 days and 3 nights, never repented of their faith to believe on something else. 

They never became apostates. They didn't say, "Well Jesus is dead, I'm going to become a Pharisee." Or "God doesn't even be real!" 

Christians all have moments of doubt and lack of faith, but what they will never do is repent of that saving faith to believe a lie instead.

teachings.title: The very elect can be deceived
teachings.summary: Points out that Matthew 24:24 says the very elect, meaning every saved Christian, can be deceived, so believers need church and the word to stand.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 24:24**
*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive **the very elect**.*

You notice it doesn't say only certain Christians. People who aren't backslidding. Doesn't say people who go to church three times a week and read their Bible everyday. It says the elect. So that's every saved Christian. 

What stops a backslidding worldly, living in sin, unchurched, flesh-feeding, Grace frustrating, Spirit quenching saved Christian from believing the hype and thinking an antichrist is the Christ? 

What could possibly protect that member of the very elect? 

Because the very elect includes those people too. 

What power stops them from believing a lie?

teachings.title: Be in a local church
teachings.summary: Says a believer must be in, or actively seeking, a local called-out assembly, and answers common excuses for staying out of church.
teachings.text:
If you are not IN a local called out assembly of believers, or ACTIVELY SEEKING to join one, you aren't right with God. 

If you are helping to enable others to forsake the assembly, excusing them, encouraging them, claiming that there are "no good ones," giving them any reason to justify their being out of Church....You are not only not right with God, you are wicked.

"I can't find one!" Ask, we will find you one. 

"I don't have a ride or way to get there!" I promise you, there is a church with the means to pick you up and get you there in your area. 

"It's too far!" People drive over an hour to go to a Bible believing church. 

"It probably is a 501c FEMA church!" You care more about feeding your fear than feeding your spirit. 

"I have social anxiety! I have Neurodivergence! I am good getting everything I need from the Internet!" You are a disaffected weirdo who needs to get in a local church and stop being a special boy.

"I work Sunday!" Sunday night? Wednesday? You work 24/7? 

"The pastor teaches a secondary or tertiary doctrine I don't agree with! He isn't PERFECT!" You are in no position to talk about perfect when you are forsaking the assembly. 

Find the best one with the right Gospel and the right Bible closest to you and get plugged in and working for God. Stop making excuses and stop following chat room mods who don't go to church, have hardly been saved for a year or two, and teach stupid and heretical garbage. 

Go let a church be a blessing to you, and you be a blessing to it.

teachings.title: Believing is not a work, and the apostate
teachings.summary: Gathers Romans 4:5, Hebrews 3, Philippians 1:6, 1 John 5:4, Romans 10:13, John 15:6 and 2 Peter 2 to show salvation is not lost and that apostates were never saved.
teachings.text:
**Romans 4:5 **
*But to him that **worketh not**,** but believeth** on him that justifieth the ungodly, **his faith** is counted for righteousness.*

**Hebrews 3:12-14**
*Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end*

**Galatians 5:4**
*Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.*

It goes on and on and on and on...

**Philippians 1:3-6**
*I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

**1 John 5:4**
*For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.*

If you believe that an apostate is able to come again unto repentance then your argument is with God.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved*.

**John 15:6**
*If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.*

You cannot lose your salvation once you've been born again. When you have trusted on Christ Jesus, believing the truth that you have eternal life as a free gift of the Father, you are quicked. Sealed by the Spirit. Held by the power of God. 

So what does this verse mean?

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. **But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.***

Wonder what this could possibly mean? **🤔**

teachings.title: Assurance and the perseverance promise
teachings.summary: Says believers can be assured they will never perish, and that enduring to the end in the Gospels is a promise for those living through the tribulation, not about spiritual salvation.
teachings.text:
"Believers in Christ can be personally assured that they WILL NEVER PERISH FOREVER because their salvation rests solely upon the faithfulness and finished work of the Savior on their behalf." 

So true. **Believers** in Christ have that blessed assurance. People who believe in vain and depart from the faith never believed in the first place, and don't have that assurance.

"Perseverance of the saints" has nothing to do with spiritual salvation or anything else regarding the gospel. It's a promise made by Jesus to people who are alive during tribulation that if they endure to the end of that tribulation, they will be saved out of it by the coming of the Lord. 

Heretics and fools twist the meaning to apply it to the gospel. They hate the word of God and have to take things wildly out of context to try and make their foolish and unbiblical arguments.

teachings.title: Saved by His death, burial and resurrection
teachings.summary: Quotes John 3:16-18 and says one who does not trust the death, burial and resurrection of Christ is not saved, since the gift is the point of His sacrifice.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him **should not perish**, **but have everlasting life.** For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned**: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

If you don't believe that your sins are all forgiven, that you have eternal life, that Jesus died for your sins, past, present and future, so that you may have eternal life, you aren't saved. 

OSAS is just shorthand for the gift promised by the grace of God, paid for by the Son and sealed by the Spirit. Never perishing, everlasting life, not condemned. This is an essential part of what you're believing on Jesus *for.*

If you don't know for sure you have eternal life, you don't know the gospel and you aren't saved. 

**1 Corinthians 15:1-2**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and **wherein ye stand**; **By which also ye are saved,** if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, **unless ye have believed in vain.***

If you don't believe that you stand and are saved by the death, burial and resurrection of Christ Jesus, as foretold in scripture and witnessed by many, you aren't saved. 

The gift is the point of Jesus' sacrifice. It's what you receive when you trust in Him. 

If you don't know what He did it for, you don't know why you need it, or what the purpose of it even was.

teachings.title: Confessing faults and repenting as a believer
teachings.summary: Teaches that saved believers should admit their sin to God and stop it, and confess faults to one another according to James 5:16.
teachings.text:
There is a repentance of sin that all saved believers should strive to do, admitting your faults and iniquities to God, and then turning from those things. To be honest with yourself and God. 

He doesn't want you to be sorry, or need you to be sorrowful, the Lord just wants you to admit it's wrong and stop it. 

So do most normal, healthy people. Parents understand. People who have had relationships with family or friends with drug addiction or other similar behaviors, they understand. No one wants to hear excuses. No one wants a slobbering apology. Just admit you were wrong, to God at least, and stop doing whatever it was. Especially be willing to make amends with the brethren;

**James 5:16**
*Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.*

You want your fervent prayer to avail much? Confess your faults and pray for each other. And forgive your brother when he does, as you would be forgiven.

teachings.title: The parable of the sower
teachings.summary: Notes that in Matthew 13 the wayside hearers are unsaved while the other three receive the word, though only the last bring forth fruit.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 13:18-23 **
*Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower. When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side. 

But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is **he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it**; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended. 

He also that **received seed** among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and **he becometh unfruitful**. 

But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; **which also beareth fruit, **and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.*

Note that in the parable of the sower, the first group are unsaved, those of the wayside. 

The other 3 are saved, receiving the word, but for the reasons given, the 2nd and 3rd aren't fruitful or become unfruitful. Yet they still are saved. The 4th are successful Christians, fruitful in bringing forth more believers, winning souls. 

There is no example of someone who receives the seed, then becomes the hardpan ground of the wayside, no longer believing, and then sprouting and growing roots yet again

teachings.title: Paul kept the faith
teachings.summary: Reads 2 Timothy 4 to show that Paul's 'kept the faith' refers to his ministry and reward, not holding on to personal belief to stay saved.
teachings.text:
2 Timothy 4:1-13
 *I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom; Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine. For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables. But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry. For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.*

Paul, in an emotionally charged farewell to Timothy, and really to the reader, says he is ready to die. He has run the race set before him, as He says in **Hebrews 12:1-3**
*Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
*
In the King James, a keeper is a person or entity that holds, guards, maintains, or has custody of something or someone. This can refer to someone like a prison keeper, the keeper of a park or flock, or someone responsible for a sacred place. The concept extends to holding a position of oversight, like a keeper of the great seal, or having a moral responsibility for another's welfare, as seen in the question "Am I my brother's keeper?"

Paul is talking about his life of ministry, as a keeper of the faith, as the evangelist to the Gentiles. Paul kept the faith and would expect a crown of righteousness for his reward, for those works. 

This has nothing to do with holding on to personal beliefs. 

Context matters.

teachings.title: Against continual believism
teachings.summary: Answers the teaching that belief must be maintained until death, using John 3, Galatians 4, 1 Corinthians 15 and Hebrews 6 to show that vain faith means never having believed.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth** in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth** on him is not condemned: but **he that believeth not** is condemned already, **because he hath not believed** in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

Calvinism falsely teaches that election is unconditional, that grace is irresistible and that belief is conferred on people by force of God's sovereign will. That they are chosen to have faith thrust upon them. (Some Calvinists will say at that point, there's a choice, but generally, they reject free will).

Saved Christians understand that there is one condition for salvation, and that condition is to believe on Christ. To believe in the name of the only begotten Son. He that believes that the Father so loved the world He gave His Son, Who while we were yet sinners, died for us, and rose again that we may have eternal life in His name. 

This is Biblical repentance. **Acts 19:3-5** defines it for us. 

*And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with **the baptism of repentance**, saying unto the people, **that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.** When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.*

Repentance towards the truth, the Gospel of God, is to believe on Christ Jesus. And believe means to trust. 

Ephesians 1:12-14
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, **who first trusted in Christ**. In whom **ye also trusted**, **after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation:** in whom also **after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise**, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Repent>believe>trust is all one thing, the Bible says. This is the condition by which one is saved. 

"But what if I stop believing?" What if you stopped trusting that the Gospel is true? What if you repent again to something else? How? There is no biblical mechanism given where this happens, where a saved believer stops believing.

There are examples given for those who backslide, who lose the joy of their salvation, who walk in the flesh, who are carnal Christians, who don't feed the Spirit, and become castaways to the calling of God. Chastened, prodigal, all of these things are given us as examples for what may happen in the Christian life of saved believers. 

But there is only one doctrine given for those that claimed to have believed and then repented to believe, to trust on something else. That they never fully believed. That they believed in vain. That it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance. 

Paul, upon hearing the church at Galatia had those among its members who were being beguiled into adopting the law to be saved, who had repented of the faith he taught them to believe something else - he wrote to them and harshly questioned if they actually were saved. 

**Galatians 3:1-7**
*O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, **that ye should not obey the truth,** before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? **This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?** Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things **in vain?** if it be yet in vain. He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.*

Note that Paul doesn't say "Well you did believe, so you're still saved," and then try and get them to change their mind again. He accuses them of not believing at all. 

**Galatians 4:4-11, 14-20**
*But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods. But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.*..*Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
*
According to this new group of people claiming "Heresy!" Paul was a heretic to be marked and avoided. 

Also John then, according to these foolish men, would be a heretic, for teaching that if one goes out from the doctrine of the truth, it was to make manifest that they never believed.

**1 Corinthians 15:12-14**
*Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.*

Faith in vain is defined for us again here, where those that had heard the truth preached, that included the resurrection of the dead, now were saying the resurrection of Christ wasn't true. Paul says that this means their faith was in vain. Empty. Having no effect. Vanity is defined again and again in scripture to mean one thing, a belief or action that has no power towards salvation in God.
