Vain works, vain idols, vain beliefs. *All is vanity, sayeth the preacher*, but one truth: *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man*, and so we are called to *Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth*. To believe. To trust. To keep in remembrance. To turn away from vanity.

Finally, this strange doctrine being promoted by very foolish men says that it is not only **possible** that *those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance*, but that God actually will force repentance and impose faith again upon the apostate, before they die, so that they are kept saved by God's sovereign will. 

A form of Ultra-Calvinism. 

They claim, contrary to God's word, that those that *crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame*, those who go out from us and are manifest that they were not of us, will, by the sovereignty of God, be brought to faith, "believing again" just in time to not perish. 

Despite the fact that the Bible says this is impossible. Despite the fact that they claim to reject Calvinism. 

They so badly want to have the ability to reject God, kill the new man, break the seal of the Spirit, and still be "saved," they've invented a foolish and damnable heresy that tells people who reject the truth to not worry about it. They "believed" once, and that's good enough and if they trust in something else later, oh well. 

Paul wrote entire Epistles in the Spirit to warn against believing in vain. Telling people to keep in memory the truth of the Gospel he preached. 

Because once you believe the truth, once you repent, once you trusted on Christ Jesus alone to be saved, you have the Spirit of truth, and not the spirit of error, and cannot be deceived.

**1 John 4:2-6**
*Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

There is a heresy that is called "Continual Believeism" that teaches, among other damnable heresies (repent-of-your-sin, baptism for babies, etc) that "belief" is a work, an action. That "belief" isn't simply knowing something is true but requires ongoing, active faith maintained until death. A "perseverance of the saints," that makes a state of mind into a process. Just as they make repentance into a process. 

The new, foolish application of this heresy makes the same mistake those who actually endorse "Continual Believeism." They too make what is a change of mind and a knowledge that something is true into a process and a work. 

They make the same damned error. 

The ""Continual Believeism" heretics say that believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe or through unrepentant sin. 

The people taking that heresy and twisting it to mean that "believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe," but they will be forced to believe again, because they "had been saved."

It's two heads of the same damned coin and a misunderstanding of what believing is, simply repenting to the knowledge something is true, accepting something true as true, trusting on it being true. 

They turn it into an action, a work, and wrest with scripture to deal with it, rather than accepting that all those who have believed for salvation just know that what they trusted in is true, even if they doubt themselves, because it is the promise of God.

Call me Colombo, because one more thing; these fools are also applying the same logic Dispensationalists hold regarding the Jews. 

That a promise of God is a promise, and so that even though the Jews are unrepentant antichrists who rejected Jesus, they will somehow still be saved in the end because they had a covenant. That in the end, God will give them faith and they will believe, and so "all Israel shall be saved!" 

The covenant with physical Israel was conditional. They no longer have the promises because they broke the condition. They held the truth in unrighteousness, and did not wish to retain God in their knowledge. 

Salvation is conditional on belief, on knowing in our hearts that Jesus is the Christ. *If thou believest with all thine heart*...If you don't know that something is true with all your heart, you don't believe it. If you know something is true with all your heart, how could you ever reject it? 

It doesn't mean you have to continually work to believe. It doesn't mean you have to constantly remind yourself that it's true that the only way a man may be saved is by faith alone in the finished work of Christ. 

It just is.

If you come up with a doctrine that contradicts clear scripture, it falls on you to explain it and make it consistent. 

If you cannot explain Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2, to make it fit your opinion, then your opinion is wrong.

teachings.title: Believed in vain
teachings.summary: Shows from 1 Corinthians 15:1-2 that believing in vain means not keeping in memory what was preached, and affirms that everything that happens at salvation is eternal.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 15:1-2**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.*

This defines what believing in vain means. That if you don't keep in memory what was preached to you, you believed in vain. It means you weren't saved. 

Not that you have to be constantly rebelieving the gospel to be saved, but if you're saved you remember the truth that saved you. It's kept in your memory, because it's true. Simple as. 

If you've been saved a while, and lived a life and been backslidden and not walking in the Spirit, for any length of time, you understand. 

You might doubt yourself but you will never doubt the truth, once you know it. How could you? It's the truest thing in existence!

I believe in OSAS. Once sealed always sealed. 

I believe in OQAQ. Once quickened always quickened. 

I believe in OJAJ. Once justified, always justified. 

I believe in ORAR. Once repented, always repented. 

I believe in OAAA. Once adopted, always adopted. 

I believe that all of the things that happen when you're saved are eternal. That once you know the truth, you always know the truth. And the Bible says if you don't know that truth, and trust something else to be saved, you never trusted in the truth in the first place. 

Let God be true....

teachings.title: Assembling together and not falling away
teachings.summary: Reminds believers that Hebrews 10:24-25 commands gathering in a local church, and that Hebrews 6 does not teach that one who truly knew the truth comes to believe it false.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 10:24-25**
*And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

Reminder that going to a called-out assembly of believers is a command, and being under a qualified pastor, in service to a soul winning, local New Testament church keeps you from drifting into weird doctrines and heresies. 

You do not have an "online ministry," and you are not satisfying this commandment by being in a chat room. If you are not in a local church, be actively seeking one. They don't have to be "perfect." They do have to accept the gospel of salvation by faith alone, the free gift given by the Father, eternal life paid for by the blood of Jesus Christ. Sealed unto redemption by the Spirit. Never to be lost. And be KJVO.

**Hebrews 6:4-9** 
***For it is impossible** for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come. If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: **But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned. **

But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

Reminder that, if you've actually believed on the truth of the gospel of God, then you know it's true. You might doubt your own faith, you might question your trust in Christ, and even wonder if you are saved, but you will never question the truth of how one *is* saved. 

And if someone does, if they had claimed to be a Christian, and then rejected the truth of God's salvation to trust their works, or to join a false religion or to become an atheist or something, they NEVER believed. They believed in vain, the Bible says. They were not of us. And according to **Hebrews 6**, such apostates are impossible to then bring again to repentance. They are done. They did not wish to retain God in their knowledge, and they held the truth in unrighteousness.

Once you know that something true is true, you won't ever come to believe it was false. 

That's madness.

teachings.title: The mark of the beast and adding to scripture
teachings.summary: Says taking the mark of the beast requires worshipping the beast and his image, and that Revelation 22:18-19 warns those who add to or take from scripture.
teachings.text:
Taking the Mark of The Beast requires one to worship the beast and his image.  

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect...And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads...And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone....And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.*

No one who is saved will worship the beast to take his mark. No person who takes the mark will repent and be saved, they are blotted out of the book of life, the Bible says. Reprobates. Rejected of God. 

Beware false prophets who seek to tell you that there is no such thing as being given up for holding the truth in unrighteousness. Who say you can be forgiven for blasphemy of the holy Spirit, when Jesus says there is no forgiveness for it. That there aren't reprobates, when the Jews who hardened their hearts were damned, unable to hear the truth and be healed.

Finally, **Revelation 22:18-19** is clear; anyone who adds to scripture or takes away from scripture is blotted out of the book of life, and accursed. 

*For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.*

Jesus Christ Himself testifies that this is true. His last command in the final chapter of the final book of the Bible. 

No one is ever written into the book of life once they've been removed.

teachings.title: Blasphemy against the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: Quotes Matthew 12:31-32 and Mark 3:28-29 and notes that no one may claim blaspheming the Holy Spirit is forgivable.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 12:31-32**
*Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men. And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.*

**Mark 3:28-29**
*Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation*.

Let God be true, and every man a liar. Beware false prophets who contradict the clear and undeniable word of God.

While I have seen people debate what it means to blaspheme the Holy Spirit, I have never seen anyone, even the most dishonest and despicable false teacher, ever directly contradict Jesus and claim that it's actually totally forgivable to blaspheme the Holy Spirit. 

Mark and avoid. That person is 100% not saved and can't discern the spiritual things of God.

teachings.title: Hope for the dead and the true gospel
teachings.summary: Says many have a false hope that anyone who acknowledged God was saved, and that the answer is soul winning and preaching the whole word to the living.
teachings.text:
Between the Pope, John MacArthur and Ozzy dying, it's really exposed how vacant and lost most people's understanding of salvation is.

People believe all manner of nonsense and vain beliefs, the primary one being that if someone vaguely acknowledged God in some way, or mentioned Jesus, that they were likely saved. 

Of course the same people promoting this desperate false hope will turn to the living and say "You can't just say a prayer and be saved!" Mock "easy believism," and "once saved, always saved." 

"You can't be saved and live however you want!" 

"We are saved by faith....BUT...."

They will promote false teachers and men who profess another gospel, or worse, unregenerate celebrities who outright tell you they believe some unbiblical nonsense about "a higher power," and get angry when we point to scripture and the specific plan of salvation given to show that we can pretty much guarantee these people died in their sins and went to Hell. 

"Only God can judge! You don't know what's in their hearts!" 

God told us His judgement, and out of the abundance of their hearts, they spoke. We don't condemn them, their own words do. 

**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

"Maybe God will be merciful to them!" He was when He sent His only begotten Son to die for us. 

"Maybe they repented on their death bed!" Maybe, but if they didn't hear Moses and the prophets and the gospels and the preachers their whole life, they probably won't. 

This is why we go soul-winning. This is why we preach the whole word, in season and out. 

Hopes and prayers that someone gets right at the last moment, or wishing someone be saved after they die, are all vanity. 

There is the gospel, preached by the saved to the lost, and the Spirit moving with their spirit, that they repent towards the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: When Paul was saved
teachings.summary: Says Paul was not saved on the road to Damascus but in Damascus when he called on the Lord after Ananias taught him the gospel, and that no one is saved without hearing the word preached.
teachings.text:
Below is an audio sermon on Paul's conversion. I've heard many dispensationalists claim that the 144,000 of the book of Revelation are actually modern Jews, who unbeknownst to them carry the exact genetics of the 12 tribes mentioned, and they are given salvation in some sort of Calvinist way "Similar to Paul on the road to Damascus." 

Paul did not get saved when he was blinded and heard the voice of Christ. Paul was saved in Damascus 3 days later when he called upon the name of the Lord after being instructed in the gospel by Ananias. 

Every saved person has another saved person who acted as their minister of the Gospel of reconciliation to bring them to Christ. Nobody is given salvation without hearing the word preached and believing what they heard.

teachings.title: Are saved versus are being saved
teachings.summary: Argues that the KJV's 'are saved' in 1 Corinthians 1:18 preserves an assured, completed state, unlike 'are being saved' in modern versions.
teachings.text:
In 1 Corinthians 1:18, the Greek present passive participle σῳζομένοις conveys salvation as a divinely assured state, rendered in the KJV as "are saved" to reflect a completed act with lasting certainty. 

This choice aligns with the Biblical emphasis on God's definitive work, presenting salvation as a settled reality for believers. We ARE saved. Now and future, because of the work of Christ.

However, modern translations like the NASB, NKJV, and LSB often use "are being saved," introducing the English present progressive tense through the auxiliary "are." This shift in tense makes it an ongoing, potentially incomplete process, which introduces ambiguity for readers, making them see salvation as something that is not guaranteed, that it isn't a past and lasting state.

For comparison, consider the translations
**1 Corinthians 1:18**
KJV: "*For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God*."

NASB: "For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God."

NKJV: "For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God."

LSB: "For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God."

Modern translations are  grammatically defensible, by dishonestly claiming their choice isn't denying the present perfect passive voice, they are lying. They will truncate it to "being saved" to make that claim, completely ducking the point that it is the use of "are being" that creates the change and renders their corrupt text as heresy. 

The KJV’s "are saved" perfectly preserves the assured, completed state implied by the Greek, whereas "are being saved" in modern versions turns that blessed assurance into a continuous, unfinished process, sowing doubt and promoting the idea that you can't know you're saved, or that salvation can be lost. 

Stick with the King James!

teachings.title: The laborers in the vineyard and lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Answers lordship and repent-of-your-sin teachers with Matthew 20, saying the saved are chastened by God but receive grace as the late laborers did.
teachings.text:
Lordshippers and repent-of-your-sinners are hypocritical vipers. 

They just want to judge other people. They want to rate their own righteousness by finding others who aren't living up to whatever arbitrary standards they have set. 

And it's always vague because they need to have wiggle room for their own sin. " You got to give your life to Christ!" What does that mean? Well it depends on when you ask them. 

"You have to repent of your sin and change your life!" What does that mean? Depends on when you ask them. 

It has to be vague and loaded with ambiguity and subjective judgment because they always have to have a way to justify their own sin. They always need to have someone else they can look down on. 

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees. HYPOCRITES!

People who think this way also neglect to understand that we who are saved are chastened by God, who scourges every son he receives. 

"You can't just live however you want!" is code for "It isn't fair that you get paid a penny for showing up at the end, when I worked all day!" 

**Matthew 20:1-15**
*For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

2 And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

3 And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

4 And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

5 Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.

6 And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?

7 They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.

8 So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

9 And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

10 But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.

11 And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,

12 Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

13 But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

14 Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.

15 Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?*

teachings.title: The one test of a false teacher
teachings.summary: Says the one criterion the Bible gives for a false believer or teacher is whether they add works to the gospel, not behavior after being saved.
teachings.text:
The one criteria the Bible gives for identifying a false believer or false teacher is do they add works to the gospel. 

Not behavior after being saved. Not by how good they are. Not if they turn over a new leaf. Not if they clean up their life. Not by how righteous they act, what church they go to, or any other thing, but what they trusted in.

teachings.title: Only the blood atones
teachings.summary: Says turning over a new leaf, baptism, joining a church or good deeds cannot satisfy the price of sin, and that only Christ's blood offered on the mercy seat propitiates, with Hebrews 9 quoted.
teachings.text:
Turning your life around, repenting of sin, joining a church, getting water baptized, making Jesus the Lord of your life, seeing real change, sacraments and good deeds... None of these things satisfy the price of sin. 

Only the blood of a holy God offered in our place and sprinkled on the mercy seat can atone for our sin and justify us before God. That is the only propitiation. The blood is for the heavenly Father.

**Hebrews 9:11-26** 
*But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, **but by his own blood** he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.

It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others; For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.*

**Romans 3:25**
*Whom God hath set forth to be a **propitiation** **through faith in his blood**, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God*

teachings.title: The gospel is not a call to discipleship
teachings.summary: Says the gospel Jesus proclaimed is repentance unto belief and calling on the Lord for eternal life by His blood, not a requirement of submissive obedience.
teachings.text:
This is not the gospel that Jesus proclaimed. It is a decision, repentance unto belief. A prayer, calling upon the name of the Lord. It was not a "call to discipleship" or a requirement for "submissive obedience." 

It is eternal life and forgiveness of sins by the blood of Christ Jesus, because we aren't capable of submissive obedience or sufficient discipleship to ever pay any of the wages of sin. Our filthy rags aren't what the Lord wants. Faith is. 

John MacArthur's heresy is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: Go soul winning
teachings.summary: Asks how a believer who knows Jesus' love can keep from telling others, and urges being part of an organized soul winning program in a local Baptist church.
teachings.text:
How many of you have enjoyed a meal or a movie or a rollercoaster ride, and felt a fire to tell other people about it? Where you can't wait to post a picture or leave a review? You want to tell the whole world about it?

If you know the love Jesus has for you, if you have felt that love, how can you not scream it from the rooftops? How can you not go out into the highways and hedges to let everyone know that Jesus loves them?

Go soul-winning!

If you aren't part of an organized soul winning program as part of a local fundamentalist Baptist Church, you aren't right. 

You read your Bible and go to church, and that's great, but you aren't complete. You aren't perfect. And you're missing out.

teachings.title: Revival starts at the door
teachings.summary: Says revival starts with a saved Christian knocking on a door with the King James Bible and the love of God.
teachings.text:
Young people, old people, men and women and boys and girls, listen to me now!

Revival doesn't start by some magical change of heart among the heathen!

Revival starts with a knock on the door by a saved Christian with the King James Bible in their hand and the love of God in their heart, magnifying it so that you get to tell them that Jesus loves them!

teachings.title: Ruckmanism and the KJV
teachings.summary: Rejects Peter Ruckman's teachings, such as serpent seed, UFOs and Jews saved by works, while holding the KJV as God's preserved word without correcting it from the Greek.
teachings.text:
Ruckman taught another gospel. It is wicked and accursed and all his other teachings that flowed from it were wicked and blasphemous and did not come from the KJV Bible. UFOs and new Adams on alien planets and the kingdom given to unbelieving Jews who were saved by works....all of it is evil. The divorces and the fruit of his ministry, wicked preachers who teach "Serpent Seed" and other wicked doctrine only adds to it. 

I don't care if you think he was right about the KJV (it's a perverted twisting of sound doctrine IMO), it cannot overcome his insane teachings. 

Imagine being correct that the KJV is the only Bible today we need and then being so spiritually blind that you pull damnable heresy from your own vain imagination instead of the rock of the word you supposedly champion. 

Good natured disagreement on the topic between brothers is fine, and there are many great pastors today who hold similar views on the providential nature of the beautiful Authorized Version. And while some could nitpick their opinions, God bless them for their standards and doctrines. Their fruit is a consistent gospel and soul-winning flocks, amen.

Lots of good pastors out there are wrong on one secondary doctrine or opinion. Hard not to be when Bible colleges and seminaries are out there, teaching for commandments the doctrines of men (especially around the Jews and the end times). 

But praise God those things shake out in the wash. Meanwhile, we all share an every word Bible, the blood of Jesus Christ and a great commission. Amen.

And I thank God Pastor Hyles stopped a bad habit he apparently had, of using the Greek to "correct" the King James. 

His moderate position bridges the gap between two extremes and his defense of the Bible his momma gave him is the sweetest KJVO testimony you'd ever need.

I can understand why someone who holds a similar (though not necessarily identical, or even more extreme) view on the inspiration behind the KJV would not like to be labeled a "Ruckmanite" as an argument-ending ad hominem. It means guilt by association with things that no sane believer would want to be linked with, and isn't fair. 

Serpent Seed and UFOs aren't being argued. In good faith, that label shouldn't be used unless they explicitly claim the whole mantel of Ruckman, or doctrines outside the stated topic of the wonderful Authorized Version.

teachings.title: The law as schoolmaster
teachings.summary: Asks how there can be revival without the law, since the law is the schoolmaster that brings the lost to repentance toward the gospel.
teachings.text:
How can there be revival without the law, when the law is the schoolmaster that brings the lost to repentance towards the gospel? 

The haters of the law and hard preaching against sin essentially want to take away the schoolmaster. How can someone know they are wrong if they don't know what's right?

teachings.title: Demon possession and Catholic exorcisms
teachings.summary: Gives the Baptist view that demon possession affects the unsaved, doubts Catholic exorcisms, and cautions against dismissing all possession as mental illness.
teachings.text:
I think that 99.9% of Catholic "exorcisms" are fraudulent. Like entirely performative and made up. The same way so many of their "apparitions" and "mold on the window looks like Mary!" Or "this inanimate object bleeding! (It's an old magic trick)" are.

In Baptist circles, generally shared doctrine on demonic possession is that it only affects unsaved people (the Spirit within the saved prevents this) and that it often is the result of sin/occult practices inviting them in. This leads to those cases brought forward to either be prayed over, fasting, etc, or outright saying it isn't their problem. But deliverance ministries are pretty often called in and successful (there are many fraudulent, false gospel people calling themselves Deliverance Ministries, but legitimate practitioners exist, and many pastors either know a guy or know of a guy). 

It usually is a quiet affair, and not turned into a show of Latin and special FX nonsense. And the goal is to get the person cleaned AND saved. 

The problem with any false gospel form of exorcism is obviously this:

**Matthew 12:43-45**
*When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none. Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished. Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation*.

And finally, because saved Christians tend not to be anywhere near as superstitious as Catholics, there's a modern tendency to dismiss what is demonic possession as just mental illness or addiction or whatever. And so they don't even address it. 

Meanwhile, Catholics will turn to a supernatural explanation, even when it is just like drug induced psychosis. Basically two ends of a spectrum if you see what I mean.

teachings.title: Grace sufficient and disagreeing peaceably
teachings.summary: Recounts a sermon on Philippians 4:19 and Lazarus and the rich man, then shows from 2 Corinthians 12 that God's grace is sufficient and urges peaceable disagreement between brethren.
teachings.text:
A brother recently guest preaching for an ailing pastor, preached a great sermon on the promise of God from **Philippians 4:19**;

*But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.*

And while making great points on walking in the Spirit, expecting chastisement rather than blessings if you're backsliding, he made an odd choice to use the story of Lazarus and the rich man from **Luke 16** to say that Lazarus was clearly backslidden and being punished by God for his sin, but despite that he was still saved. 

His premise was that, because **Philippians 4:19** is true, that the only explanation for him being a believer, yet a filthy beggar of crumbs, covered with sores, liked by dogs, having misery in this life, was he was backslidden and unresponsive to God's chastening. 

Immediately, my mind went just a few chapters to the left, to **Luke 13:1-5**;
*There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things? I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem? I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.*

Or why Job's friends were wrong to assume he deserved what was happening to him, or **Matthew 5:45**;

*That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

Or **Ecclesiastes 9:11**
*I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all*.

I also thought of this story from **John 9:1-7**; *And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth. And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind? Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world. When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.*

My brother's assumption that Lazarus' life contradicted the promise of God to fulfill all his needs, and so had to be rationalized into making sense, failed to take into account the glory of God being demonstrated. That when Abraham says to the rich man in Hell, *Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented*, that the story has served as a comfort to the broken hearted and a warning to the proud, that has been used uncountable times to show the glory of God and His promises. 

What my friend saw as eternal shame for Lazarus in Heaven, every time the story is preached, I see as a wonderful blessing for a faithful man who lived under terrible conditions for a brief moment, but who is in eternity with Christ, knowing that what he suffered on earth wasn't in vain. 

And finally, that while our expectations for God's promised providence should be trusted, in the end our suffering may not be of our own cause, but for His glory. His grace should be sufficient.

**2 Corinthians 12:7-9**
*And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.*

So, while he was correct in preaching against spiritual complacency in expectation of the promise of blessings, I vehemently disagreed with his proof text and assumptions. 

My pride wanted to immediately confront him on it. That he was drawing inferences that weren't present in the text and that he was missing the bigger picture, and that there is no inherent contradiction between the promise to provide and Lazarus' life. That His grace is all the provision we need, anything else is a blessing. And while, when we are afflicted, we should examine ourselves before complaining to God, we shouldn't assume every bad thing that happens to another is for their own sin...I wanted badly to confront him with this truth. 

But, praise God, I stopped to consider the matter first. To reflect before speaking. To make sure I was acting out of love for a brother, not my own pride. 

At the end of the day, it's a minor disagreement over an opinion. And despite being convinced I have all the facts and all the arguments and all the proof texts and everything else, I determined it is better to allow him his opinion, and talk softly about what mine is, and why, than charge at him in rebuke.

Don't let how Internet fights are conducted influence you, especially in real life. Understand that there's room for disagreement. That other people don't have to have total conformity to your opinion to be brothers. That *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

teachings.title: Do not wait for persecution to go soul winning
teachings.summary: Pairs Acts 1:8 and Acts 8:1-4 with Matthew 24 to warn that complacent Christians may be scattered by persecution, and urges going soul winning now.
teachings.text:
**Acts 1:8**
*But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.*

**Acts 8:1-4**
*And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him. As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison. Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word.*

Jesus told them to go out to the world and spread the Gospel to every creature, to the uttermost parts of the Earth. And instead they stayed in Jerusalem. 

So the Lord brought tribulation and persecution to them in Judea, scattering the saints abroad, so that they would preach everywhere. 

Are you waiting for the tribulation to go out into all the world and preach? 

**Matthew 24:9-14**
***Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake.** And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. **And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.***

When Christians are complacent and don't go out into the highways and hedges, compelling others to come in, spreading the gospel, God will bring persecution and tribulation to get us off our pews. 

Don't wait to be persecuted for His name's sake before you get up and go soul-winning.

teachings.title: The KJV, the received text and other languages
teachings.summary: Explains that the KJV was translated from the received texts, that translating other languages from the TR may be more accurate than from the KJV English, and that God's word was preserved before 1611.
teachings.text:
While the KJV is the inerrant and preserved word of God in English, it was translated from what was called the received texts, thousands of manuscripts that had been compiled by Erasmus, Beza, and Stephanus prior to 1611, as well as manuscripts that we no longer have access to, and earlier translations like the Bishop's Bible, which used these and other Antioch preserved scripts. 

Scrivener’s Greek New Testament (1881), usually refered to as the Textus Receptus, or received text, was a compendium of the previous Greek TRs, synthesized, using the KJV authorized version to bring all the Greek into alignment. 

If we were to attempt a translation into another language, such as Spanish, there are some who believe this must be done from the KJV English, as an intermediary. And while it could be possible, it wouldn't be as accurate to read in that language as a translation from the TR. Idioms, phrasing, and word choice would create problems. For example....

Example 1: **John 1:1**
   
KJV English: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."   
 
Translated from KJV to Spanish: "En el principio era la Palabra, y la Palabra estaba con Dios, y la Palabra era Dios."   
 
Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "En el principio era el Logos, y el Logos estaba con el Dios, y el Logos era Dios."   
 
Problem: Translating from the KJV to Spanish loses the nuance of the Greek term "Logos" (λόγος), which carries more philosophical and theological depth than "Palabra," missing this richness. Additionally, the TR Greek specifies "el Dios" (the God) with the definite article, emphasizing distinction, which the KJV-to-Spanish translation might obscure by following the English structure too closely. Direct translation from the TR preserves these subtleties, avoiding the loss of meaning inherent in translating a translation from Anglo-Germanic to a romantic language like Spanish, which has so many similarities to Greek. 

Example 2: **Philippians 2:6**
   
KJV English: "Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:"   
 
Translated from KJV to Spanish: "El cual, estando en forma de Dios, no consideró como robo el ser igual a Dios:"   
 
Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "El cual, existiendo en forma de Dios, no consideró el ser igual a Dios algo a que aferrarse:"   
 
Problem: The KJV phrase "thought it not robbery" translates the Greek "ἁρπαγμόν" (harpagmon), which implies something grasped or seized. Translating from the KJV to Spanish retains "robo" (robbery), which can suggest a negative act, potentially misrepresenting the intent. 

The direct TR-to-Spanish translation captures the nuanced meaning of "harpagmon" as something not clung to and exploited, rather than a sense of theft. Translating from the KJV introduces ambiguity by relying on an English idiom, which we understand, but may be lost on the Spanish reader. So rather than the original Greek’s theological precision, it introduces confusion in the finished Spanish product. 

Example 3: **Matthew 5:18**
   
KJV English: "For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled."   
 
Translated from KJV to Spanish: "Porque de cierto os digo que hasta que pasen el cielo y la tierra, ni una jota ni una tilde pasará de la ley, hasta que todo se cumpla."   
 
Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "Porque en verdad os digo que hasta que pasen el cielo y la tierra, ni una iota ni un ápice pasará de la ley, hasta que todo se realice."   
 
Problem: The KJV uses "jot or tittle," translating the Greek "ἰῶτα" (iota) and "κεραία" (keraia), referring to the smallest Hebrew letter and a serif-like mark, respectively. The KJV-to-Spanish version keeps "jota" and "tilde," which are familiar but may not convey the precise Hebrew scribal context. The direct TR-to-Spanish translation uses "iota" and "ápice," preserving the original terms’ specificity and cultural nuance. Translating from the KJV risks losing the exactness of the Greek terms by adhering to English equivalents that are less precise in a word-for-word English to Spanish translation. This example is less problematic than the others, because you'd still need to understand the Hebrew style being referenced, but it would be in a word choice that the Spanish reader could better understand. 

These are but a few examples. And if we got to the Masoretic Text, to English-to Spanish, instead of a direct translation, we would see even more problems, because Hebrew is far from a romantic language, let alone English, and a lot of the beauty and wordplay would be entirely lost.

God's preserved word has been available, in its most complete and necessary form, from all time. We are blessed to have a finished and easily accessible Bible, in English. But it would deny preservation to say that the word of God was not preserved until 1611, as millions were saved from every nation and tongue long before it, by faith. Which comes from hearing the word of God. 

On Pentecost, the Apostles and disciples speaking in tongues, preached the word of God in more than a dozen languages. 

When the NT saints heard the gospel, it was in Greek and Hebrew, and likely Aramaic and other languages. 

The power is in the word itself, and the Spirit moving in those receiving it. Not in the languages. 

We can recognize the providential nature and power of God used to create our KJV, without denying the preservation and power that His word has always and will always have.

teachings.title: The Didache and baptism
teachings.summary: Observes that the Didache teaches baptism for believers with no mention of original sin or infant baptism.
teachings.text:
The Didache (late 1st/early 2nd c.), a short book often cited by Papists, teaches baptism for believers, and talks instruction in the gospel before the rite. 

No mention of "original sin," or infant baptism suggests its author saw baptism as for those who can profess faith, implying the early church understood infants were sinless and wetting babies, pointless.

teachings.title: Original sin, infant baptism and grace
teachings.summary: Argues that teaching original sin leads to baptizing babies as a work for grace, and that anything added to grace makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
The false teachings of "Original sin" are the root of most damnable heresy. The false teachings of it immediately stir the maternal to ask "What about my baby??!!" From there it becomes about works and cult-control

As soon as you are water baptizing babies because moms are freaked out about being told that if their kids die, they might go to Hell (Or maybe limbo,) you've put faith in a rite and a priest and a church. Not Jesus. And not a just God.

And the churches that teach this damnable heresy have convinced you to do a work for grace that's not in the Bible. 

From that point on, their people have accepted a lie, and so they will be invested in maintaining the lie, even when there is no scripture teaching it, at all. Even when they are shown why the handful of out of context scripture that they are told actually teaches baptism of babies is wrong. Spiritual blindness because of fear and pride.

Doing something to "receive grace" makes grace no more grace. 

Grace is the unearned and unmerited favor of God. Work, laboring, receives a wage, not grace. Anything that adds anything to create merit or to be deserving in any way, means you are going to receive your just wages. 

Death and Hell.

teachings.title: The gospel on Resurrection Sunday
teachings.summary: Notes how many churchgoers have never heard the gospel and urges giving the gospel on Easter, with the hope of the resurrection to eternal life in Christ.
teachings.text:
One of the saddest things when you go out soul-winning, giving the gospel, are the number of people who attend a supposedly Christian church, and have never heard the gospel preached and couldn't tell you if they are going to Heaven because no one's ever asked them that before.

Living in a predominantly Catholic area, where 90% of doors knocked where the person claims to attend church name their local parish, we meet people both young and old who have never heard the Bible verses we use. A surprising number don't even recognize John 3:16. And they are always caught off guard when asked if they know for sure they are going to Heaven. They've never even considered the question. They've never been given the opportunity before to think about it. 

Easter Saturday, a beautiful spring day, and the celebration of the resurrection being at least in the back of people's minds, and yet so many were lost. 

We had an older man, Catholic, tell us in a matter of 5 minutes that he didn't know for sure he is going to Heaven, that he was sure he was because he's a "good person," that Hell isn't real, that the earth is Hell, and finally "You put too much faith into that book!" 

At least he was willing to listen before rejecting it. Most Catholics when asked if they have a minute to hear what the Bible says, say "no not really interested. I'm busy." And close the door. 

Many will hear "The Bible says you can know for sure you're going to Heaven" and say "No thanks, I am Catholic." 

Many of them will make their biannual pilgrimage to attend mass, today. And hear at least some Bible read about the resurrection. But, lacking anyone who is saved reading it, and not having hearts to receive it, it falls on the stoney pathways and won't take root.

Being so close to the truth, and rejecting it. 

But even so, give the gospel today. Remind the unsaved people in your life what you are actually gathered together to remember. The hope that is Christ Jesus and the resurrection unto eternal life promised by God in Him.

teachings.title: Flee fornication, marry, and church discipline
teachings.summary: Teaches from 1 Corinthians 5, 6 and 7 that those living together unmarried should stop and marry, and that a brother in unrepentant fornication is to be disciplined out of the church.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 6:18-20**
*Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body. What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.*

If you are currently living with or fornicating with your boyfriend or girlfriend, you should stop and get married. 

**1 Corinthians 7:2**
*But to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.*

**1 Corinthians 5:9-11 **
*I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators: Yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or with idolaters; for then must ye needs go out of the world. But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolator, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.
*
You should be disciplined out of the church if you are living in sin or engaging in fornication, and won't abstain and get married.

teachings.title: Calvinism and election
teachings.summary: Says Calvinism makes election rest on foreknowledge or God's sovereign will rather than grace, reads Romans 9 as about nations, and cites Ephesians 1:4-5 for predestination in Christ.
teachings.text:
Even so, Calvinism falls into the same heresy, making the election not of grace, but of foreknowledge and predestination, God choosing who is saved based on His "sovereign will." That they are elect because of something God saw in them. Some merit.

They also use **Romans 9**, which was written about nations of people, the very scripture dispensationalism uses to justify its own heresy towards Jews, except changing the election from a physical nation to another innate quality; their usefulness to God. 

**Romans 9:10-13**
*And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated*.

Again, Paul is writing about nations, not individuals, and drawing the comparison between the children of promise through Isaac, and the inheritance of that promise through Jacob rather than Esau. 

Paul goes from **Genesis**, the first book of the Old Testament, through **Malachi**, the last to make his point, and that point is not that God pre-ordains who will be saved and who is condemned.

Rather God pre-ordains that His promise will be kept, and those that partake in the conditions for that promise, are heirs to it. In this case, the election of grace through faith in His word. 

**Romans 9:22-24 **
*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

God predestined that those who believe on His promise will be given the gifts of that promise, being longsuffering towards the unregenerate Jews, that His mercy may be shown to all who believe, in Christ. 

For all men are called; The Bible says:

**John 12:32**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.*

And again:

**2 Timothy 1:9**
*Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.*

And:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
*
All are drawn, all are called. God's will is that no man perish. It is to His purpose that we avail ourselves of the grace given the whole world, whom He loves. *That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. *

But by making the election not of grace, but sovereign will, and not to all men, but the select few, they make the promise of God to no effect. That whosoever believes isn't whosoever, but the preselected few, drawn by irresistible grace and unconditional election. 

"Unconditional election," is an oxymoron, used as a fig leaf to say "actually, we aren't special boys. We are randomly chosen, basically." An election without conditions is not an election, not a chosing, but is a random decision. It is a false humility used to hide their pride. 

They don't believe in grace, but in their own worthiness. Even if they say they don't know why they are special, only that they are. 

**Ephesians 1:4-5**
*According as he hath chosen us **in him** before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us to be adopted his sons by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.*

All who trust Christ are predestined in Him. That election of grace given the whole world, is predestined in Jesus according to the will of the Father. It is Christ Who was chosen before the foundation of the world. Not the special boys who believe themselves to be their own little christs, making grace no more grace.

teachings.title: The election of grace
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 11:5-6 and Galatians 3 that election is of grace, and that salvation for the Jews as Abraham's seed makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
Every damnable heresy in "professing Christianity" is based on rejecting the election of grace. They make grace contingent on merit, making grace no more grace. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

Grace is the undeserved and unmerited favor of God. 

Here in Romans, Paul is writing to explain why physical Israel, Jews after the flesh, are not elect. That their blood relation to Abraham cannot save them. That it is by the election of grace man is saved. Continuing in verse 7;

*What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.*

Which election? The election of Grace. And so, the heresy of dispensationalism fails when the scriptures are searched to see if it is so. And the damnable heresy of hyperdispensationalism is undone by the doctrine of grace. 

**Galatians 3:16**, **26-29**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.* *For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The Jews being saved for being the seed of Abraham makes grace no more grace.

**Romans 9:6-8**
*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

teachings.title: Holding the standard in church and life
teachings.summary: Pairs Romans 7:12 and 1 Timothy 1:8-11 with the point that a person cannot expect society to keep godly standards if the church and the believer do not.
teachings.text:
**Romans 7:12**
*Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.*

**1 Timothy 1:8-11**
*But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

How can we make society conform to Godly principles and standards if you aren't even holding them in your church or your life.

teachings.title: Following God's commandments and the law used lawfully
teachings.summary: Calls believers to keep God's commandments, tithe, attend church and win souls, and says the law is good when used lawfully.
teachings.text:
Follow the commandments of God that it be well with you. Follow the Law to show that you love Jesus. Hold others to standards that it should lead them to understand they are sinners in need of redemption. Advocate for the law because it is good, when used lawfully, to punish evildoers. 

Romans 7:12
*Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.*

Tithe. Go to church. Stay sober and vigilant. Win souls. Edify the brethren. Don't lie. Don't steal. Don't lust in your heart or fornicate with your members. Don't cheat each other. Look after one another and place the brethren's profit above yours. 

This shouldn't be controversial.

teachings.title: Every believer a priest, not a priest class
teachings.summary: Sets 1 Peter 2:9 and Hebrews 4:14-16 against sacerdotalism, showing Christ is our only High Priest and every saved believer is part of the priesthood.
teachings.text:
Catholicism is a godless, hopeless false gospel

**1 Peter 2:9-10**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.*

**Hebrews 4:14-16**
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

**1 Timothy 2:5**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus*

**1 John 5:11-15**
*And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

Sacerdotalism is the heretical teaching that a priest class are essential mediators between God and humanity. That none come to the Father themselves, through Christ, Who is our High Priest, Who is our only mediator, but that we need men to act as intermediaries. 

Catholicism again spoils God to give to men the divine roles and responsibilities. 

As for priests, every saved believer is of the priesthood of Christ. Giving the gospel that others become part of that holy priesthood of believers. A peculiar people. Separated unto the gospel of God.

teachings.title: Entering the rest in Hebrews
teachings.summary: Shows from Hebrews 4 that only those who believed the promise entered Christ's rest, and that sin does not lose salvation while those who reject the truth for their own works were never saved.
teachings.text:
*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you **should seem to come short of it.** For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached **did not profit them, not being mixed with faith** in them that heard it. For we which **have believed** do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world. For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest. Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and **they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:** Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. **For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day**. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. **For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his**. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest**, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.***
...
***Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.** But exhort one another daily, while it called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. **For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;** While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, **harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.** For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? **And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.***

**Hebrews** teaches clearly that only those who have believed the promise, and entered into the rest of Christ Jesus, are saved. 

It does not say if we sin, we lose salvation. It doesn't say if we forget our rest, we aren't saved. Paul writes that those without faith unto salvation, who heard the word and yet turned to their own works, and hardened their hearts, never entered into that rest. 

It isn't our faith and confidence in ourselves that saves. We aren't condemned, even if we forget who we are, made new in Christ.

But if one were to fall away from the truth, and reject the offer of rest to do their own works after knowing better, they were never saved and they will be condemned. Apostates, as **Hebrews 6** goes on to describe.

teachings.title: Calvinism makes grace no more grace
teachings.summary: Argues that election by a chosen purpose introduces merit, so the TULIP doctrines undo grace and are self-refuting.
teachings.text:
Rebuking a Calvinist, and it occurred to me that they make grace no more grace. If grace is entirely unmerited, but God "chooses" someone for His own purpose, that introduces merit. That person then has a predetermined purpose, and value, or God wouldn't have chosen them. Thus they are needed and inherently that's merit.

Even if you introduce the concept of limited free will, the Calvinist who doesn't hold to irresistible grace, and says "if not me, then He could use someone else," they are simply making a pool of merit, shared across a group. 

To make irresistible grace work in a limited atonement system, you'd have to then deny their other doctrine of God's sovereignty, and say it's random. Which of course isn't what election is. No one is elected by random. There are candidates, considered for their qualities, and chosen. A sovereign god, who micromanaged creation, couldn't leave it up to chance anyway. 

Calvinism, especially the TULIP doctrines, are self-refuting.

teachings.title: Struggling faith versus rejecting the truth
teachings.summary: Distinguishes a believer whose faith falters from one who rejects the truth and was never saved, pointing to Hebrews 6, Romans 1 and 2 Peter 2.
teachings.text:
If a person’s faith falters, fails, or is unfruitful will that person be lost? No. Of course not. 

If a person becomes a full on atheist, believing in their heart there is no God, or becomes a Catholic, believing in their heart they must do works to be saved, or a Buddhist or something else, believing in their heart that Jesus isn't the Christ, and salvation isn't of God, THEY WERE NEVER SAVED. 

And not only were they never saved, they are now most likely a **Hebrews 6** apostate. A **Romans 1** reprobate. A **2 Peter 2** case:

**2 Peter 2:21-22**
*For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

Dogs. Swine. Reprobates. Falling away and believing in vain. 

The difference between struggling with faith and having doubt after being saved vs rejection of the truth they understood but never trusted in, to believe a lie.

Don't be confused.

teachings.title: Same gospel for Jews and Gentiles, and idols
teachings.summary: Shows from Acts 15:11 that the apostles believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles, and from Acts 19 that early Christians opposed idols in worship.
teachings.text:
*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

**But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.***

The heresy that Paul taught a different gospel to Gentiles than the Apostles taught the Jews relies on a false interpretation of **Acts 15**. But it is made clear here in **Acts 15:11** that the Apostles in Jerusalem believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles. By the Lord Jesus Christ.

**Acts 19:24-28** 
*For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen; Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth. Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth. And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.*

Catholics, particularly Orthodox, all insist that graven images and "icons" were always part of worship for Christians, from the days of the Apostles. Obviously false, as Idolatry was consistently prohibited by God's commandments, and by the Apostles and Epistles, saying to flee idols and not to eat meats offered to them. 

But to really reinforce this idea, we have the story in **Acts 19** of the silversmith, Demetrius and the cause he's tired up against the disciples of Christ in Ephesus. Because the Christian teaching was against images in worship, Demetrius was able to argue their craft was in jeopardy. That they'd go bankrupt if people no longer required idols made of hands. 

If early Christianity only taught against images of false gods, and not the entire practice itself, their trade would not be unprofitable. Instead of Diana they could make a living with crucifixes and statues of the passed saints. 

It's just another example of how foolish these appeals to vain tradition are in light of the Bible.

teachings.title: Falling away and those never saved
teachings.summary: Explains from Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2:19 that one who truly trusted Christ does not fall away from the faith, while backsliding and doubt differ from rejecting the truth. Adds that doctrine comes from clear scripture, not parables.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:4-6 **
***For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened,** and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, **to renew them again unto repentance**; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.
*
No one, once saved, who has trusted on Jesus, and the promise of God, baptized of the Spirit and sealed unto redemption, having the spirit of adoption, knowing with all your heart that Jesus is the Christ, Whom the Father promised, will ever doubt that truth. 

We may backslide, doubt our own salvation and commitment to Christ, even deny Him to others. Doubt God's grace for us. Even forget the joy of our salvation. Have fear, little faith, get caught up in false doctrines, etc...

But you will never fall away from believing that Jesus is Lord and God is real, and that salvation is by grace through faith, to believe in your heart that something else is true. 

If someone chooses atheism after having full knowledge of salvation, they were never saved. They believed in vain. They had head knowledge, but didn't trust in their heart. And if they do reject the truth, it is IMPOSSIBLE for them to come again to repentance.

**Proverbs 26:7**
*The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.*

Take your doctrine from clear scripture, not trying to wrest one from parables.

teachings.title: Neither... nor in Daniel 11:37
teachings.summary: Walks through the grammar of 'neither... nor' to show that Daniel 11:37 says the antichrist will regard neither the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god.
teachings.text:
***Neither shall he regard** the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women...*

For the non-English speaker, understanding basic grammar can be a stumbling block for understanding God's word.

"Neither... nor" is a negative correlative conjunction that connects two or more parts of a sentence to indicate that both options are not true.

"Neither... nor" must be used in parallel structures, meaning both sides must be balanced. For example, if "neither" is followed by a verb, "nor" must also be followed by a verb, or call back to the original verb, and apply it equally to the object of the sentence. For example;

"Neither shall he regard":

"Shall" is the main verb, with "he" as the subject. "Neither" is a coordinating conjunction modifying the verb "shall regard."

"The God of his fathers" is the direct object of "regard."
("The" modifies "God." "Of his fathers" is a prepositional phrase modifying "God.")

"Nor" introduces the second object, "desire" which parallels "God."

("The" modifies "desire."
"Of women" is a prepositional phrase modifying "desire.")

So in the verse about the antichrist, taken from **Daniel 11:37**

*Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all.*

...the Bible says that the antichrist shall not regard the God of his fathers, shall not regard the desire of women, nor shall he regard any god, (small L lords.) Why? For (because, for this reason) he shall magnify himself above all. 

It's easy to get caught in strange doctrine and weird beliefs when you don't understand how our language works. Especially when you refuse to attend church and despise correction.

teachings.title: Reading the Bible for yourself
teachings.summary: Encourages reading the Bible itself through a reading plan instead of study Bibles or devotionals, and notes that Psalms and Proverbs read twice cover a year.
teachings.text:
If you want to grow closer to the Lord this year, I encourage you to find a Bible reading plan and stick with it. 

Don't use study Bibles or devotionals or a verse of the day. Make 2025 the year you take the training wheels off and read the Bible for yourself in the Spirit. 

There is no devotional or study guide better than the Bible itself. We have the whole word of God, He can talk to you everyday if you let Him. What a privilege! What a blessing!

Did you know there are 150 Psalms and 31 chapters of Proverbs? That's 181 chapters. If you use them as a daily devotional in addition to regular reading, that covers a half of a year. 

If you read through Psalms and Proverbs twice, that's 362 days. (God even gives you 3 days of grace a year!)

Instead of reading other people's prayers, or verses curated and taken out of context in a devotional, why not read the prayer book and wisdom written by the Lord?

teachings.title: The doctrine of baptisms
teachings.summary: Reads Hebrews 6, Mark 1, John 20 and Acts 2 to explain that there are three baptisms in the New Testament: John's and the believer's by water, and the Spirit's by God.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1-3**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, Of the **doctrine of baptisms**, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. And this will we do, if God permit.*

The doctrine of baptisms, plural, is one of the "milk of the word" doctrines according to Paul.
