Along with the understanding of salvation in Christ, repentance from dead works (both ceremonial and self-righteous) and of faith towards God (biblical repentance), laying on of hands as a means of ordination and ministry, the resurrection at the day of the Lord, the rapture and the eternal judgment of Christ, the judge of the quick (we who are saved, at His judgment seat) and the dead (the damned, cast into the lake of fire at the Great White Throne).

Each one is prone to misunderstanding and abuse and heresy, despite them being the foundational doctrines of the faith. If we are to grow as Christians we need this milk to be understood, that we may go on to the meat of the word. 

There are three main baptisms mentioned in the New Testament. Two water and one fire. All significant. 

First, to define the word, baptism means to be immersed, to become part of, to join with. It does not mean to wash or get wet. Jesus uses the term to mean to be part of His suffering. To join in it. To be immersed:

**Matthew 20:22 **
*But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able*.

This understanding of the word is why Baptists fully submerge believers, in the likeness of His death, burial and resurrection. Sprinkling and pouring are a taste of a thing, baptism is to become one with it.

Baptism then to be fully joined to something, we see then there are more than one method or reason, and of what one is joining and becoming part of. 

While Jesus uses the term to mean partaking in the unique suffering, death and Hell He would experience, in **Matthew 20:22**, there are 3 other Baptisms man could partake in mentioned in the Bible. 

This first is the Baptism of John. The baptism unto repentance. 

**Matthew 3:1-6**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.*

John as prophet was leading all who would hear to make their hearts ready for the Christ Who would come, to understand that the prophesied Kingdom of Heaven was near. They believed the word of God and were baptized in the water of the Jordan. But they did not know Who would be the Christ, let alone what Jesus would do to deliver them. 

They had the scriptures John preached to them, and the same faith of other Old Testament saints of deliverance. But the specifics were not clear, and faith in Christ to come was given from the word alone. 

They were led to repentance from dead works and faith towards God, but received not the sign of Jonas, nor the holy Spirit. This is an important point to keep in mind. They confessed sins, admitting they needed salvation and placed their trust alone in Him without ever seeing Jesus. But their hearts were prepared to receive Him. The paths made straight. The King's Highway laid.

**Mark 1:1-11**
*And John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey; And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose. **I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost**. And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan. And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.*

John the Baptist preached that the Christ he was preparing the way for was not only greater than he, but that He would baptize believers with the holy Ghost the way John has with water. 

Matthew 3:11 
*I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: **he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:** Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.*

Jesus is the first water baptism that the holy Ghost was involved with. The only one up and until after the resurrection. But John speaking the word of God promised they would be baptized by the holy Ghost, by the Spirit, as with fire. Signifying there was another baptism than his.

*I indeed baptize you with water **unto** repentance...*

Unto is another word with specific meaning. As the scripture uses it, unto means move towards till joined or completed, the state of going to a specific end, or being made part of that end. 

John's baptism is repeatedly called the baptism UNTO repentance. For the forgiveness of sins. These people were before Christ, in the old covenant, without the Spirit, only faith in a promise yet to be fulfilled. They were baptized unto repentance, in the lifetime of Jesus that when He came, they knew Him. 

**John 1:40-41**
*One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother. He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.*

**Luke 7:17-23**
*And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about. And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight. Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached. And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.*

Unlike the prostyles of the Pharisees and Sadducees, who were not meet for repentance. Who were being made twofold more the child of Hell by their vain traditions, the disciples of John had repented to believe the Christ was imminent. Even if there was doubts and wonder, they sought after Christ in Whom all their faith layed. 

**John 11:25-27 **
*Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.*

They had been baptized with the baptism UNTO repentance. To the faith in something yet to come. In someone yet to prove they were the anointed of God. Jesus before the death, burial and resurrection. Without the Spirit yet sent to them. Without the baptism of fire.

**John 20:20-22**
*And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord. Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost*.

The disciples and Apostles gathered in the great room after Jesus' death. There He revealed Himself to them, and it was there that He breathed the Spirit, the Holy Ghost upon them. The baptism of the Spirit of God He had promised them. 

**John 3:5-6**
*Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.*

They were born again in the Spirit, quickened, regenerated and sealed unto redemption. This is a separate occurrence from the gifts of the holy Ghost that came as tongues of fire upon them at Pentecost. 

**Acts 1:4-8 **
*And, being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye have heard of me. **For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost** not many days hence. When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. **But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you**: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.*

It was during this time the resurrected Jesus taught them of yet another water baptism, in the name of the Father, Son and holy Spirit.

**Matthew 28:18-20**
*And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, **baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost**: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. Amen.*

The baptism of John was, we have to assume, was in the name of the Lord. Jehovah God. People were saved by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord since the sons of Seth. The baptism of the holy Ghost, the Spirit of regeneration and forgiveness of sins, is in the name of Jesus. 

But the new criteria for the ordinance of water baptism for believers was in the name of the Godhead itself, Father, Son and Ghost.

**Acts 2:38 **
*Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost*.

Peter preaching at Pentecost lays out all the ways the Jews gathered there had failed to recognize Christ among them, killed their Saviour and not believing the promise of God which all the prophets gave witness. He calls on them to change their minds, believing and in Jesus' name, be baptized by the holy Spirit for the remission of sins.

He isn't leading them to water. He isn't ignoring Christ's great commission to water baptize in the name of the Father, Son and holy Ghost. He is talking about being born again in the Spirit, baptized by fire.

**Acts 8:34-39 **
*And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.*

Here, we see how salvation is by faith, hearing the word of God. Calling upon the name of Christ Jesus, and this is required before water baptism. Believers baptism in the name of the Trinity is the only water baptism of the New Testament. And it is different from the baptism of John unto repentance. 

**Acts 19:1-7**
*And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost. And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus. When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied. And all the men were about twelve.*

First, Paul differentiates John's baptism from what he is preaching to them. John baptized **unto** **repentance** *that they should believe on Him which should come after him. *

But hearing the gospel, the truth that Jesus is the Christ, and had come, Paul asks if they'd been baptized by the holy Spirit.

In my opinion, these men believed God and it was counted for righteousness. Had they died before this moment, I believe they were saved. Yet they were lacking the truth of Jesus and the baptism of the holy Spirit that was now available to them. 

Note that it is **after** they call upon the name of Christ and are baptized by the Spirit that Paul then lays hands upon them, ordaining them to ministry with the gifts of the holy Ghost. 

These gifts were given the first generation of believers, to be a sign and witness, absent the completion and availability of the scriptures. Before the Bible was complete and available. This is the difference between what happened on the great room when Jesus breathed in the gathered disciples, and the gifts of the Ghost that came on Pentecost. 

One is a baptism of regeneration and forgiveness which all believers receive, the other a special gifting of supernatural abilities not given to all who are saved.

And so, in my opinion, there are 3 primary baptisms in the New Testament. Two by water, acts of man to give testimony of their faith, and one by God, of fire, given by the Spirit upon repentance towards that faith. 

John's was for repentance to come. The Spirit, upon repentance. Believers baptism for those to whom repentance and Spiritual baptism had already occurred. 

The Apostle Peter, writing to the saints about the salvation from mockers and scoffers, as Noah was saved by the flood from those disobedient who jeered at his faith, compares the ordinance of believers baptism to the deluge:

**1 Peter 3:21 **
*The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ*

He says, it isn't the means of putting away the filth of the flesh, of how we are cleaned from sin, but **an answer** of a good conscience, received already by the resurrection of Jesus Christ. By faith in His being risen from the dead. By the baptism of the Spirit, inwardly, that seals us and quickens us and is the earnest payment, a promise for redemption in the last days giving us a clean conscience that we may be baptized in the name of the Father, Son and holy Spirit without fear. Knowing our sins are forgiven. Being adopted as sons of God.

That's a lot of Bible. I don't claim to know definitively that this is all there is to understand about the doctrines of baptisms, but it occurs to me that the Bible teaches this. I would ask that Christians of good faith spend the time to read it and search the scriptures to see if it is so. And enter the new year with the joy of the Spirit, having been baptized by fire into the Kingdom of Heaven.

teachings.title: The Olivet Discourse was spoken to believers
teachings.summary: Shows from the use of ye and they that Jesus spoke the Olivet Discourse to His disciples, with redemption drawing nigh for them.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 7:14 **
*Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.*

**Isaiah 9:6 **
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace*.

**Micah 5:2 **
*But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.*

To Him gave all the prophets witness.
Amen

Dispensationalists falsely claim that the Olivet Discourse found in **Matthew 24, Luke 21** and **Mark 13** are "written to the Jews, not believers. There is no evidence of this, but there is clear evidence that Jesus was speaking to His disciples, believers, and made a clear distinction between "ye" and "they."

**Luke 21:7-28** 
*And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass? And he said, Take heed that **ye** be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go **ye** not therefore after them. But when **ye** shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by. Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven. But before all these, they shall lay their hands on **you**, and persecute **you**, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake. And it shall turn to **you** for a testimony. Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what **ye** shall answer: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all **your** adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist. And **ye** shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of **you** shall they cause to be put to death. And **ye** shall be hated of all men for my name's sake. But there shall not an hair of **your** head perish. In your patience *possess ye your* souls. And when **ye** shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

Then let **them** which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let **them** which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not **them** that are in the countries enter thereinto. **For these be the days of vengeance**, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. But woe unto **them** that are with child, and to **them** that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon **this people**. And **they** shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. 

And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men's hearts failing **them** for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken. And then shall **they** see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and **lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.***

Jesus speaking to saved Christians, His disciples, uses "ye" and "you," but talking about the unbelieving Jews, uses "they" and "this people." 

"They" get the days of vengeance. "Ye" get "your redemption." It's a clear distinction. It is not "written to the Jews," but to believers.

teachings.title: Rebellious people and joining a church
teachings.summary: Sets Isaiah 30 on people who want smooth things beside the observation that telling saved people to join a church makes them spiral.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 30:9-13**
*That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord: Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us. Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon: Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.*

Tell people that if they are saved, they should go join a church, and they SPIRAL.

teachings.title: Avoid those who teach against attending a local church
teachings.summary: Warns to mark and avoid anyone online teaching that believers should not attend a local New Testament church.
teachings.text:
One more quick note: If you see someone online using whatever clout and reach they have to teach that you shouldn't attend a local NT Christian church, mark and avoid them. 

If they are teaching for commandments the doctrines of men, such as "all churches are 501c3 FEMA centers and the 'pastors' are greedy and money hungry so you don't have to go!" they are misleading people. 

They might be just justifying their own sin, and getting others to partake in it. Or they might be vipers with other weird doctrines and they want to keep you under their power, and away from normal Christians and pastors who teach rightly. Either way, they are wrong and shouldn't be listened to.

teachings.title: Why join a local church: Ephesus and definitions
teachings.summary: Opens a pre-Christmas series urging saved believers to join a local church, defining church as a called-out assembly of believers and starting through the seven churches of Revelation.
teachings.text:
This offended some, good. It should spur you to do what's right in the eyes of God. 

I understand the inertia that not going to church builds up. I have suffered through it at times in my life. I have bemoaned the lack of good churches in my immediate (and convenient) area, and used it as an excuse to put off going to a church, a called out assembly of believers, getting baptized into the congregation, plugged in, under a qualified man of God. 

What I never did was lie to myself that I was right with God by forsaking the assembly. What I never did was encourage others to do the same with foolish excuses. 

If you have social anxiety, or some other lame excuse, or you truly live in an area where there are no Bible-believing independent NT churches preaching the right gospel, you should still be encouraging others who aren't in that situation to attend. 

It is where the works of God are done. Edifying others, praying as a group, singing Psalms and hymns, giving one to another, learning under a pastor, and most importantly, soul winning and evangelizing of some kind, even if it's just invitations and tracts. 

"They are all 501c3s!" No they aren't. Some might be, most aren't. Tax status and how the books are kept isn't a biblical reason to avoid a church anyway. The doctrine is. 

"Church can be anywhere! It doesn't have to be a special building!" Yes. It's the people, so true. But the people gathering in one central location, and an appointed time, with a roof and heat and lights sure is a blessing. 

Most people who say "church can be anywhere!" don't actually go anywhere to gather together. They stay at home and watch YouTube and Rumble and sit in group chats and discords and spread foolish doctrines. In my experience. 

If this is you, and it offends you, good. It should provoke you to to do the right thing. Here is a fantastic resource for American Christians;

https://militarygetsaved.tripod.com/

Imagine going to a church, learning it is correct on the gospel, every member is a confessing born-again Christian, the pastor is qualified, and then saying "Well, I need to see your accounting before I come here. How do you arrange your taxes?" 

Foolishness!

teachings.title: Knowing God's will starts with the basics
teachings.summary: Says those who claim a special walk with Jesus but spend more time online than in the Bible or church will never find the deeper things of God.
teachings.text:
Oftentimes, people who say that they have learned how to have a special relationship and walk with Jesus, so that they can listen to God and discern his will, spend more time online than they do reading the Bible. And most don't go to church.

If you claim to want to know God's will for your life, and you don't do the basic things layed out in the Bible, then you'll never figure out the deeper things that He has in store for you.

teachings.title: The preserved words of the LORD
teachings.summary: Reads Psalm 12:6-8 on the Lord preserving His pure words and notes the KJV defines its own words and uses nothing outside the dictionary.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 12:6-8**
*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.*

God-made theology, that His word is inspired and preserved for all time, settled in Heaven before the world was made, the unchanging rock upon which our faith rests, is true and the Authorized Version, called the KJV, is that preserved word, in English.

And not a word in it is not found in the dictionary, with the meaning expressed in scripture as an entry. And the KJV also acts as its own reference, defining the words itself.

teachings.title: What the Bible says an idol is
teachings.summary: Defines an idol as any image or representation made by hands for religious service, whether of God, Christ crucified, angels or creatures.
teachings.text:
God says not to make idols. Not to bow before them or serve them. To not offer any kind of sacrifice to one, or to pray to them or to the spirit they believe it represents, for deliverance or favor. Not to light incense or candles to one.

According to the Bible, an idol is any image or representation, made by hands, representing either the living God in any form, including Christ crucified, or any representation of the creation, such as the goats of heaven, angels, a man, woman, or animal, used in religious services.

teachings.title: Was Mary good?
teachings.summary: Answers that Mary, like every believer, was made good only in Christ and called God her Saviour in Luke 1.
teachings.text:
Was Mary good?

I'm not good, either. 
But in Christ I am made good in Him, and saved by so sweet a Savior!

Just like my sister Mary. 

**Luke 1:46-47**
*And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.*

teachings.title: Lying vanities forsake mercy
teachings.summary: Warns that those who deceive themselves with vain lies about their behavior forsake their own mercy and reap what they sow.
teachings.text:
One of the things that you learn when you read the Bible regularly is that if you choose to deceive yourself, and tell yourself vain lies about your own behavior, God has no mercy for you. You will reap what you sow. 

That should terrify people. And yet...

**Jonah 2:8**
*They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy*.

teachings.title: Eating candy and conscience
teachings.summary: Applies 1 Corinthians 10 to what is sold or given at Halloween, eating without asking question for conscience sake unless another's conscience is affected.
teachings.text:
Here is my policy on eating miniature Butterfingers, Whoppers, Milky Ways, etc...that may come into my possession today and tomorrow 

**1 Corinthians 10:25-30**
*Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake:
For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof. If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake. But if any man say unto you, this is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience? For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks?*

teachings.title: The order of events: tribulation, then the gathering
teachings.summary: Says Jesus gave the order of events, with the rapture after the tribulation and before the wrath of God, matching Revelation 6, 7, 13 and 14.
teachings.text:
Pre-tribbers hate this. But Jesus was very clear, this is the order of events.

This is the same order of events given in Revelation 6 and 7. 

There is no secret rapture before the tribulation. There is a very public and unquestionable rapture before the wrath of God is poured out, after the tribulation.

Revelation 13 and 14 give the same events from a different perspective. The beast makes war upon the saints. This is the great tribulation. And the harvest is the rapture.

teachings.title: How you can know you are a child of God
teachings.summary: Answers that assurance rests on the promise of God who cannot lie to all who believe on Christ and call on His name, not on our desire or willingness to obey.
teachings.text:
The answer is "Because God Who cannot lie promised before the foundation of the world that whosoever believes on Christ Jesus, calling upon His name for salvation, has eternal life, and are sealed and regenerated by the Spirit that you may KNOW you are a child of God. 

MacArthur makes it of herself. Her desire. Her willingness to obey God. All of these things that any Christian may struggle with at times. 

He makes it of her because he doesn't believe that God's grace extends to all, that it is conditional of accepting the free gift, and that we may know we can trust God's word.

teachings.title: Jesus quoted the Old Testament
teachings.summary: Counts Jesus' 78 and the apostles' 209 quotations of the Old Testament, none from the Apocrypha.
teachings.text:
Jesus quoted the Old Testament 78 times, the Pentateuch alone 26 times. He quoted from Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, Hosea, Amos, Jonah, Micah, and Malachi. He referred to the Old Testament as “The Scriptures,” “the word of God,” and “the wisdom of God.” The apostles quoted 209 times from the Old Testament. 

None of these are quoted from the Apocrypha.

teachings.title: Praying to saints is superstition
teachings.summary: Says Catholic prayers to saints treat them as house gods or demigods and amount to a spell no less superstitious than pagan practice.
teachings.text:
Catholics will say they don't pray for the power of the saints to be given to them. But they always vacillate between "intercession" and actually having the spirit they claim to be praying to, to work a miracle themselves. They treat these idols and spirits as house gods or demigods. It is wicked as Hell

Note the casual blasphemy that a man was as perfect, complete in righteousness, as Christ, and that God gave this demigod a magic ability to find lost items, through an incantation. A spell basically, that invokes this magic power for the caster. 

It is no less superstitious and profane than common pagans, witches and sorcery.

teachings.title: Jots and tittles are Hebrew
teachings.summary: Notes that jot and tittle are terms of the Hebrew alphabet, showing Jesus quoted the Hebrew text and not the so-called LXX.
teachings.text:
*For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled*...

Reminder that Jesus and the Apostles quoted the OT from the Hebrew texts, compiled by Levite scribes, and not a Greek translation, or the so-called LXX. 
 
Jots and tittles are explicitly terms from the Hebrew alphabet and written Hebrew. A jot refers to *yod*, the smallest letter in their alphabet, and tittles a pen stroke or accent mark that differentiates one Hebrew letter from another.

teachings.title: Bonosus and the perpetual virginity of Mary
teachings.summary: Records the fourth century bishop Bonosus who taught against the perpetual virginity of Mary and was condemned by Rome.
teachings.text:
Bonosus was a Bishop of Sardica in the latter part of the fourth century, who taught against the doctrine of the perpetual virginity of Mary. His followers were later labelled "Bonosians" and considered heretical by Roman apostates.

The council of Capua (391) condemned Bonosus and tried to excommunicate him, but Bonosus did not stop using his episcopal functions.

The Bonosians rebaptized converts from Roman Catholicism.

teachings.title: Romans 3 against works salvation
teachings.summary: Walks through Romans 3 to show that no flesh is justified by the deeds of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ.
teachings.text:
A key passage teaching against the damnable heresy of works salvation comes in **Romans 3**, where Paul writes;

*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God...**Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.**

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: **For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:** Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus...Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. **Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.***

Of course, this passage clearly states that by works of the law, no flesh shall be justified. It is undeniable.

But a common argument against the scripture that they will use is that "works of the law" refers only to the ceremonial law of the Old Testament. The Levitical laws and ordinances, sacrifices and washings done away with in the New Testament. *
*
Fortunately, we have the full context, established in the previous chapter.

**Romans 2:14-15** 
*For when the **Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves**: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)*

Paul, speaking of the Gentiles, says they do by nature the things contained in the law. That they have the works of the law written in their hearts, even in their conscience. 

Is Paul saying the Gentiles are keeping feasts and sabbaths and not mixing fabrics "by nature?" That the sacrifices and offerings and other carnal ordinances of the Levitical ceremony is written in their hearts? 

Of course not. That's foolishness. 

The law is the knowledge of sin. A schoolmaster to lead us to repentance, that we accept Christ as our savior. 

Paul clearly means the commandments and civil ordinances that make up the law of God when he writes that no flesh shall be justified by the deeds of the law. By works. 

For sin is the transgression of the law.

God is not the author of confusion. Let God be true and every man a liar. 

We conclude that no flesh shall be justified by the deeds of the law, but by faith. Believing on Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Repent-of-your-sins is a false gospel
teachings.summary: Notes the inconsistency of KJV-only believers who claim grace alone through faith alone yet teach repent-of-your-sins and Lordship salvation.
teachings.text:
It is amazing to me that there are supposed KJVOists, who claim salvation is by grace alone through faith alone, and yet teach the false gospel of "repent-of-your-sins" which comes from satanic perversions.

It always amazes me when a Protestant tries to use this passage to justify baptizing babies, or to say that it is a "means of Grace," That somehow the water water creates the ability for someone to believe. 

And when you show them this order of operations and break it down for them, they simply cannot understand it. They see baptism saves and call it a day. 

The only thing that can explain their inability to simply read the passage and follow along the order of operations is that they are spiritually blinded. They have a supernatural blindness to the truth

teachings.title: What IFB stands for
teachings.summary: Explains Independent, Fundamental and Baptist, and that a believer can walk away to another church when a church stops holding those things.
teachings.text:
They were called fundamentalists first in America.

**I** for independent of any denomination.
 
**F** for fundamentalist by inclination and practice. 

**B** for Baptist because they agree on the first two.

And when they don't anymore we can walk away, and go to another church that does. It's amazing how God's system for churches is so much superior to man's.

teachings.title: Matthew 23 and the Catholic catechism
teachings.summary: Reads Jesus' woes on the scribes and Pharisees as describing Catholic and related false religion, noting that their dogmas keep people from believing the gospel.
teachings.text:
It's the most wicked of all their damnable heresies and doctrines of devils. 

Calling faith "sin." 

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.*

In **Matthew 23**, as Jesus preaches hard against the Jewish religious leaders who perverted the law and led their charges to perdition, He points out their pride in their fathers and their tradition, despite their fathers being the same that killed the prophets of God:

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because** ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.** 

Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, **that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.***

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers**.

**Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?** 

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.*

A scathing indictment of the Jews, and the unbelieving Israelites that came before them, but it is also damning the Roman Catholic Church that came after, and those that swear by its "fathers" today.

Those who build up the tombs of the martyrs, the early saints whom the apostate church murdered by the millions. Who now change history and claim a false succession, robbing Peter, betraying Paul. 

Jesus sent among them prophets and holy men and scribes, those made righteous by faith, not by denomination and sacraments and rites, and they crucified them and burned them at the stake, flayed them and put whole churches to the sword. Often burning copies of God's word on the same pyre as the people found with them. 

They claim a lineage with men who persecuted the faithful from city to city, who slew the elect for a millennium, and then the harlot daughters of that protested their whore mother picked up where she left off, and slew Christians all the more.  

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.*** 

Embrace your tradition. Vipers. Hypocrites. Serpents. 

**H*ow can ye escape the damnation of hell?***

If you read the chapter and picture each verse, and how it applies the Roman Catholic Church and the schisms off of it, you understand that this is as prophetic as chapter 24.

And Paul, Peter and Jude all preached on it in scripture. What was and what was to come. And Jesus revealed to John the same vision of the whore. The clouds without water. The wolves in sheep's clothing. It's about Cathodoxy and, new Evangelicals and reformed protestantism. They all fit. False religion is all a sideways corruption of what the Bible says. 

And they all have dogmas and heresies that if you sincerely believe them, you won't believe the gospel. There are boxes that you have to consciously check to believe in. Not that they cannot repent to the truth, but some can't. 

It's why so many are immune to argument, especially from scripture. They can't be shown because their eyes are blind and they can't hear because they are dull of hearing. 

The catechism is a reprobation machine. 

Win souls while they are available to win.

teachings.title: The Shroud of Turin
teachings.summary: Gives the history of the Shroud of Turin as a denounced forgery and points to 1 Corinthians 11:14 against its long-haired image.
teachings.text:
It shouldn't have to be said, but no, the so-called "shroud of Turin" is not "authentic," and has not been proved to be the "burial shroud of Jesus."

It was labeled a forgery by the Catholic Church at the time of its "discovery," when it was first presented to the public in the 1350s. The shroud was denounced as a forgery by the bishop of Troyes, Pierre d’Arcis, in 1389. 

Previous attempts to verify its authenticity have repeatedly come up short, and in fact seemingly confirmed it was a recent relic, made over a thousand years after Christ. Chemical analysis found the stains made with colored pigments in a gelatin medium. Historical analysis of the weave pattern used in creating the shroud wasn't in use during the time period of the 1st century, or the area of the Levant and Asia Minor, but was common in 14th century Europe. 

Anatomy analysis of the image shows that the proportions are wrong. The head too small, arms too long and site of wounds incorrect for "blood" patterns present. 

The new technique, "x-ray dating," does not accurately measure the cloth in a way that proves anything about its dated origin, especially given the fire damage, preservation and restoration it has undergone over the past centuries. True dating is next to impossible. 

Believers in the hoax point to this verse:

**Matthew 27:59-60**
*And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.*

But they miss key context, that while His body was indeed wrapped in linen, Jesus head was covered with a separate piece of cloth:

**John 20:6-7**
*Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie, And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself*.

Further;

**Isaiah 52:14**
*As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men*

And of course;

**1 Corinthians 11:14**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?*

So no, that image going around isn't Jesus.

teachings.title: Mary's perpetual virginity
teachings.summary: Shows from the church fathers and Matthew 1 that Joseph knew Mary not until she had brought forth her firstborn son.
teachings.text:
The "perpetual" virginity of Mary was primarily regarded by the early church fathers as *virginitas ante partum* (Ignatius of Antioch) [i.e. virginal before conception and giving birth.] As regards the perpetual virginity of Mary there was no fully general consensus before the Council of Ephesus [431]. This idea that Mary remained a virgin was not taught by Tertullian, Irenaeus, Origen, and was considered only theoretically possible by a neutral Basil.

And it clearly states in scripture:

**Matthew 1:24-25**
*Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: **And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son:** and he called his name Jesus.*

teachings.title: One mediator and boldness before the Father
teachings.summary: Contrasts the believer's access to the Father through the one mediator Christ Jesus with Catholic reliance on Mary, saints and priests.
teachings.text:
God tells us, who are saved, who have the Spirit of adoption, that we have one mediator with the Father, Christ Jesus, and one intercessor for prayer, the holy Spirit. We go boldly before the Father with confidence as sons.

But Catholics don't. They use idols and "Mary," and "saints" and priests as intermediaries. Because they know in their hearts they cannot go to the Father as sons. 

Most Catholics are just misled. Not full blown apostate reprobates. And they know in their hearts they cannot enter boldly before the throne. 

So the Catholic church tells them to go through stone and wood and to human intercessors, for their conscience's sake.  Very sad.

teachings.title: Repent is not penance
teachings.summary: Says false teachers have turned repent into Catholic penance and that its historical meaning is a change of mind.
teachings.text:
False teachers have perverted "repent" into penance, promoting the Catholic heresy, sneaking it into Baptist circles. They should be shut up by scripture, which shows these vipers teaching works salvation by a "repent-of-your-sins" false gospel. 

But barring that, the historical understanding and application of "repent," as a change of mind, especially upon reflection or new understanding, should also serve to shut them up. 

They don't hear God's voice, perhaps they'll listen to man's.

teachings.title: The Lord's Supper and the word Eucharist
teachings.summary: Distinguishes the Lord's Supper as a symbolic act of remembrance from the Catholic Eucharist as a ritual bestowing salvation.
teachings.text:
No offense intended to you or any saved believer who understands that the Lord's Supper is a symbolic act done with genuine thanks and awed remembrance of Christ's sacrifice when you break bread with fellow believers.

Generally those that use the term "Eucharist" mean an act that bestows some measure of salvation and done as a ritual or rite with meat and drink sacrifices to an idol as part of a perverse and blasphemous false gospel. 

If you happen to use the word in the sense of giving thanks and having remembrance of Jesus for what He did, this wasn't directed at you.

teachings.title: The word of God and the Bible as final authority
teachings.summary: Lists what the word of God is and does, from Jesus Christ the Word to the preserved 66 books, and says those who reject the Bible as final authority reject Jesus.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 138:1-3**
*I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee. I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name. In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.*

**Psalm 56:4-10**
*In God I will praise his word, In God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil.They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul. Shall they escape by iniquity? in thine anger cast down the people, O God. Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book? When I cry unto thee, then shall mine enemies turn back: this I know; for God is for me. In God will I praise his word: in the Lord will I praise his word. *

**Psalm 119:89-90**
*For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven.Thy faithfulness is unto all generations: thou hast established the earth, and it abideth.*

**Psalm 119:105,114-116**
*Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path..Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word. Depart from me, ye evildoers: for I will keep the commandments of my God. Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope.*

**Psalm 33:6**
*By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.*

**John 1:1-4**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.*

**Colossians 1:12-17**
*Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

**John 1:14**
*And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.*

**2 Timothy 4:1-4**
*I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom; Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine. For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.*

Jesus Christ is the word of God. The word of God created all things. The word of God is what we place our hope on, and are never ashamed. The word of God is the lamp to our feet, our shield, our strength and our sword. The word of God is pure, settled in Heaven, from everlasting. The word of God is preserved for all time. It is the source of faith, for faith cometh by hearing the word of God. It is the power unto redemption for all who believe. It is His will that the word be preached to the corners of the earth, to every creature. The word of God is found in the collection of inspired scripture, 66 books known collectively as the Bible. 

**2 Timothy 3:16-17**
*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works.*

That a man of God be perfect, that is complete. Throughly furnished, meaning having everything one would need. 

**Matthew 4:4**
*But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

Every word. 

The Bible is the word of God. Jesus is the word of God. 

And all those who discount this truth, who place their tradition and rituals above the word, who say things like "Jesus left us a church not a Bible," are rejecting the word of God as their final authority. As the head of their assembly. 

They reject Jesus, because the Bible IS Jesus. 

Not paper and cardstock, ink and glue. But the words and their spirit and the truth.

teachings.title: Catholicism and the false gospel
teachings.summary: Says Catholic purgatory and working off the debt of sin make grace no more grace and Christ's sacrifice of no effect.
teachings.text:
Catholicism is leading people straight to Hell with a false gospel and unbiblical teachings.

There is no such thing as purgatory. There was no "assumption of Mary." If you think you have to work off the debt of sin, it isn't forgiven, you make grace no more grace and you make Christ's sacrifice in vain. It becomes of no effect for you.

teachings.title: What an apostate really is
teachings.summary: Answers those who say a saved person can choose to stop believing, defining an apostate as one who knows the truth intellectually and rejects it but never trusted the Lord.
teachings.text:
It's always funny reading posts from people who don't believe the gospel, who reject eternal security and being sealed by the Holy Spirit, who are trusting in their works to save them.... Telling saved Christians that you can choose to not believe anymore once you're saved. That an apostate is someone who believed and received the spirit of adoption and the quickened new man inside of them, who believed in their heart that Jesus paid for their sin... That they can walk away from all that if they "choose not to believe" later. 

It's such a natural man understanding and says so much about them.

Just so we're clear, an apostate is someone who knows the truth, who has heard the true gospel and understands it intellectually and rejects it. Who has tasted the spiritual gifts but not internalized it and believed it in their heart. They've never trusted the Lord. 

The people who are saved understand that you'll never not believe once God has begun the work in you. It's impossible. 

*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

teachings.title: The God of the Old Testament is the God of the New
teachings.summary: Calls the idea that the Old Testament God is a different or evil God a damnable heresy, and cites Hebrews 11:6.
teachings.text:
Here's a heresy that I have not encountered before. Possibly the dumbest one of all. People professing to be Christian who think that the Old Testament has nothing to do with Jesus. That the God of the Old Testament is a demon.

If you don't know that the God of the Old Testament is the same God as the New, you don't know God. This isn't up for debate. It is damnable heresy and you're perishing. Repent.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

teachings.title: The Septuagint chronology problem
teachings.summary: Points out that the Greek chronology of Lamech and Methuselah would have Methuselah living past the Flood.
teachings.text: The Septuagint forgery has a major problem. The Greek chronology says Lamech was 188 years old when Noah was born, so from Lamech's birth to the Flood was 188 + 600, or 788 years. But claims Methuselah lived 802 years after Lamech's birth. This means he lived for years after the Flood. Which is stupid and anyone using it is an idiot.

teachings.title: You can know you have eternal life

teachings.text:
**Romans 3:10-20**
*as it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, There is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; There is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; With their tongues they have used deceit; The poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Donald Trump's going to Hell, but you don't have to! The Bible tells us that we can know, today, that we have eternal life. A free gift given by the grace of the Father through faith on His Son, Christ Jesus.

If you aren't sure that you're saved, if you are like Trump and are hoping on being good to get to Heaven, please take a few minutes to hear this message of the Gospel. The Bible way to Heaven

teachings.title: Long hair on men and the scripture
teachings.summary: Explains from 1 Corinthians 11 why long hair is a shame to a man, and that a disputed length must still meet the stipulations of the passage.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 11:14-15**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.*

Had someone in the comments to this come sowing doubtful disputations over the idea that there's nothing wrong with men having long hair. They were apparently ignorant to the scriptures, and he wanted to argue the point. 

He asked what I would consider "long." I gave shoulder length as the cut off line, shorter than for men and longer than for women. He tried to offer the old "that's subjective! Cultural standards are relative!" argument. 

And so, I asked him what length he would suggest fits the scripture?

He fled the chat. 

But the truth is, there could be some debate over the specific length, the name of the neck for men. Shoulder blades for women. Their waist perhaps. A man's natural neckline. 

So how do we rightly divide then? By looking at what facts we do have, and applying the word of God. 

We know that **1 Corinthians 11:14-15** says there is a length that is acceptable for men and women. That on a man, nature itself tells us that too long is a shame. That on a woman, her hair should be as a covering for her head. So these points are stipulated:

- That nature tells us it is a shame for a man means that it is not relative to style or changing with the times. It is observably true, in all times, because God says we may know it. 

- Men having effeminate hair being shameful is generally considered past the shoulder. 

- Women must be able to cover their head. So, not shorn or short. 

So, while one could debate the shoulder length line, your alternative interpretation must meet those stipulations. Unless you can, you should probably not come into a chat, guns blazing, or you'll end up leaving as a fool.

teachings.title: The false gospel of infant baptism
teachings.summary: Explains that baptizing infants is a false gospel, since baptism is an outward sign of belief and infants do not carry sin they have not committed.
teachings.text:
The damnable heresy of paedobaptism, the false belief that if an infant is sprinkled with water, initiating them into a denomination, that they are cleansed from sins (that they haven't committed), is accursed, being another gospel. A false gospel. 

This heresy gives parents the mistaken idea that their child would otherwise be cast into Hell without a human authority giving them some form of absolution. 

That the water baptism that is given by God as an outward sign to men that someone has believed on Christ is what regenerates the saved, and not the baptism of the Spirit, as the Bible teaches. That infants carry sin. That God judges the innocent who have not the understanding of good and evil, right and wrong, or the capacity to commit it. 

That the gospel of God is a series of transactions and works instead of a loving relationship between Him and His children. 

Anyone who teaches that infants need to be baptized are not saved.

**Acts 8:26-39**
*And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him. The place of the scripture which he read was this, **He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.**

And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus.

And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?

And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.*

The most comprehensive example of soul winning and the baptism of believers in the New Testament is given here, in **Acts 8**. Water baptism of new believers is mentioned several times in the narrative given in the Acts of the Apostles, but while the order of operations remains the same, the story of Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch is the most detailed. 

We are shown that an unsaved person searching for truth will have opportunity to be given what he seeks. That saved believers will come I their life to preach the word of God. That a saved Christian must lead them through scripture to faith. That faith comes by hearing the word of God. 

And, importantly, we learn what is required to be water baptized, as an ordinance to testify of their found faith, that you *believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God*.

The only examples given are all of adults. And all are believers first, the water baptism being an answer to their good conscience before God, as Peter writes. Not the cause of that good conscience, which is found by the regeneration of the Spirit, being baptized into Christ, spiritually, by faith.

teachings.title: How we know we are going to Heaven

This is just natural man click-bait made by someone who has no idea if they are going to Heaven

We who are going to Heaven know we are going to Heaven because God who cannot lie promised that all who believe on Christ, that His Son Jesus died and rose again from the dead in fulfilment of scriptures, have eternal life. 

Nothing else matters. Not what we do. Not how we feel about it. Only that He gave us His word.

teachings.title: The Olivet Discourse and the destruction of the temple
teachings.summary: Reads Luke 21 on the destruction of the second temple and the signs of the end, noting that believers need not fear and Christ's return will be open and visible, not secret.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:5-36**
*5 And as some spake of **the temple**, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,

6 As for these things which ye behold, **the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down**.

7 And they asked him, saying, Master, but **when** shall these things be? and **what sign will there be** when these things shall come to pass?

8 And he said, **Take heed that ye be not deceived**: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

9 But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, **be not terrified**: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

10 Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

11 And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

12 But before all these, **they** shall lay their hands on **you**, and persecute **you**, delivering **you** up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers **for my name's sake.**

13 And it shall turn to **you** for a testimony.

14 Settle it therefore in **your** hearts, not to meditate before what **ye** shall answer:

15 For I will give **you** a mouth and wisdom, which all **your** adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

16 And **ye** shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of **you** shall they cause to be put to death.

17 **And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake.**

18 But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

19 In your patience possess ye your souls.

20 And **when ye** shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

21 Then let **them** which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let **them** which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not **them** that are in the countries enter thereinto.

22 **For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled**.

23 But woe unto **them** that are with child, and to **them** that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon **this people.**

24 **And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations:** and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

25 And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

26 Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.

27 And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

28 **And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh**.

29 And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;

30 When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.

31 **So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.**

32 Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.

33 Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

34 And **take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares**.

35 For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

36 **Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.***

The construction of the first Temple by Solomon put me in mind of the destruction of the 2nd Temple, as prophesied by Jesus. 

And reading through the end times prophecy contained in what is called the Olivet Discourse, found here in **Luke 21**, and similar teaching in **Matthew 24** and **Mark 13**, you can see the layers of prophecy, both short term and the long term, both as has passed and what is to come. 

It really stands out here in **Luke 21** that Jesus is addressing believers, contrasting them ("You," "ye") with the unbelieving Jews ("They," "them"). For believers, tribulation and persecution, both the disciples of that time, brought before the synagogues and rulers and persecuted for His name's sake, and the general understanding that this will be the fate of believers in the end times as well. "You shall" suffer for His name's sake. And never perish, having eternal life. *Be not terrified...In your patience possess ye your souls.*

This is separate from the "days of vengeance," which came upon the Jews in 70AD as well as in the time to come, after the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. When everyone who will get saved has been. After these many signs take place. 

And it is the same pattern, the armies compass the city about and the Jews fall by the sword. "They" shall fall and be led away captive. 

Many false doctrines claim this was all written to the Jews or that all of this was fulfilled in 70AD and the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple, but the far reaching implications laid out by Christ shows that this was dual prophecy. Many things had to happen then, and are yet to happen. 

Jesus lays out not only the short term, but the understanding that there will be wars and disasters and all manner of tribulation; *when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.*

By and by means soon. Any minute. 

It is also important to recognize that the disciples asked for a sign and the timing of His return, and Jesus provided it to us. He says it is like seeing the budding of a fig tree, that we may recognize the times and the seasons. That we not be caught off guard the way the rest of the world will be. 

The day of the Lord only comes upon us unawares if we are *overcharged with surfeiting*, that is consumed with gluttony and covetousness, or with drunkenness, or the cares of this life. Things of the flesh and of the world, and not the spiritual things of God. 

The rapture is not "imminent," and Jesus does not come as a thief in the night to those of us who keep watch. Things must come to pass, and we shouldn't be afraid, but ready and watchful. 

All who live godly will see tribulation. But not a hair on our head will perish. We have eternal life. 

And when Jesus returns, it will be *with power and great glory.* Everyone will know and see it. It won't be secret. And we who are saved shall rejoice;

*And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.*

Amen

**2 Thessalonians 2:1-9**
*Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him, That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. teachings.text:
“God came in 70 A.D. and did what...? Destroyed the temple. But there’s coming a day, beloved, 
in the future when God is going to send the Messiah back to rebuild the temple.”- damned viper, John MacArthur

Jesus IS the Temple, the Lord God Almighty is the Temple. The church built upon the truth of the Gospel, that Jesus is Christ, are the pillars of that Temple.
