teachings.title: The Masoretic Text, the Dead Sea Scrolls and preservation
teachings.summary: Shows that the Qumran fragments sit closest to the Masoretic Text, that the Masoretes preserved the Hebrew with great precision, and that critical text scholars prefer older outliers over the majority text.
teachings.text:
The "Dead Sea Scrolls" are either forgeries or immaterial to the idea of preservation of the word, being "buried for millennia," however, Qumran fragments can be classified as being closer to the Masoretic Text than to any other text group that has survived. 60% can be classed as being of proto-Masoretic type, and a further 20% Qumran style with a basis in proto-Masoretic texts, compared to 5% proto-Samaritan type, 5% alleged Septuagintal type, and 10% "non-aligned" or original errors. 

Other Greek translations made in the post-temple period after 70AD, such as the Greek of Aquila of Sinope and Theodotion and have minimal differences with the Masoretic Text, unlike the LXX which deviates significantly from other historical sources.

One of the interesting developments stemming from the post 70AD scattering of the remnant Jews, and their increasing slide from Temple Hebrew religion to what is now known as Judaism, was the adoption of numerology and applying these strange doctrines to the Hebrew scriptures. 

Lacking the understanding that the inspired word of God was picturing Christ, and unmoored from even the old covenant ordinances and sacrifices, Jews began seeking understanding from vain and superstitious avenues, which eventually led to the creation of Talmudic Judaism. 

But this foolish pedantry, some of which was seen in the New Testament as Jesus rebuked the Pharisees, resulted in a curious side benefit. If the Hebrew scriptures were to be "interpreted" by legalistic understanding and filtered though the numerology of the Kabbalah, the Jews had to have a consistent set of copies, which kept every jot and tittle, (ironically, just as Jesus prophesied).

Because Hebrew as a written language had no vowels, to prevent misunderstandings of the OT Scriptures, scribes added small markings above and below the letters of the text to indicate which vowels should be used.

The scribes also devised an elaborate system of marginal notes called “Massorah,” which were transcribed into each new manuscript along with the text. 

The Massorah did not include thoughts or commentary on the meaning of the Scriptures. Instead, they recorded facts and statistics about each book of the Bible itself: the number of letters per page, the middle letter, the number of verses and the middle verse, the number of times a certain group of letters or words appeared, and so on. Because of this strict format of transcription, the Massorah locked each letter and word of the Old Testament manuscripts firmly in place, virtually guaranteeing accurate transmission. 

Because of their work on the Massorah, the scholars in Tiberias earned the name “Masoretes” or “Masorites,” and the authoritative biblical text they produced (work that spanned a 500-year window, from the fifth to 10th centuries AD) was called the Masoretic Text. The earliest and latest Masoretic manuscripts match one another with a degree of precision that astonishes modern scholars.

Even in their apostasy, cut off from God and the Kingdom, God used their strong delusion to preserve His word for His elect, believers on Christ.

Fundamentally, what it comes down to is that "critical text" heretics, when given the choice between majority texts used continually for centuries, copied under strictly pedantic methods, manuscripts that largely agree with one another, or new-found "older" scraps and remnants found in caves or in trash bins, buried and unavailable for centuries, riddled with errors and deviating from the received text, they will always choose the outlier, even if it contradicts clear doctrine. 

If it is "older" it is assumed better, and as the viper James White has admitted, if a manuscript was found to be older than all other available copies, he would accept it as correct, even if it denied the very divinity of Christ and the gospel itself.

teachings.title: The Septuagint is a forgery
teachings.summary: Says there was never a pre-Christian Greek translation of the Hebrew Old Testament and that Jesus and the apostles did not quote from the LXX.
teachings.text:
Reminder that the forgery called the Septuagint, or LXX, is gnostic heresy and a perversion of God's word, invented by Alexandrian heretics after Christ's resurrection, full of Jewish fables of the so-called Apocrypha, and riddled with errors and contradictions. Embraced by the whore and her harlot daughters.

It is of the same provenance as the "modern versions" issued from "critical text" readings today. And like all modern versions, is designed to further the satanic "Ye, hath God said?" sowing of doubtful disputations. 

There was never a BC translation of the Hebrew into Greek, other than some verses from the pentateuch. There was no letter, no 72 Israelite scholars. And Jesus and the Apostles did not "quote" from it. It was a Jewish lie from the beginning, adopted by the apostate church of Rome.

**Luke 24:44-45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in **the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms**, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*

Jesus, opening the disciples understanding of the scriptures, lays out precisely the format of the Old Testament, and excludes all other works that some claim to be scripture. 

There is the Law of Moses, the Pentateuch - the first five books of the Bible, credited to Moses. The Prophets, the series of books telling the history of Israel through the prophets of God. And Psalms, the songs and Proverbs inspired by God. These are the oracles of God, the scripture that taught of Christ. 

There was no mention of apocryphal books or texts, because they did not write of Him.

teachings.title: The Septuagint myth
teachings.summary: Argues that the story of 72 scholars translating the Septuagint in 250 BC has no evidence behind it, and that the LXX people cite today is Origen's own work.
teachings.text:
It is harder to take seriously people who think the "Septuagint" (or the "LXX" as it's called) was really compiled and translated by "72 Israelite scholars" 6 each from the "12 tribes," in 250BC than it is to take seriously those who accept the "Dead Sea Scrolls" as authoritative.

It was a creation of the apostate Origen, in the second century AD, filled with errors, contains later apocryphal works, and was used to justify heresies of gnostics in the early Roman Catholic cult. 

Jesus cited the OT scripture, compiled in Hebrew by scribes of Levites, that He Himself had inspired. With jots and tittles. 

The "Letter of Aristeas" that supposedly commissioned this work, appears to have been a forgery written by the Alexandrian apostate Jew, Philo, in the first century AD, to justify his heresies. The "12 tribes" did not exist in 250BC, and there were no scribes in among the long scattered and destroyed 10 tribes of the Northern Kingdom. There is no evidence of the existence of a Greek translation, other than a copy of Deuteronomy 23-28, with zero indication that it was from a larger work, and dated to 150BC, a century later than the supposed Septuagint.

When people today talk about the LXX they are not referring to a translation from 250BC, but are entirely talking about the second column of Origen's Hexapia, where his own translation was recorded.

teachings.title: Look and live: the brazen serpent and John 3
teachings.summary: Shows from John 3 that, like Israel looking at the serpent, anyone who believes is saved without turning from sins or doing anything but looking and living, and will be raised on the last day.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
***And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

When Moses lifted up the serpent, all who looked upon it were saved from the venom of the fiery serpents. All who looked and believed were healed. They did not have to turn from their sin. They did not have to make the serpent the Lord of their lives. They did not have to do anything but look and live. 

Jesus Christ tells us that this is a figure of the salvation that He came to bring the world, that through Him man is saved. That God the Father so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son. And all who BELIEVE, that is trust that Jesus died for them and nothing else, are justified. Given eternal life. 

As Jesus says again in **John 6:37-40**

*All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that **every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.***

Not might. Not if they deserve it. Not if they have repented enough to please some man or group of men, but that see Jesus and believe, and they have eternal life and shall in no ways be cast out. Because the Father's will is that all who look to Christ, raised upon the cross and believe that was for our sin, have eternal life. Will be raised on the last day. 

If you are trusting in anything else but Christ on the cross, and the hope of the promise of resurrection of which He was the first fruit, repent. Think again. And if you don't believe that gift is eternal, that Jesus WILL raise you up on that last day, that your works are needed to keep you in grace, repent. Think again. All who believe are not condemned. All who believe HAVE eternal life in Christ. All who believe WILL be raised on the last day. Amen

teachings.title: Praying to be used of God
teachings.summary: Reads Romans 8 and 1 Samuel 12 and shares that walking in the Spirit shifts prayer from fears and needs to asking God to use us to bless others.
teachings.text:
**Romans 8:18-28**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God. **And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.***

**Psalms 56:11**
*In God have I put my trust: I will not be afraid what man can do unto me.*

**1 Peter 3:15-16**
*but sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

**1 Samuel 12:24**
*Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.*

I think the most surprising thing you find when you walk in the spirit and God is blessing you, the thing that you start to actually pray for, instead of your fears and needs, is that He use you. Praying that you can be the means of blessing someone else. That God use you to benefit someone else, because you know He's already got you. 

Have that faith.

teachings.title: Thanksgiving in prayer
teachings.summary: Wishes more of church prayer time were thanksgiving for blessings, and gives reasons believers hold back public thanks.
teachings.text:
I wish more of the prayer time in a service were of thanksgiving than for asking. It's nice to have people pray for you and your needs, but God already knows our needs. Even if we don't. And He grants us petitions for sure. But the blessings out of the blue, little things even, all add up.

I think sometimes Christians don't give public thanks for blessings in their lives for a few reasons. One, much of the time it is personal. It's something between you and the Father and He blessed you. Maybe even embarrassing, dealing with a sin or whatever. But other times I think people hold off because they don't want to be seen as bragging, or boasting against those who maybe aren't as blessed. 

What if I told you that the people you think aren't as blessed as you need to know they can be. 

Using discernment, tact and grace, with all sincere humility, glory God for all that goes right in your life, especially answered prayers made just in daily communication with Him. 

That morning prayer and Bible reading gives you confidence to ask of God, and He rewards in abundance. In ways big and small. 

People need to hear that. It gives hope to the hopeless. It draws people to Christ. Because you walk in the Spirit and do what you can to not be spotted from the flesh. 

It is edifying to people who may be in a bind to know that faith does favor with our Lord, Who loves us. You read His word and learn it and understand where He's coming from. What He asks. His yoke is light. 

And the gratitude given in thanksgiving from us to God is a light to those in the dark.

teachings.title: Every works religion redefines repentance
teachings.summary: Observes that religions from Catholicism to Calvinism to Hebrew Roots agree in denying that repentance is a change of mind, and so teach a false gospel of works.
teachings.text:
Every religion that teaches that eternal life is not a gift, that you have to turn from sins to be saved, that denies eternal security of the believer, salvation is a "process," that "faith without works is dead" means you aren't saved without works, or that salvation is not offered to all men...every flavor of religion from Catholicism to Calvinism, to Hebrew Roots to Evangelical Protestantism to CI and 7th Day Advantists...they all agree with each other that "repentance" doesn't mean a change of heart/mind/understanding. 

They would condemn each other in a circular firing squad yelling "HERETIC!" over their other doctrine, but they all agree with a false gospel of works. Self-righteousness. Of earning eternal life, and denying that we are saved by grace through faith in Christ, are sealed by the Spirit and held by the power of God the Father.

teachings.title: Salvation is by Christ's righteousness
teachings.summary: Warns against teaching that salvation depends on our own righteousness and reminds that all fall short of the glory of God.
teachings.text:
Too many false teachers are in the world teaching that our salvation is contingent on our ability to be righteous rather than by Christ's righteousness. Denying eternal life. Teaching salvation can be lost if we aren't "good enough." 

News flash, you aren't good enough. No one is. We all fall short of the glory of God.

teachings.title: Calvinism does not match John 3:16
teachings.summary: Sets limited atonement, unconditional election and denial of eternal security against the plain words of John 3:16.
teachings.text:
If you believe in "Limited Atonement," you don't believe the Gospel.

*For God so loved **the world*** ***that he gave his only begotten Son***...

If you believe in "Unconditional Election," you don't believe the Gospel.

...*that **whosoever believeth** on Him*...

If you don't believe in eternal security, you don't believe the Gospel. 

*...**shall not perish but have eternal life**.*

teachings.title: Repent and be baptized in Acts 2:38
teachings.summary: Explains that repent in Acts 2 means to think better of unbelief in Jesus as the Christ, and that baptism follows remission of sins rather than bringing it.
teachings.text:
How baby baptizers read **1 Peter 3**

When Peter is preaching to the crowd at Pentecost, and many Jews who were there were convicted of the heart and asked "*Men and brethren, what shall we do?*" Peter responds, "*Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost*."

This has been abused by many false teachers, both who say that repent here means to turn from sin, and that say water baptism is how our sins are forgiven. 

The repenters argument is foolish and has no basis in the text. Peter clearly explained their failure to recognize Jesus was Christ, and so he is saying they need to repent, to think better of that and believe.

The baptizers argument has more weight. But it comes from not understanding the meaning of the word "for" in this usage, and placing the emphasis on the baptism itself, rather than the cause of remission. 

"For" in this usage is "because of," Jesus Christ the reason.

Because of that repentance, in Christ's name they received the remission of sins, and for that reason they should be baptized.

teachings.title: The critical text and the preserved word
teachings.summary: Criticizes modern translations built on old but contradicting manuscripts over the preserved majority text.
teachings.text:
"Critical Text theologians," who support the modern translations, using corrupt, incomplete or contradicting text found on a scarp of parchment discovered in a cave, or minority texts in trash to be burned, and insist on their use being superior to the preserved majority text, because they are "older," think they are covered on the "*Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it*" clause.

That they have immunity. 

It's similar in spirit to the Jews who put the copper wire around Manhattan. A talmudic Phariseeism that they can trick God. 

They offer a passive aggressive means of corrupting God's word; "Hey, they aren't doing anything of the sort! They're simply using the oldest available text! It's a perfectly fair translation of those corrupt texts. Those verses are missing there, don't blame us!" 

It is like the devil's inverted counterfeit version of God's preservation, except it relies on corrupt texts kept in a burn pile for centuries, riddled with errors, rather than a continuous passing down of unchanging word of God. 

But they see karmic release in their trying to trick God. But they won't. *God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.*

It is the most arbitrary standard that could possibly exist. If they are "older," they are more reliable. If they've been kept from the knowledge of all men for centuries, then it doesn't matter what contradictions they create.

But they are sons of Belial. It's the devil's oldest trick;* Ye hath God said?*

teachings.title: The persecuting spirit and the desire for a king
teachings.summary: Compares Catholic persecution to the murderous spirit of the unbelieving Jews and to Israel demanding a king in 1 Samuel 8, with Constantine offering the church a pontiff.
teachings.text:
Imagine having so much frustration at not being able to defend your heresy from scripture that you resort to the same impulse as the Jews who killed Christ and martyred Stephen, beheaded James and sought the deaths of the Apostles, and martyred so many other believers. The same murderous spirit that drove the unbelieving Jews to this, drives the Catholic Church and its conquests and inquisitions. 

When Great Tribulation comes and Christians are being martyred by the beast, it will be Catholics under the whore mother church doing the beheading. Because all they have is murderous violence, burning God's word, bringing dark ages upon mankind. 

We have the surety of God living within us, and the sword of the Lord, His powerful word. We are meek, and as much as lay within us, we live peaceably with all men. Trusting God. 

We are not the same.

You can see the same spirit that fell on the elders of Israel in **1 Samuel 8**, demanding a king, upon those who fell away from the early churches led of Christ. The desire for earthly power and prestige, and a top-down structure of their own making, rather than being led by Christ in autonomous cells of believers, acting in fellowship, one towards another. 

When Constantine offered them a king, a "pontiff," and the political power that came with it, despite all the warnings from God's word, they jumped at the opportunity. And for 1600yrs they have sought to control the affairs of men, for filthy lucre's sake, damning their people to Hell, rather than accept Jesus as the head. They chant "Christ is King!" but their hearts are far from Him. And they hold the truth in unrighteousness to this day. 

When the Antichrist rises, and a one world Babylonian government presents the Whore of Babylon the chance to oversee its religion, they will trample themselves to take the power offered, even as they slip in the blood of the martyrs they will kill.

teachings.title: Indulgences and prayers for the dead
teachings.summary: Traces indulgences and prayers for the dead to a works-based Catholic doctrine borrowed from pagan ritual.
teachings.text:
Indulgences, the heretical doctrine that says to avoid temporal punishment for sins one must do a work, say a prayer or pay an offering, led to collections of cash to spring the dead from "Purgatory." 

The Roman Catholic Church not only adopted the pagan rituals of prayers for the dead, but monetized it. 

"*As soon as money in the coffer rings, the soul from purgatory's fire springs."*

teachings.title: Assurance is not presumption
teachings.summary: Answers the Catholic claim that faith in the gospel is a sin of presumption, pointing to the sealing of the Spirit and the knowledge of eternal life.
teachings.text:
One of the most pernicious and wicked damnable heresies of the Catholic church is to make faith in the Gospel into a "sin of presumption." 

They take the knowledge of salvation, whereby we know we have eternal life, sealed by the Holy Spirit unto redemption, the earnest of our inheritance, and blasphemously claim that the Spirit of God does no such thing. 

But we who are saved know that we have the Holy Spirit testifying within us that we are the sons of God. 

And we are called to share the glory of God found in his Mercy extended towards us with everyone. Having a ready answer for the hope that lies within us.

Needless to say, this person claiming that having faith in God's promise is "blaspheming the Holy Spirit" Is actually in danger of the very thing he's falsely accusing others of

teachings.title: Purgatory and praying for the dead
teachings.summary: Shows that purgatory is a 12th century Catholic invention and that Luke 16 explains the folly of praying for the dead.
teachings.text:
Purgatory was invented in the 12th century by Catholics who deny that salvation is paid for by the perfect work of Christ Jesus. That our sins are washed clean in His blood. That He is the propitiation, offered by the Father, for the sins of the whole world. That His death, burial and resurrection are insufficient to cleanse believers and His imputed righteousness not enough to cover our sins.

The practice of praying for the dead is found in pagan religions throughout the world. 

But Christ Jesus explained the folly of praying for those who had their chance to believe while on this earth;

**Luke 16:20-31**
*and there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, and desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried; and in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And **beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.** Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: for I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, **They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. **And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. **And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.***

teachings.title: James 2:17 used against the gospel
teachings.summary: Observes that those who use James 2:17 against the gospel hold to a self-righteous zeal not according to knowledge and are very hard to reach.
teachings.text:
When someone pulls out **James 2:17** as a Uno reverse card against the Gospel, they have admitted they aren't saved, and it is nearly impossible to get them to budge from their self-righteous position.

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

They seek to establish their own righteousness, and so they oppose themselves. There are none righteous. Our only righteousness is imputed of Christ. 

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

I have never managed to free a person who has stumbled and been snared by **James 2:17**. All the scripture in the world, and they cannot see.

teachings.title: What fruit means
teachings.summary: Teaches that fruit in the Bible means souls led to the Lord, that good works and obedience are done so we may bear more fruit, and that separation exists for the sake of the gospel.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 3:1-10**
*In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of **the Pharisees and Sadducees** come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? **Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.** And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore **every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.***

**Luke 3:1-*9****
Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene, Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness. And he came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth; And all flesh shall see the salvation of God. Then said he to the multitude that came forth to be baptized of him, **O generation of vipers,** who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore **fruits worthy of repentance**, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: **every tree therefore which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.***

**John 15:2-13**
***Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.** Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Abide in me, and I in you. **As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine**; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. **Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.** As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love. If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love. **These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.** This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.*

"Fruit" in the Biblical sense, means people who've been led to the Lord. Those saved by hearing the gospel from someone else who is saved. 

It doesn't mean doing good works or following the commandments. We do good works and follow the commandments so that we may bear more fruit. 

When John the Baptist tells that generation of vipers, the Sadducees and Pharisses to bring forth fruits meet for repentance, he is challenging the religious leaders of the Jews to prove they aren't false teachers. To produce their fruit who would believe that the Kingdom was at hand. That the Christ was come. 

And they could not. Because they were false prophets. 

**Matthew 7:15-20**
*Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? **Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.** Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.*

This is what happened to the Jews who were charged by God to preach His word and have prostyles, who, when Christ came, would recognize Him and believe. Fruit meet for repentance.

**Mark 11:12-22**
*And on the morrow, when they were come from Bethany, he was hungry: And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if haply he might find any thing thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for the time of figs was not yet. And Jesus answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it. And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves; And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple. And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves. And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people was astonished at his doctrine. And when even was come, he went out of the city. And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away. And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.*

And so we, having faith in God and staying in the vine, producing fruit. Winning souls. 

This is our calling. It is the purpose of separation, being separated unto the gospel. Being blameless that all men are by our conversation the reason for our hope. It's for no other purpose. We are saved to save people. 

**Matthew 13:3-23**
*And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow; and when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up: some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: and when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them: **but other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.***

teachings.title: Underused scripture for eternal security
teachings.summary: Reads Ephesians 1 and Acts 13 as support for eternal security and justification by faith alone, not of works.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-14**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace; Wherein he hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence; Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him: In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will: **That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.***

**Acts 13:38-39** 
*Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: and by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.*

Underused scripture for eternal security and salvation by faith alone, not of works.

teachings.title: Christ left us His word, not a church
teachings.summary: Argues that the rock in Matthew 16 is the gospel Peter confessed and not Peter himself, and that Jesus left His word as a sword rather than a church institution.
teachings.text:
Who should we place our trust in? A church? A denomination, made of men? 

Or Christ Jesus. The rock of our salvation?

The difference between saved, born again Christians and those that believe "God left us a church, not a Bible!" comes down to their saying that the "rock" in Matthew 16 is a man, Peter, rather than the truth of the Gospel that Peter had just proclaimed, that Jesus is the Christ.

It is the good news, the Gospel, which is the key to Hell and death. The power to bind a soul to Heaven, or condemn it to Hell. The power to forgive a brother, bring Him to Christ and by doing so, Jesus builds His church.

"But Jesus only gave the power to Peter!!!" 

Two chapters later, while teaching all the disciples, Jesus said they all had this power. 

Jesus left us the Gospel. God's word. 

Not a church. 

God left us a sword.

Jesus left us His word, not a church. He left us a sword. 

He builds His church from the pillars that are saved believers. Adopted sons of God. And our fruit are those souls won to Christ, who trust in Him alone. 

Not "So long as I..." 
But "Because He said."

teachings.title: The kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Sets Daniel 2:44, Matthew 4, Mark 1 and Luke 17 side by side to show the kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God are one and the same.
teachings.text:
**Daniel 2:44**
*And in the days of these kings shall **the God of heaven set up a kingdom**, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.*

**Matthew 4:17 **
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for **the kingdom of heaven** is at hand.*

**Mark 1:15 **
*And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

**Luke 17:20-21**
*And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when **the kingdom of God** should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, **the kingdom of God** is within you.*

**Luke 13:28-29**
*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, **in the kingdom of God**, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in **the kingdom of God.***

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, **in the kingdom of heaven**. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

There's no way a saved Christian can read these verses and come to the conclusion that they are two separate things. 

The only way they can come to that conclusion is if some false prophet told them so.

teachings.title: Doctrine in Psalm 119
teachings.summary: Points out that two verses of Psalm 119 hold salvation by the word, confession with the mouth, being taught His precepts and eternal security.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 119:107-109**
*I am afflicted very much: **quicken me, O Lord, according unto thy word.** Accept, I beseech thee, **the freewill offerings of my mouth,** O Lord, and teach me thy judgments. **My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.***

The Psalms are dripping with doctrine. Here, in just two verses of the longest (and best IMO) Psalm, you have salvation by the word of God, calling on Him to quicken our spirit as He has promised in His word, the confession with his mouth, the promise to teach us His precepts and judgments. Eternal security. And the understanding that despite our salvation, we still do not forget the law.

teachings.title: The feasts of the LORD, Passover and the word Easter
teachings.summary: Shows the spring feasts as a picture of Christ's first coming and defends the KJV's use of Easter in Acts 12 against claims that Christian celebration is pagan.
teachings.text:
The Lord God gave Israel Spring feasts and Fall feasts; that served as a picture of Christ. 

Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, now called Easter, the Feast of First Fruits, and the Feast of Weeks also called Pentecost, were given as a picture of Christ's first coming. 

The LORD'S feast mirroring the Lord's last supper. The Passover lamb, Christ's sacrifice. The purging of the leaven, the remission of sin. First Fruits, Jesus' resurrection.The Feast of Weeks, Pentecost is known as the Feast of Harvest or the Latter Firstfruits, the day the gospel was preached and 3,000 believed on Christ and took that truth to the ends of the earth, an offering to the Lord. 

**1 Corinthians 5:7**
*Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us*.

**1 Corinthians 15:20**
*But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.

***Leviticus 23:9-12***
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest: And he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it. And ye shall offer that day when ye wave the sheaf an he lamb without blemish of the first year for a burnt offering unto the Lord.
*
Similarly, the Fall feasts, or the Harvest feasts; The Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Tabernacles, given in **Leviticus 23**, all point to the Day of the Lord, the judgment and the rapture. Jesus' second coming, which throughout the Bible is compared to agricultural terms. Harvests. Bringing in the sheaves. The fruit of believers, after their own kind. The increase going to the Lord. 

Amen. 

These feasts and days were given of the Lord to us that we may better understand His word, the fulfillment of His promises in the Spring, a time of rebirth, and the prophetic second coming of the end times.

People get caught up in nonsense peddled by some that seek to subvert the faith of many. Vain jangling. And one of the most pernicious is the idea that since pagans had spring and fall feasts, early Christians must have been corrupted by them into adopting them, and so if we mark the occasions in service to the Lord, we are partaking in pagan rituals. 

This is wicked as Hell. 

Pagans had spring and fall feasts because Satan cannot create, only copy. His pale imitations of the feasts God uses as a parable for His people, were taken from us. Not the other way around. 

The Lord Christ Jesus is risen. The final harvest awaits. Let us come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves.

There is an argument between some KJVOers and those who seek to push false Bible versions and sow doubtful disputations, about the use of the word 'Easter' by the translators in **Acts 12:1-5**;

*Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.) And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people. Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.*

The argument states that since the translators had chosen to use the neologism of William Tyndall, 'Passover' in all other instances where the term 'Pascha' appears in scripture, that either the translation is an error, or they were signifying a completely different feast than Passover. 

The transliterated word pascha, from Ancient Greek πάσχα (páskha), from Aramaic פַּסְחָא (paskha), from Hebrew פֶּסַח (pésakh), was used throughout scripture to refer to the Passover feast of the Lord and the feast of Unleavened Bread that follows, commemorating the use of the blood of the lamb, signifying Christ, and the Exodus from Egypt, signifying salvation by the mighty hand of God. 

Obviously, those claiming it is a translation error are wrong. The KJV is the inspired and preserved word of God in English. Without error. 

But those who should know better claim that the translators made this choice to change what term they used to translate Pascha to teach a secret doctrine of a feast to Astare/Asteroth that Herod was keeping, separate from the Jewish feast. 

This is nonsense. 

The primary argument is that "Passover is a day. Not the entire week long feast of Unleavened Bread, and it says after Easter, so it can't refer to Passover day! Thus it is a pagan holiday."

This is begging the question. The premises are not true, and so the assumption made isn't an argument. 

**Luke 22:1***
Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.*

Same author as Acts, Luke. Same word being translated, here as Passover, in **Acts 12**, Easter. The Bible defining itself, it refers to the entire feast. All the days. 

See also **Deuteronomy 16:1-3**, which refers to Passover and Unleavened Bread as one, long feast;

*Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God: for in the month of Abib the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night.Thou shalt therefore sacrifice the passover unto the Lord thy God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which the Lord shall choose to place his name there. Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction; for thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt in haste: that thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life.*

So we know that these were the *days* of unleavened bread, that Herod sought to please the Jews, and so he arrested Peter, intending to bring him forth to the people, to be executed like James had been, after Pascha had ended. After the feast of Unleavened Bread. After Passover. After Easter. 

There is no other argument made in this regard that comes from scripture. And there is no argument put forth using scripture that supports the claim that this refers to a pagan feast, rather than the Pascha of the Lord. 

That the translators used the only chronological mention of Passover, the feast of Unleavened Bread, that appears in scripture, following the resurrection, to refer to the feast using the English term Christians called it, differentiating the OT understanding from the NT, is in my opinion a deliberate choice. Again, the Bible defining itself.

And the final nail in the coffin of this weird doctrine, that the translators were not talking about the Passover feast, from the feast of the Lord through resurrection Sunday, which takes place during the days of Unleavened Bread, but were actually cluing us in to Herod being a pagan celebrating a feast to Asteroth, is that they included this handy chart to track the days given the difference between the Gregorian calendar and the shifting lunar calendar used by the Hebrews to mark the days. 

"To find Easter for ever." They were not including a means to find the date of a pagan festival. They knew what the word meant to Christians for hundreds of years before them. Easter being used by the earlier translators in place of Pascha, who didn't rely on Tyndall's newly invented 'Passover.' 

It is preposterous to claim to be KJVO and then say the translators included a pagan holiday calendar in it. 

They did not make an error and they did not mean a feast for Astare.

They meant the Pascha, and the risen Christ.

"But there are pagan spring holidays that have rabbits and eggs and fertility ceremonies and sacrifices! Modern use of a bunny and baskets with chocolate eggs are pagan, so the entire thing must be rejected!" 

Again, pagans do a lot of things that they copied from God. The first animal sacrifice is God teaching Adam and Eve about Jesus. Pagans do animal sacrifices too. I guess God was teaching them to be pagans. 

Just because localized cultural traditions spring up (no pun intended) around Christian holy days, doesn't make the holy day wrong. 

When a pastor or someone claiming to be a teacher brings forth a strange doctrine that cannot be proven from scripture, but relies on a fallacious argument, extra biblical sources and teaching for commandments the doctrines of men, judging those who disagree or trying to sow doubtful disputations with those weak in the faith, search the scriptures to see if it is so. The Bible is the final authority.

**Colossians 2:16-17**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.*

One more thing; invariably, almost without fail, the people who push these internet doctrines the hardest, that seek to make celebration of Christ's birth, death and resurrection into pagan festivals to discourage Christians from celebrating, are hardcore Judaizers. 

Lots of sincere Bible-believing, soul winning, separated Christians get caught up in these things, and are just trying to do the right thing for the Lord, as their conscience sees it. **This is not about them**. I want to make that very very clear. 

But the ones who seem to push the notion that "Celebrating traditional Christian holidays is actually pagan. So don't do it!" the most are Hebrew roots types. Like the one who just spammed my chat with some nonsense meme using "hashem" and other Jewy terms to say if you celebrate Easter you aren't saved. 

Jews main argument against Christianity is that it is a pagan religion. They push their noahide law doctrines on Gentiles, that flat out states worshiping of Christ is Idolatry, punishable by death. By beheading. 

And to that end, they promote things like the pagan origins of holy days, and push Christians to adopt Hebrew feasts. To keep the Sabbath. To blow the shofar. 

It is no wonder that churches heavily influenced by dispensationalism, Zionism, and the pre-tribulation rapture, also often fall prey to these memes. They will also teach things like the Satan seed heresy, that nephilim are half breeds, and that "God is not done with Israel yet."

I think dispensationalism is a foot in the door for Judaizers. And Jewish fables claiming that Christianity is just Mithraism, that Enoch is hidden scripture, or that Easter is a pagan holiday, are deliberately done to make the name of Christ be hid. To bring us under bondage. As a snare.

That false churches like the Roman Catholics do pagan things in their religion gives these Judaizers ammunition. They feed each other and do the work of Satan.

teachings.title: Adonijah and the queen mother's intercession
teachings.summary: Shows from 1 Kings 2 that the only Bible example of a queen mother asked to mediate with her king son ended with the request refused.
teachings.text:
There really is only one example of a Queen Mother being asked to be a mediator with her son, the King. 

Adonijah went to Bathsheba to beg for intercession with Solomon in **1 Kings 2**. It didn't end well for him. Adonijah had unsuccessfully attempted to take the throne. Being thwarted, he asks Bathsheba to ask Solomon for the hand of Abishag the Shunammite to wife. 

The queen mother, sitting at the newly anointed Solomon's right hand asks this of her son. 

Solomon rightly sees this as a ploy by Adonijah, and has him killed that day, denying the intercession of his mother.

teachings.title: The timing of the crucifixion
teachings.summary: Gives his view, held without dogmatism, that the crucifixion was on Wednesday and Jesus was taken down at sundown ahead of the first feast day.
teachings.text:
I am not dogmatic on this, but I disagree with this timing and believe the crucifixion was Wednesday day. Taken down from the cross at sundown for the first full feast day (Thursday) which began at sundown Wednesday night. Thursday Passover, Friday Unleavened sabbath, Saturday sabbath. Three sabbaths in a row. No work while Jesus was in Hell. Risen on the first day of the week. 

Shelley might be right. We know for certain was it wasn't a Friday.

teachings.title: Palm Sunday and the cry of the stones
teachings.summary: Reflects on Luke 19 and the multitude praising the King, noting that some who cheered Him were calling for His crucifixion days later.
teachings.text:
**Luke 19:37-40**
*And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen; Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest. And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples. And he answered and said unto them, **I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.***

That verse stirs my soul. That this dead sinner became a lively stone, crying out to the Lord. Amen.

Imagine on Palm Sunday (I think Palm Saturday, but who's counting?) making the same mistake as the Pharisses, telling Jesus that the cries of the people, that *He is the King that cometh in the name of the Lord* was offensive.

Some that cheered Jesus that day were calling for Him to be crucified a few days later. 

Most of the people tweeting "Christ is King" aren't saved. 

*What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.*

 *I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.*

Christ is King.

teachings.title: All babies go to Heaven
teachings.summary: Reads Job 3 and Ecclesiastes 6 to show that infants who die go to rest in Heaven, and that there is no such thing as Limbo.
teachings.text:
**Job 3:11-19**
*Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly? Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck? For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest, With kings and counsellors of the earth, which build desolate places for themselves; Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light. There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor. The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.*

Job wishes he died at birth, to be at rest in Heaven rather than suffer what he did. 

Because all babies go to Heaven.

**Ecclesiastes 6:3-5**
*If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.* *For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness. Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this hath more rest than the other.*

Because all babies go to Heaven.

There is no such thing as Limbo.

teachings.title: Leprosy as a picture of sin
teachings.summary: Notes that leprosy in scripture pictures sin in the unregenerate man and its healing pictures saving grace through Christ.
teachings.text:
All throughout scripture, the disease of leprosy acts as a picture of sin in the unregenerate man. And the miraculous healing of leprosy, a sign of the saving grace from God. Being healed by Christ. It serves as a like image of our spiritual self, consumed by sin. 

And it takes hold of people in nations that are turned away from God.

teachings.title: My grace is sufficient
teachings.summary: A personal testimony from 2 Corinthians 12 of being carried by the Lord in weakness and trouble.
teachings.text:
**2 Corinthians 12:9-10 **
*And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.*

This. I cannot tell you what this truth of God's word feels like, you have to experience it. When there is trouble or you are being tempted, and you think you cannot go on, you turn to the Lord and He carries you there, to where you need to be. It is a peace that passes all understanding. And I praise my God for it, and pray for you all to know the feeling of being lifted up by the Lord.

teachings.title: John 5:24 is the gospel
teachings.summary: Holds that justification is only by the imputed righteousness of Christ through faith, not works, from John 5:24.
teachings.text:
**John 5:24** 
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

This is the Gospel. There are no other way to justification before God but by the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. Who died for the sins of the whole world, a propitiation for sins, especially for those that believe. Sealed unto redemption by the Spirit. Predestinated to be adopted into the promise in Christ, by faith. Whosoever believes this, not works, not of themselves, not by any other means but the gracious offer of God the Father, though the Son, to all who believe.

teachings.title: Godly roles in the household
teachings.summary: Reminds husband, wife, parent and child that each is commanded by God to keep up his own responsibility regardless of how well the others do.
teachings.text:
It's a funny image, but if your life reflects this, you're doing something wrong. 

Each person in this image has a Godly role and responsibility, as both servants and masters. Husband and wife. Parent and child. 

Regardless of how well the others do at keeping up their responsibilities, you're commanded by God to keep up yours.

*And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord. Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them. Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord. Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged. Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God; And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ. But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.*

teachings.title: Preterism, amillennialism and contending for the faith
teachings.summary: Says preterism and amillennialism are signs of a wrong gospel or of a babe in Christ carried about by every wind of doctrine, and cites Jude on contending for the faith.
teachings.text:
Preterism and amillenialism are signs of either believing in vain with the wrong gospel, or in some circumstances, being a babe in Christ *tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive*. Taken away by confident sounding men, rather than Biblical teachings.

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. **I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not..**..But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever. And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.  

These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage. But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ; How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts. These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit. But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ **unto eternal life**.*

teachings.title: John 3:16 is the whole gospel
teachings.summary: Walks through Jesus teaching Nicodemus and urges testing any doctrine against John 3:16, since anything that violates it is a false gospel.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned**: **but** **he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

This set of verses contain everything anyone needs to know regarding salvation, Biblical repentance in the context of salvation. The clearest explanation of the gospel found in scripture. 

He that believes *not* is condemned. 

He that believes is not condemned.

Repent and believe; Turn from non-believer to believer. That is the Gospel.

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved? ... And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

The same Gospel Jesus preached is given by Paul. 

Not believing that God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son is what makes a man perish. Believing that He did, and that His Son is Christ Jesus, gives a man eternal life. 

This is the choice. This is the repentance. This is the good news. That is the God, that is His Son. The gift is eternal. Everlasting.

It's an amazing thing, in **John 3** You have one of the head religious leaders of the Jews, Nicodemus, sitting down with the Son of God, and Jesus teaches him the Gospel. We are allowed to witness this. Think about it. Think about how amazing that is. What a blessing it is.

Nicodemus who is a teacher of the people, well versed in the law, one of the highest ranking Pharisees, rich, powerful, sitting down being instructed by the Lord. And missing it.

*If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
*
We have the preserved word of God, spoken to man, and he received it not. 

And how many people today are like Nicodemus? And cannot read this in all and wonder and take it as God's word that this is how you are saved. That there's nothing more to it than this simple truth.

If someone cannot agree that the plain reading of **John 3:16** is the entire Gospel, they aren't saved. 

*For **God** so **loved** **the world**, that **he** gave **his only begotten Son**, that **whosoever** **believeth in him** should **not** perish, **but have** ***everlasting* life.***

That's it. That's the entire good news of the living God by His grace, His **love** for the entire world, not some. Not few. And for that love, The Father gave His Son as a gift. Not to some. But to  **whosoever**, without caveat or conditions except one, **that believes**. Believe means trust to be true. To have faith in. A secure knowledge. A lively hope. It doesn't mean anything more than that. He gave a gift of His Son to the whole world that if they believe in Him, they won't perish. They will never die. They **have** everlasting life. That means eternal. Never ending. 

This is not some esoteric rendition where the "God" means a mode of Jesus, not a Father sacrificing His son. Or of a Jesus that is not divine. Not where "the world" and "whosoever" don't mean "the world" and "whosoever." Where "believein Him" actually means doing works and trusting in yourself, or a denomination, or rituals and sacraments. Where "perish" isn't wrath and Hell. Where "have" means "will have" or "used to have" "or could get" or "could lose." Where "eternal" doesn't mean eternal.

All of those things, as well as the addition of things and concepts not present in this or the verses that immediately follow them, culminating 20 verses later, God summarizing it once again in **John 3:36**;

*He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

That's it. If you don't believe this is the sum total of the Gospel, the theology of salvation, you need to repent, and believe. Or the wrath of God abides on you.

Pro tip: When someone is bringing doctrine to you that sounds ok or a little sus, and you're just not sure if it's right or not, compare it to **John 3:16**. 

If it violates any of it, you know immediately it's a false gospel. 

There are some doctrines you have to get elsewhere, most actually. But salvation, the most important one, can be taught straight from **John 3:15-18** and **3:36**.

(Go ahead and try it in the comments. Think of a damnable heresy you've heard and see where it violates **John 3:16)**

teachings.title: What the Bible means by good works
teachings.summary: Contrasts Catholic acts of self-righteousness with good works as outward service to others, citing James 1:27.
teachings.text:
I think what is interesting is that they call acts of self-righteousness, like ashed foreheads, rosery, confession and communion, etc etc..."good works." It's the most selfish and self-centered view of Christianity. That the vain performative nonsense they do to themselves are what the Bible means by good works. They practice idolatry, fornication, drunkenness and all manner of sin, they toss in a tax deduction here and there to say they have charity. But all their good works are selfish. And done entirely to "earn" grace, the free gift of God. They believe it is saving them from Hell. It's why they do it. 

Good works are an outward practice towards people. To the benefit of others. 

*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

teachings.title: Rapture anxiety and the pre-trib leaven
teachings.summary: Argues that the pre-tribulation rapture teaching feeds a weekly fear in children and congregants, while the biblical order of end times and secure salvation brings peace.
teachings.text:
There is an apostasy movement happening in evangelical circles that primarily focuses on normalizing sodomites and promoting feminism as a reaction to "religious trauma." It teaches a false and warped view of the gospel, that "Jesus is love," and so whatever you do that makes you "happy" is good. These "nu-Evangelicals" hold the Bible to be imperfect, that much of its teachings no longer apply, or were the opinions of "misogynists" and "homophobes" like Paul. 

They use a mix of genuine failure in their churches, and their own inventions of evil to rationalize their falling away. One of their primary excuses is something called "Rapture Anxiety," and the cause, they say, is the teaching of the heretical doctrine of the Pre-tribulation Rapture. The imminent return of Christ taught by most mainline evangelicals in America today. The primary doctrine of dispensationalism.

While we should note it is their own wicked hearts that has led them to this error, and the itching ears yearning for feel good doctrines from reprobates who have crept in unawares, turning aside to vain jangling, there is a basis of truth to the complaint. 

When a church goes all in on a false doctrine, that cannot be justified by scripture, but only through what amounts to gaslighting, it has an effect. When the doctrine teaches different gospels, different "dispensations," and that the church itself is a failure, due to be replaced by the Jews at any moment, it has an effect. Especially among children raised in it. Add to that the rise of "Lordship salvation," "Repent-of-your-sins" heresy and the holier than thou attitudes these bring, and it is no wonder that many fall for this satanic movement. The church having had a bad report. Lying and dissembling about scripture, and, because they teach a "fruit inspector" mentality, they inevitably fall into cover-ups and hypocrisy. They become respecters of persons, and make excuses for those that are elders, tithe more, volunteer more, etc, while condemning those who they judge are worse sinners than themselves. Who will be "Left Behind" if they don't get right. Heresy begetting damnable heresy. The leaven of the Pharisses, which is hypocrisy, enters a church and corrupts it over time.

Pre-trib rapture is leaven. The idea that nothing matters, that any moment you can be caught up to heaven and so you'll never experience tribulation, appeals to older congregants, but is terrifying to children who aren't secure in the gospel, because they are taught a confusing message of faith plus works. Who are told week after week that "At any moment, maybe before the end of this service, Christ might return!" Doomsday prophets, setting dates on charts are bad enough. But when that date is always "Now!" it becomes a weekly trauma. 

Biblical end times prophesy, the teaching of the rapture being after tribulation, after a falling away, after certain undeniable signs, the man of sin being revealed, etc...is meant to teach us patience and longsuffering. It is hopeful, and should increase our faith. The security of salvation by grace through faith making those that believe understand they are secure, sealed by the Spirit unto redemption tied with the understanding that that redemption may be well after our natural lifetime, leaves the believer in peace. 

The knowledge that the church isn't a "plan B," but the only plan for salvation, and the gospel being true, not changing for different people and eras, is meant to be a comfort, not a terror. Knowing we have already overcome the world in Christ. The peace that passes all understanding.

It would be the height of irony if Dispensationalism was the seed of the great apostasy, the "falling away."

teachings.title: The way of Cain and the error of Balaam
teachings.summary: Shows that selling blessings and cursings is the natural end of a works-based theology.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.*

The selling of blessings and cursings, the "error of Balaam," where a priest or prophet offers to perform a religious duty, or call upon their god for filthy lucre's sake, is wicked as Hell, but it is also the logical end-result of having a works-based theology, where righteousness and blessings are bestowed by the person's own works. 

They make the supposed house of God into one of merchandise

teachings.title: The Bible explains itself
teachings.summary: Notes that scripture interprets itself through parallels between the Old and New Testaments and that God is not the author of confusion.
teachings.text:
On the subject of parallelism in scripture, the best example of it is the Old Testament and New. The Bible explains itself, because God gives examples and parables and like manner of things to explain the spiritual. And then he will do it multiple times just to be sure we understand. 

That's why people who say that interpreting the scriptures is difficult are showing that they're not saved. While there are passages that we see through a glass darkly, most of the truth of the word of God is readily available to those in the Spirit. God is not the author of confusion. 

*But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

teachings.title: Grace and love in human relationships
teachings.summary: Explains that modern culture's trouble with relationships comes from rejecting the free gift of God's grace, and shows from Romans 8 and 1 John 4 that Christ's love is what heals and teaches us to love.
teachings.text:
The foundational problem with modern culture when it comes to human relationships, is that we've abandoned Christ, and so the knowledge and understanding that we are saved by God's grace, through faith, that is trust, in His promise. 

People reject that free gift, offered up front by God, paid for by Jesus. Grace being the unmerited and undeserving favor of God. His love shown by being for our best interest, Jesus dying for us while we were yet sinners. A gift of love. Charity. 

They do this for a variety of reasons, but it mostly comes down to seeing love as transactional. 

They may think they aren't worthy of His grace; an oxymoron. They may think they can earn it on their own, and so they deserve His grace; pride. They may not be willing to trust that which they cannot see, just by the word of God. Trust issues and defensive behavior created through trauma. 

They may have been raised in a toxic household where parents doled out approval transactionally. They may have been raised in a church that teaches you have to work for salvation. They may have been poisoned by culture, as the video posted here suggests. 

But it is directly a result of people and our culture losing the meekness and humility that comes from accepting the gospel, and the grace and charity that follows when you realize what true love is. 

**1 John 4:10**
*Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins*.

**Romans 8:35-37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

It is God's love: The Father so loving the world that *He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.*... *That God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us...*That Jesus so loved us, He died for us...*Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends...For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die*... *For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.*...*So I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee...and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me...And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.*

**Zephaniah 3:17 **
*The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.*

It is by this love that we are healed. This is how the brokenhearted are comforted. This is how we learn to live God with all our hearts and to love our neighbor as ourselves. This is how a husband learns to love his wife as his own flesh. And how a wife learns to submit to her husband. And how a child learns to honor his parents. 

It is how we as saved believers develop charity. 

**1 Corinthians 13:4-7**
*Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.*

Having grace and mercy for others, comes from God's grace and mercy on us. His love for us is magnified through us towards others. 

**James 1:27 **
