*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

This is the purpose of our salvation. These are the works we are asked to do. To love one another. To esteem others more than ourselves. To put their profit above our own. 

**Philippians 2:3-4**
*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.*

If you are saved by the love of God, then show His love to others. Have grace. Understanding that their condition isn't any different than yours. That it is only by the grace of God you're in a better spot than they appear to be. Showing them the love you'd want shown unto you.

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

teachings.title: Once saved, always saved
teachings.summary: Gathers John, Jude and 1 Peter passages to show that the believer is kept by the power of God, and urges trust in the risen Christ.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life*.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life*.

**John 6:37**
*All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.*

**John 10:27-29**
*My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand.*

Romans 8:38-39
*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,  Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

**Romans 11:29 **
*For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance*.

2 Corinthians 1:21-22 *
Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts*.

**Ephesians 2:8-9**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, least any man should boast*.

**Ephesians 4:30-32**
*And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption. Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.*

**Philippians 1:6**-**7**
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.

***1 John 5:10-13***
He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
*
**1 Peter 1:3-5**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that **fadeth not away**, reserved in heaven for you, Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.*

**Jude 1:24 ***
Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy*

There is no doubt that salvation...once we have heard the gospel, repented towards faith in the promises of God, been born again in Christ, our dead spirit quickened, our flesh nailed to the cross, inwardly a new creature, sealed by the Spirit unto the day of redemption, made by God to sit together in heavenly places. Kept by His power to an inheritance incorruptible through faith unto salvation, a promise given without repentance of eternal life, made co-heirs with Christ, adopted by God, the Spirit testifying within us that we are sons of God, our spirit crying out, 'Abba!" Once we have not only tasted of the heavenly gifts and heard the calling, but have trusted in the record and obeyed the Gospel of God...there is no doubt that we shall stand in the grace of God and continue in faith until the end of the world. Amen

Once you are saved, you are always saved, or else God is a liar. That eternal security He has promised is the hope we have in Christ. The rock of our salvation. 

Do not doubt Him that is able to deliver you. Let go and trust in the risen Christ.

teachings.title: Choose life
teachings.summary: Reads Deuteronomy 30 and Joshua 24 and urges the reader to choose life, embrace truth and follow Christ.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.

But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

From the beginning, God has offered us a choice. Without that choice, the evil in this world makes no sense. As the Calvinists teach falsely, their god is the author of evil. But our God provides us the choice between good and evil, life and death. 

Throughout the Bible, from Adam and the tree, through even the Millennium Reign, God allows man a choice. 

Of those that choose life or choose death, God may elect some to serve a purpose. To perform a task. To serve as an example. But the choice of life and death stands before all men. 

When the unsaved ask, "If God real, why bad things happen?" We have the answer; because man chooses death over life. 

Calvanism has no answer other than to profane God and blame Him as the heathen do. 

Without that choice, none of the scriptures make sense, none of the judgments of God are righteous. It all becomes a play, a Punch and Judy show of cruelty. 

Choose life. Embrace truth. Pick up your cross and follow Him. 

**Joshua 24:15**
*And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.*

teachings.title: Eternal security and Judas
teachings.summary: States that those who believe on Christ are sealed and kept by God's power, and notes that Judas was never saved.
teachings.text:
The good news of God is that for every one that believes on Christ - that He is the Son of God, who lived, died and rose again, and that all who believe on Him have eternal life and remission of sin, are sealed by the Spirit unto redemption. To an inheritance incorruptible, that never fades. Kept by the power of God. Eternal security. Once saved, always saved. 

*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

Judas was not saved. 

*Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?*

teachings.title: Titus 2 and 3: grace teaches good works
teachings.summary: Strings together verses from Titus 2 and 3 to show that grace teaches us to live godly and that believers need to be reminded to maintain good works.
teachings.text:
***For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men**, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; **Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works**. These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. But after that **the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour**; That **being justified by his grace**, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that **they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men**.*

Amen

Note that this series of verses from **Titus** 2 and 3 debunks Calvanism, works-based false salvation, and shows that good works are not automatic, but that we need to be exhorted and reminded that they are good and profitable to do.

teachings.title: The children are free: the tribute money
teachings.summary: Sees in Matthew 17:24-27 a picture of the free gift of salvation without works, since the King's children do not pay tribute.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 17:24-27**
*And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Doth not your master pay tribute? He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? Peter saith unto him, Of strangers. Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.*

What a wonderful example of the free gift of salvation, without works. The children are free. They don't pay tribute to the King. We are adopted into the Kingdom as heirs in Christ. We don't pay a thing.

teachings.title: "Wisdom is justified of her children"
teachings.summary: Explains Christ's saying in Matthew 11:19 as a rebuke of unbelieving Israel: wisdom is shown true by the fruit it bears.
teachings.text:
*Wisdom is justified of her children.*

What a profound saying of Christ that I hadn't considered before. It comes from **Matthew 11:19**, where Jesus was just speaking of John the Baptist and is about to lay into the cities that saw the signs and wonders, healings and miracles and yet didn't repent to believe on Him and the salvation of God. 


**Matthew 11:7-20**
*And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses. But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet. For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows, And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented. 

For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil. The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children. Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not
*

It's a subtle and devastating rebuke of the unbelieving Jews, who as Jesus says, dismissed John the Baptist as having a devil for living on locusts and honey, and Christ Beelzebub for dining with publicans and healing the sick. 

That their wisdom, what people think to give as their opinion, is justified by its children, or that is, shown to be true or not by what following it begets. The fruit that wisdom bears. 

It should be used more. It's so true.

teachings.title: The Ethiopian eunuch: a textbook salvation
teachings.summary: Reads the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8 as salvation by hearing the word and believing Jesus is the risen Christ, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
It still stuns me that there are people who read the story of the Ethiopian eunuch, a textbook salvation; from hearing the word of God from a saved believer, to accepting that Jesus was that promised Christ, who takes away the sins of the world. And then getting baptized, already saved, as a believer, and add things to it of their own. 

It's God's word, His testament, that saves. Accepting His word as true. That Jesus is the Risen Christ, and by His blood we are saved. Just as He promised. Plus or minus nothing.

teachings.title: Salt of the earth
teachings.summary: Reminds saved Christians that they are the salt that preserves the world and must not lose their savour.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Remember that we are the salt of the Earth, as saved Christians. We are the thing that preserves the world. If we lose our savor, If we no longer act as the salt, the world is good for nothing. It will rot. Become rancid. Trodden by men. 

Stay salty my friends.

teachings.title: "Naughty or nice?" and the gift of grace
teachings.summary: Contrasts the works-based Santa Claus idea of earned gifts with God's gift of salvation, freely given by grace.
teachings.text:
"Naughty or nice?" 

There is none nice. No not one. There is none that isn't naughty. 

"Santa Claus" teaches a false, works-based doctrine. That gifts have to be "earned" by good behavior. But if you have to earn something, it is not a gift. 

But the gifts of God are by His grace, undeserved, given freely of love by His mercy:

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus*

Make sure your children know that whatever gifts you decide to bless them with, that it is done freely, out of love unfeigned. Unconditional. 

Not by some creepy old elf judging their worth.

teachings.title: Gifts of the Spirit: their purpose
teachings.summary: Lays out from Romans 12 and Matthew 6 and Mark 10 that gifts given by grace are talents lent to serve God and bless others, with a reward in this life and the next.
teachings.text:
**Romans 12:5-9**
*So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another. Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether **prophecy**, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or **ministry**, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on **teaching**; Or he that exhorteth, on **exhortation**: he that **giveth**, let him do it with simplicity; he that **ruleth**, with diligence; he that sheweth **mercy,** with cheerfulness*.

By the grace bestowed on us by God, our talents are lent to us that we may serve Him, and by doing so profit others. 

As we've discussed, knowledge and wisdom are gifts of the Spirit, the knowledge of God's word and wisdom of God found in it; the understanding of spiritual things of God. 

And so the gift of prophecy, stems from that that is preaching of the word. Many confuse prophecy with prediction, being a seer, but absent the visions of what was to come given prophets of old by God, prophecy primarily is simply telling others, preaching, the words of God. 

To the extent that one has the gift of preaching, it is from knowledge. And with the knowledge comes wisdom. It helps lead others to Christ and strengthens the faith of those who have already believed. 

And the spiritual discernment gained from the knowledge, understanding and wisdom of God revealed in His word, allows us to tell truth from lies, and "see the Future," by recognizing the consequences and the inevitability of God's judgement that comes from man's sin. 

It isn't being a seer. It isn't looking into a crystal ball or having a revelation in a dream. It is knowing and understanding God's word and recognizing His will, and applying it to your surroundings and seeing things the way He sees them. Morally, and also temporally. The long view. Thinking past ourselves and our time, to see the holy judgment of God, and be at peace with it. 

And so, with the gifts of knowledge, wisdom, prophecy, comes the gift of teaching. Discipling others. Edifying the weaker in faith and knowledge. Helping them to become more useful to God, and so to others. 

The ability to teach the spiritual things of God, with all patience and longsuffering, is a wonderful gift. Sharing the fruits of the Spirit, the word of God, bringing others to see the simplicity of Christ, the understanding of His judgements, growing in faith and losing fear and cares of the things of this world, fearing only God, learning sanctification and separation, to better serve others. It is a ministry full of rewards. 

The gift of exhortation, encouragement and good cheer towards all, secure in the knowledge of the truth and full of faith in God, that others who are troubled or fearful or uncertain, caught up in the cares of this world, the brokenhearted, and help them gain the same spirit of comfort and hope, grounded in faith towards God. Being *ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear*.

There's the gift of giving, the blessing of being put by God's divine appointments into the position to give to others, to minister their needs. Be they physical needs; clothing the naked, feeding the hungry, comforting the sick or brokenhearted, judging the fatherless that they may come to see the mercy and judgment of God in Christ, or spiritual; giving the gospel, preaching the word, edifying the brethren. This is possibly the most precious gift we are given outside of being able to win a soul to Christ. The blessing of being given the chance to help someone else, brings unexpected blessings upon us. 

We are called to offer the right judgment of God on all those we've been blessed to be put in positions over, all leadership and hierarchy being of God. We are to love, show mercy and  rule with cheerfulness. Not as if they are a burden, but recognizing the blessing it is, that we be better servants of Christ.

God rewards those who diligently seek Him. We are given knowledge, wisdom and the ability to preach and teach His word, that we are able to exhort and edify, and comfort the afflicted. To give freely, to judge rightly, in love and mercy, revealing the glory of God by His mercy towards us, that others may come to believe. 

I feel that it is in these moments, where God uses us and the talents given of the Spirit, that He as the potter has fit us to, is how He rewards us in this life. The blessings that follow our being a blessing to others, is wonderful. God's glory revealed through us.

**Mark 10:29-30**
*And* *Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.*

**Matthew 6:19-21**
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

**Hebrews 11:6 **
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**1 Corinthians 3:7-15**
*So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour. For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

All this to establish the mechanism and purpose of gifts given us by the Spirit. That by the grace of God, who rewards those who seek to know Him, understand His will, given through the Spirit, and by His inspired word, that we may be blessed with opportunities to help minister to others, that we may be blessed in this life and rewarded in the next. 

It is the awesome will of God, manifest in us. 

Tomorrow, God willing, we will break down some of what it's not. And how many misunderstand and misuse the idea of gifts of the Spirit to teach weird and sometimes damning doctrines of devils.

teachings.title: People rediscovering the reprobate doctrine
teachings.summary: Says that as God's wrath is seen on those who reject Him, it opens people to hear the gospel, with Romans 1:16-32 as the text.
teachings.text:
People are rediscovering the Reprobate Doctrine on their own. God's wrath, revealed from Heaven against those who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. Who are past feeling. Conscience seared as with a hot iron. 

It's a great time to preach the Gospel to those noticing

People, on their own observations, are being shown by God's wrath the truth of His glory, and it opens them up to receive from us the Gospel of grace and mercy. It is part of God's purpose that people be led to Christ by the fall of others who reject Him. 

**Romans 1:16-32**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith. 

For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: 

Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Giving thanks: any day honored to God is acceptable
teachings.summary: Answers a claim that Thanksgiving is pagan by pointing to Romans 14 and the verses that call believers to give thanks in everything.
teachings.text:
JK don't listen to Judaizing vipers who say things like this. They are fools. 

**Any day** you esteem in glory to God and thanksgiving for the blessings He has provided, honoring Jesus, or celebrating His perfect work that is our salvation, is acceptable to the Lord. 

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**  
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.*

**Philippians 4:6 ** 
*Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God*.

**Psalms 107:1** 
*O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever*.

Happy Thanksgiving to all my brothers and sisters in Christ. God is great, Amen.

teachings.title: Modern versions drop "hunger" in John 6:35
teachings.summary: Points to the omission of hunger in the NIV and ESV against John 6:35 as a reason to read the Authorized Version, the preserved word of God.
teachings.text:
NIV: Earliest manuscripts and many other ancient sources don't include hunger.

NASB: ....

ESV: omitted - The earliest manuscripts do not include hunger

 
 If you aren't using the Authorized Version, refered to as the King James Bible, you aren't reading the preserved word of God. You will die of hunger 

*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.*

I seriously don't understand how people read the modern translations. The fact that they are all corrupt aside. They are horribly translated and the additions of the doubtful disputation footnotes and the letters and call outs and chapter titles...it's like comparing Shakespeare to Korean stereo instructions.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Matthew 16
teachings.summary: Explains that the rock in Matthew 16 is the confession that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter or a denomination, and what the gates of hell not prevailing means.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 16:13-18**
*When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am? And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets. He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, **Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.** And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and **upon this rock** I will build my church; **and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.***

Catholics cite verse 18, stripped of context, claiming that Simon Peter is the "rock," rather than the testimony that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Despite "Peter," or *Petra*/*Cephas* meaning a small stone. (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*). 

What they also miss is that it is this confession of the faith that Jesus says the gates of Hell shall not prevail against. The "i*t*" in that clause refers back to the "*rock*," which refers back to the Gospel, the truth of Who Jesus is. 

All those who believe on that truth are part of Jesus' church, and the gates of Hell cannot prevail against that confession; believing that Jesus is Christ. 

If we strip the Biblical context away, and try to make sense of it as Peter being the rock, and the church being a physical denomination on earth, what in the world does the phrase "the gates of Hell shall not prevail against" actually mean? 

There is no other reference to "gates of Hell" in scripture, other than Jesus possessing the keys to death and Hell at His resurrection (the Gospel). 

How exactly would Hell's "gates" prevail over anything? How does a doorway to Hell prevail against a church? It becomes a non sequitur in the hands of the natural man, and while it sounds epic, it carries no actual meaning in that incorrect context.

teachings.title: The prodigal son and biblical repentance
teachings.summary: Reads Luke 15 as a picture of the Father's love for His children and of repentance as turning toward Him, not sorrow, willingness to work, or making Him lord.
teachings.text:
**Luke 15:11-24**
*And he said, A certain man had two sons: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: and bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.*

In this beautiful picture of the Father's love for His children, which teaches God's unconditional love for those that are His, even when we backslide, even when we despise our inheritance and go after the world in sin. Even as we served other masters and feed the swine. That no matter what, we may return to the Father. 

More, we see that even though it may be important for us to feel the need to be full of sorrow and remorse at having gone astray, and to want to work it off, to be worthy of the Father, God isn't interested in any of that. Only that you turn towards Him. 

We see the father runs to meet the son. He ignores the son's groveling. Even before the son gets it out the Father has hugged and kissed him. He doesn't even get a chance to offer to work off his sins, the Father sends for him to be clothed in the best robes, given a ring and shoes. To be made whole in the gift of the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. And a joyous feast is called to celebrate. 

Blessed is the man to whom God will not impute sin. Blessed are we who have been forgiven.

When the son *came to himself*, is the moment of repentance. That he needed salvation from the state he was in. Being hungry and without, led him to it. 

It was that turning towards the Father that shows repentance. Not his sorrow and regret. Not his willingness to work, or wanting to make his father his lord.

It was his coming towards the father, who seeing him afar off ran to meet him. 

That is biblical repentance. It's all God asks of us. That we turn to Him and allow Him to clothe us in righteousness that we did not earn or expect or deserve. And to rejoice, celebrating our reconciliation.

teachings.title: Everything is to God's purpose
teachings.summary: Reflects that God can use every free choice and experience for His purpose, because He knows the beginning from the end.
teachings.text:
Everything is to God's purpose. 

It's something that is difficult to conceive, but every free will choice we make, God could say "I can use that." "I can work with that." 

And it's elegant and wonderful. 

Not cheap like writing a story. But artistry with time populated by independent consciousness, all reacting and moving of their own volution, but yet always to His purpose. Because God knows the beginning from the end. 

So never let anything that happens go to waste. Do the things that He tells us that it may be well with us, but either way, good or bad, every experience is part of His purpose.

teachings.title: John 6 does not support Calvinism
teachings.summary: Shows from John 6 and John 12 that all men are drawn but not all believe, so the passage does not teach election of individuals to salvation.
teachings.text:
BTW John 6 does not support Calvanism. 

For we know that it is ALL who will be drawn. But not all believe. 

*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw **all** men unto me.*

**John 6**
*43 Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

44 No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.

45 It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.

46 Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father.

47 Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.

48 I am that bread of life.

49 Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.

50 This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

51 I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.*

The life of the world. Believe.

teachings.title: The gospel is not 200 years old
teachings.summary: Traces the same salvation by faith in the sacrifice of the Lamb from Adam and Eve, Abel and Cain, and Enos in Genesis 4:26 to answer the claim that the gospel is new.
teachings.text:
There is a resurgence of unsaved people using the false argument that the Gospel by which we are saved is "only 200 years old." Many heresies come in cycles. You will see the same one suddenly pop-up from multiple people, and it is currently the trending heresy I am witnessing. 

The idea that the same salvation of Genesis is "new," is absurd. 

Adam and Eve, having sinned, sought to cover themselves with figleaves they sowed themselves. God corrected them and showed them, covering their sins with the lamb skins He provided, the blood shed representing Christ's, the redemption by faith. 

Righteous Abel believed God and He pleased the Lord. Cain sought to offer his own works and God rebuked him. And Cain in his pride became the first reorobate. 

**Genesis 4:26**
*And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

This is the same Gospel as we preach today. Faith in the sacrifice God offered for us. Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Justified in the blood. Covered by the snow white wool of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. 

Amen.

teachings.title: Trusting anything but the finished work of Christ
teachings.summary: States that anyone trusting works, rites or turning from sin to be saved is perishing, and gives the gospel of grace by which whosoever believes on the Son is saved, plus nothing, minus nothing.
teachings.text:
If you are trusting in anything other than the finished work of Christ to save you from Hell and death, if you believe that your works play a role in justification before God at the judgment, if you are trusting in traditions, rites, your sacrifices, prayers to saints, carnal ordinances and sacraments, doing good works or turning from your sins to save you, you are assuredly perishing. You must repent towards the Gospel of grace and reconciliation.

The Bible is clear. 

The only salvation is by grace of God, the unmerited favor He extends to all, that whosoever believes on His Son, who was made flesh, lived a sinless life, died for our transgressions, suffered in our place, and rose again to life after 3 days and nights, the propitiation for our sin, and ascended into glory, the first fruits of the promise of eternal life that all believers share. Period. 

Plus nothing. Minus nothing.

teachings.title: Lot and the Corinthians: sanctification does not decide who is saved
teachings.summary: Explains sanctification and separation as service for edifying the brethren, and shows from Lot in 2 Peter 2 and Paul's greeting in 1 Corinthians 1 that sinning believers are still called saints and righteous.
teachings.text:
The point of sanctification and discipleship is to edify the brethren and the point of separation is to be more useful to God in winning souls and being a blessing to others by being blameless and as much as possible, peaceful with all men. 

If you have been blessed to be able to devote more time and more energy to the word, to winning souls and ministering to the faithful as a servant of God, healing the broken hearted with the baptism of faith in Christ, rather than hold it as a standard of piety like a hypocrite, use the opportunity to bear fruit with gladness, longsuffering and patience and receive those weaker in the faith that they can, by your ministering, be disciples that they may do great things for the Lord.

**2 Peter 2:6-8**
*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Just Lot, that righteous man, with a righteous soul, who is celebrated in the New Testament by God as such, dwelt among the filth in ACTUAL SODOM, the most wicked city ever to exist, where there was only one just man. 

But some yahoo with a works salvation false gospel is going to call Lot a "believer" with scare quotes, and imply he is less saved somehow, less of a "Christian" because he had to be physically carried out of Sodom by angels, while another guy has a double wide on a hobby farm and so he's more righteous somehow. 

Hypocrites.

**1 Corinthians 1:1-9**
*Paul called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both their's and our's: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ; That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge; Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you: So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth, to those who are called to believe saints, who received grace of God through Christ, and peace with the Lord, sanctified in Him, and Who shall confirm them unto the end; eternal life.

He says that they are blameless in Christ. That being confirmed unto the end, he is assuring them that they are once saved, always saved. The testimony of Christ confirmed in them. 

Paul is writing this epistle with *Sosthenes our brother*, the same Sosthenes who, in Acts 18 accused Paul before the Roman magistrate Gallio, the deputy of Achaia, Because *Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.*

Sosthenes was Crispus' replacement as chief ruler of the synagogue, and when he brought Paul before the deputy to accuse him, Gallio ignored him and the Greeks beat the rabbi. 

The next time we see him, Paul is calling him a brother in Christ. He's recorded in this epistle as the scribe for the Apostle. 

Really consider all of this, and then understand the context of why Paul is writing to them, to chastise them for multiple sins and divisions. Pride and even fornication amongst them, worse than even the heathens. A list of sins he calls them out for. 

Paul, who persecuted the fledgling churches, helping to kill the saints, dictating to a man who was once the chief Rabbi in the synagogue of Corinth and who had accused Paul trying unsuccessfully to have him punished by the government, to a church full of divisions and boasting, a man sleeping with his stepmother, and all kinds of other issues in the church....

.... And he opens it with that greeting!. 

Go read it again. 

He doesn't question their salvation. He doesn't make them doubt it. He reaffirms the gospel by which they've testified, and through which they've received the grace of God and been called to be saints. Who were not lacking spiritual gifts. 

Really makes you think. 

Really puts things into perspective, especially when you have someone claiming to be a man of God, berating believers as being insufficiently pure enough for him. Who don't meet his standards. Questioning their salvation when he himself preaches a false gospel.

Hypocrite.

teachings.title: Easy believism and the simple gospel of grace
teachings.summary: Answers those who mock the simple gospel as easy believism, saying they add burdens to what Christ paid in full, and calls for repentance toward the gospel of grace and reconciliation.
teachings.text:
People who use the term "easy believism" to derisively mock the simple Gospel of grace and reconciliation, are trying to keep men under the yoke of bondage. They deny that Jesus paid it all. They add burdens grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders. 

If you aren't sure you have eternal life, if you don't know for certain you have peace with God, if you are counting on your own ability to turn from sin, obey commandments or keep traditions of men, ordinances and sacraments to be saved, repent towards the Gospel of God. The truth that in Christ Jesus, all is forgiven. It doesn't seem easy to just believe, but that is the only way to heaven. 

**Galatians 2:16-21**
*knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid. For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God. I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.*

teachings.title: The reprobate doctrine in the old and new IFB
teachings.summary: Says the old IFB and the new IFB teach the same reprobate doctrine, that God's offer of salvation is not available forever, so believe now.
teachings.text:
The OIFB taught the Reprobate Doctrine, focusing more on before God gives up on somebody, the NIFB focuses more on the consequences of after. But it is the same doctrine from the same Bible and says the same thing; God's offer of salvation is not available to all men forever. There comes a time when it is too late, reprobate! 

So don't delay, don't put it off. Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved.

*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, And in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation*.

teachings.title: Metanoia: repentance is a change of mind toward God
teachings.summary: Explains the word translated repentance as a change of mind and heart toward God and belief, and argues that adding "of sin" came with modern versions.
teachings.text:
*Metanoia*, the Greek word translated in our King James Bible as "repentance," is a changing of the mind. “Meta” comes from the root for “after” or “beyond,” while “noeo” is “to think.” So metanoeo means to reconsider or to rethink something. At its root, repentance is about changing one's mind. 'Metanoia' literally means to 'change your mind, to change direction' …has nothing to do with guilt or shame. 

So, when John the Baptist calls his audience to repent, he is telling them to understand the Kingdom is at hand and to have a thorough change of heart and mind regarding salvation and the coming Christ. To reconsider and believe. To be convicted in the Spirit. To turn towards God. 

This has always been its meaning and no one changed it until modern Bible versions in the 20th century began to append "..of sin" and delete the instances of God's repentance, to begin pushing the Devil's favorite damnable heresy, works salvation. 

That's why in scripture, again and again, repentance and belief are used in tandem to express conversion, by believing on Jesus and receiving the gift of eternal life promised by God. 

This is the Gospel of the Bible and how men have been saved from the time of Seth. The notion that it was changed or twisted in the 1980s to something other than that is not only biblically and linguistically wrong, it is absurd.

" In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Feel bad about sinning and try not to sin: for the kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

Hey that sounds like works...

teachings.title: The red heifer and the burnt offerings pictured Christ
teachings.summary: Reads the red heifer of Numbers 19 and the Levitical sacrifices as pictures of Christ already fulfilled, warning against the idea that they are a prophecy for the Jews today.
teachings.text:
The burnt offerings in the Old Testament were all a picture of Christ Jesus. Not a prophecy of the Jews today. See **👇**

**Numbers 19**
*And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

2 This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke:

3 And ye shall give her unto Eleazar the priest, that he may bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:

4 And Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood directly before the tabernacle of the congregation seven times:

5 And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:

6 And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

7 Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the even.

8 And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the even.

9 And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water of separation: it is a purification for sin.

*
The foolish and unbiblical "Red Heifer prophecy" was created in 1989 by an American Pentecostal preacher who practiced Zionist-dispensationalism, and who decided that, since he bred red cattle, and one of the carnal ordinances included a burnt offering of a red heifer, that should the Jews offer one, they could usher in the end times, forcing God's judgment and the second coming of Christ. 

Since then, Jews have been using this half-assed prophecy to fundraise off of gullible Christians misled by Scofield, wicked TV charismatics funded by Israel, and a generation of pastors trained to teach the worship of Jews over Christ. 

We see clearly in the one mention of a red heifer, that it was yet another picture of Christ Jesus. The cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet, present during the time Abraham set to offer his son Issac, upon the same hill Jesus would later be crucified on, and included in many of the burnt offerings described in the Levitical laws, all of which pictured Christ. 

The cedar of the cross. The hyssop soaked in vinegar. The scarlet of His blood given for us. The oblation given of a spotless sacrifice. A propitiation for our sin. To whom no yoke had ever been upon. 

This false teaching is having renewed interest today, as the Jews who say they are but are not, but do lie, attempt to join in the propaganda campaign going on now to meme judgment day into being. To trick God, and despair men. 

Don't be fooled! God's timing is His own and the sacrifices of the Old Testament were a picture of His Son, who has come already and in whom the sins of the world have already been paid by the blood He shed. He was the burnt offering, in Hell three days and nights, and resurrected into glory, overcoming the world. With the keys to Hell and Death. 

Be at peace in Jesus. Let no man deceive you. Be not afraid.

Remember that this is the reason God destroyed Israel and brought judgement upon Judah. Child sacrifice, as the Canaanites did.

teachings.title: God hates: righteous anger and leaving vengeance to the Lord
teachings.summary: Collects Psalms and other verses showing that God hates the wicked, and teaches that believers may hate evil while leaving wrath to God and handling a wronged brother biblically.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 5:5** *The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity.*

**Psalm 5:6** *Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man.*

**Psalm 11:5** *The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth*.

**Psalm 26:5** *I have hated the congregation of evil doers; and will not sit with the wicked.
*
**Psalm 31:6** *I have hated them that regard lying vanities: but I trust in the LORD.
*
**Psalm 10:3** *For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth*.

**Psalm 53:5** *There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.*

**Leviticus 20:23** *And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.*

**Leviticus 26:30** *And I will destroy your high places, and cut down your images, and cast your carcases upon the carcases of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.

Deuteronomy 32:19 And when the LORD saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.

**Proverbs 6:16-19** These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

 **Proverbs 22:14** *The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.*

**Psalm 139:21** *Do not I hate them, O LORD, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?* *I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.
*
**Zechariah 11:8** *Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me.*

**Hosea 9:15** *All their wickedness is in Gilgal: for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more: all their princes are revolters.*

**Malachi 1:2-3** *I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.
*
**Romans 9:13** *As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

God hates. And He calls us to abhor that which is evil that we may love the good. 

A lot of the anger and frustration that you feel is righteous. It's justified. They are legitimate grievances. And it's okay to have that hatred. But God also tells us to leave the wrath to him. That vengeance is His. 

But that doesn't mean you can't hate them that hate God. And that doesn't mean you can't protect your family and community from them, In a legal peaceful way. And no one stopping you from winning souls which brings people to our side. Brethren for life. 

There are so many things to do and be done before it ever comes to violence. Why in the world are we letting them talk us into it?

And on the same topic, You can hate a brother with cause. There are remedies for it, and if they ask for forgiveness sincerely you have to give it to them and you don't mention it ever again. And if they don't and they don't respond to your biblical outreach to them, You just don't have to have anything to do with them anymore. 

Of course, that's with cause. And after you've considered what you might have done differently. And being repentant for whatever it is you might have added to the situation.

teachings.title: The clearest presentation of the gospel in John 3
teachings.summary: Reads John 3 as the clearest gospel from Jesus: all are condemned by sin, and whosoever believes on the Son has everlasting life, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
**John 3***
14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
...
33 He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true.

34 For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.

35 The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
...

34 For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.

35 The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him*.

This is the clearest presentation of the Gospel of God, given by Jesus and note all the elements contained in it. That we are condemned by sin. But God so loved the world, that's everyone in it, that whosoever shall believe, that is trust and have faith in Christ Jesus, not our works or our genealogy or our ability to turn from sin, but faith alone, has eternal life and shall not perish. 

This is what we believe to be saved. 

If you don't accept any element of this or add something to it, you deny the record and aren't saved. You are perishing.

teachings.title: Eternal security and salvation by faith alone
teachings.summary: States that those who deny eternal security or salvation by faith alone are perishing, and offers John 6 and Romans 8 as the proof of the believer kept.
teachings.text:
If you don't believe in the eternal security of salvation, or that you're saved by faith alone and given the gift of eternal life through the grace of God, then you are perishing and you are going to go to hell.

John 6:39-40 
*And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may **have** **everlasting** **life**: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**Romans 8:38-39**
*For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.*

teachings.title: Online preaching is no substitute for the local church
teachings.summary: Warns against making a scene of online preaching one's identity and urges believers to be plugged into a local assembly, citing 1 Corinthians 3.
teachings.text:
And, I shouldn't have to say it but, online pastors and preaching, while it can be a blessing, is no substitute for being part of a local church and edifying it. 

Don't get caught up in being a fan or part of a scene, even if it is based on something positive like biblical preaching. Don't let your online cliques and subjective tastes in the content that you consume, become your identity. 

*For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; **are ye not carnal?** Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man? I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.*

Getting plugged in to a local assembly of believers and contributing, even if the pastor differs on some secondary and tertiary doctrines, is a blessing. It is doing the will of God. 

Consuming online preaching can help shore up your understanding, but it shouldn't ever become the only source for it. 

Online scenes are cringe. Your identity comes from Christ, not by consuming content.

teachings.title: Sanctification is not justification: works that bless others
teachings.summary: Distinguishes sanctification and discipleship from justification, noting that works God leads believers to are a blessing to others and that fruit inspectors who judge them are not walking in love.
teachings.text:
People who conflate sanctification and discipleship with justification, or take a calvanist view of discipleship, that says you *will* show works, almost always they mean personal works of self-improvement. That you clean up your life or you're not saved. 

And the ironic thing is that those saved by Christ alone, not of anything we've done in the flesh, and who walk in the spirit know that the works God brings us to aren't of ourselves. They're almost always a blessing for others. Most you don't even realize you've done and few people if any recognize it, beyond maybe the person you helped. It is in these acts that we come to grow in love, and the thorns of our heart that leads us to sin are removed. 

But that's a personal choice to choose separation and doesn't affect a person's salvation. 

Hypocritical fruit inspectors never gain that spirit of love from being blessings to others because they are always comparing themselves to others, to justify themselves before men and God. Being holier than thou makes you resent and look down on others. Not love them. 

And so, they aren't used of God, they aren't even saved. The good acts they do or the leaf they turned over are in vain. Filthy rags. And the thorns of their heart remain. Their later end is worse.

teachings.title: Repent: behave, or believe?
teachings.summary: Asks whether Jesus' call to repent in Matthew 4:17 means cleaning up one's act or believing that salvation is at hand, to fit the gospel of grace.
teachings.text:
Here's one. (Assuming you denounce works salvation, and believe it is by grace through faith alone, sealed unto redemption)

**Matthew 4:17**
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.*

Would Jesus be telling the Jews of the gospel of grace by say to them "**Behave**, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand," *or* "**Believe**, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand?" 

Which way of saying it fits the gospel? 

Would He be telling Jews to clean up their acts, or to believe they need salvation, and that that salvation, promised by God, was at hand?

teachings.title: Justified by the faith of Christ, not the works of the law
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that works of the law means only ceremonial law, using Galatians 2 and Romans 4, and sets Christ's once-for-all sacrifice in Hebrews 10 against Rome's daily sacrifice.
teachings.text:
**Galatians 2:16-21 **
K*nowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, **but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ**, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified*.

I just banned a pagan heretic from the chat, who insisted that works are needed for salvation. When presented with this emphatic passage from the epistle to the church at Galatia, he used the standard apologetics dodge that "works of the law" only pertains to Levitical ceremonial laws. 

This is false, as we see elsewhere (**Romans 4** for example), but even within this passage they always fail to address the other emphatically-made point, that man IS JUSTIFIED ***by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ***.

**Romans 4**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,

7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

This defines it clearly, that works of the law is a debt, not grace, and that it pertains to sin. And what is sin?

**1 John 3:4-6**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law. And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin. Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him.*

As we see in **1 Timothy 1:9**

*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers*...

It's simple. But those carried away by their own vain conceits cannot see it.

**Hebrews 10:9-13**
*Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. **By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.** And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: **But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, **sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.*

The apostate cult of Rome, with its priests daily offering meat and drink sacrifice to idols, that profane Christ by turning His sacrifice once and for all, and the ordinance to remember it by, into a cannibal cult, deny that Jesus Christ, being the substitutionary sacrifice, the propitiation for sin that was offered once and for all, paid it all.

teachings.title: Belief on the Son: what the record in John says it takes to be saved
teachings.summary: Strings together the believe passages of John and 1 John 5 to show that eternal life is given to those who believe on the Son, and that anyone who adds requirements to that belief brings another gospel.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. **He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. **And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

**John 1:6-8**
*There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. **The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.** He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.*

**John 1:11-13**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not. **But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name**: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.*

**John 2:11**
*This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; **and his disciples believed on him***.

**John 2:19-23**
*Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body. When therefore he was risen from the dead, **his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.** Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, **many believed in his name,** when they saw the miracles which he did.*

**John 3:12**
If *I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, **how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?***

**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: **That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.** For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish,** but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
**He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already,** because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**John 3:36**
***He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life:** and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

**John 4:39**-**42**
*And many of the Samaritans of that city **believed on him for the saying of the woman,** which testified, He told me all that ever I did.* *So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days. **And many more believed because of his own word;** And said unto the woman, **Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.***

**John 4:46-50**
*So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death. Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die. **Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him,** and he went his way.*

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, **He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life**, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**John 5:37-39**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you: **for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.** Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

**John 5:43-46**
I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me.
*
**John 6:28-29**
*Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? **Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.***

**John 6:35**-36
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: **he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst**. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.*

**John 6:39-40 **
*And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**John 6:68-70**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. **And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.** Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?*

**John 7:31-32**
***And many of the people believed on him,** and said, When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this man hath done? The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him.*

**John 7:38-40**
 *He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (**But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive**: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet*.

**John 7:45-50**
*Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have ye not brought him? The officers answered, Never man spake like this man. **Then answered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived? Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him? But this people who knoweth not the law are cursed.*** 

**John 8:23-25**
*And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world. I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: **for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins**. Then said they unto him, Who art thou? And Jesus saith unto them, Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning.*

**John 8:30-32**
*As he spake these words, many believed on him. Then said Jesus to those Jews **which believed on him,** If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And **ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free**.

***John 8:44-46***
Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not. Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?*

**John 9:35-38**
*Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God? He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him? And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee. And he said, **Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him*****.**

**John 10:25-27**
*Jesus answered them, **I told you, and ye believed not:** the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me. **But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep**, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me*.


**John 10:37-39**
*If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him. Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand

**John 10:42**
And many believed on him there.*

**John 11:14-16**
*Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. **And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe**; nevertheless let us go unto him. Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.*

**John 11:24-27**
*Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: **And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.***

**John 11:40**
*Jesus saith unto her, **Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?***

**John 11:41-43**
*Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, **that they may believe that thou hast sent me.** And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.*

**John 11:45**
*Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, **believed on him**.*

**John 12:10-12**
*But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;
Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus. On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem*

**John 12:36**
*While ye have light, **believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.** These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

**John 12:37-40**
*But though he had done so many miracles before them, **yet they believed not on him:** That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, **Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?** Therefore **they could not believe,** because that Esaias said again, **He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them**.*

**John 12:42-48**
*Nevertheless among the chief rulers also **many believed on him**; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.
