Jesus cried and said, **He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.** And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me**.***** *I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness. And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.***

**John 13:18-20 **
*I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me. Now I tell you before it come, that, **when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me**.*

**John 14:1**
*Let not your heart be troubled: ye** believe in God, believe also in me.***

**John 14:9-11**
*Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Show us the Father? Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works. **Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works' sake.***

**John 14:12**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.*

**John 14:29**
*And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe.*

**John 16:7-12**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.*

**John 16:27**
*For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, **and have believed** that I came out from God*.

**John 16:29-32**
*His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb. Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God. Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe? Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.*

**John 17:5-9**
*And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was. I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. **For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.***

**John 17:20-23**
***Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word**; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: **that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.** And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.*

**John 19:34-36**
*But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. **And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. **For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
*
**John 20:8**
*Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.*

**John 20:25-30**
*The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
Then saith he to Thomas, R**each hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed**. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book*

**John 20:31**
*But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.*

Let me post this again:

**But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
**
In case you aren't clear about what it takes to be saved. It isn't knowledge of the law, or adherence to the law. It isn't turning from sin, it isn't your willingness to turn from sin. It isn't that you were chosen to believe when others aren't. It wasn't because of who you are or where you were born or into what family or what genealogy you have or anything else about you. 

As the Gospel of John, which is the only book of the Bible specifically written to the unsaved that they may BELIEVE that the Lord Jesus is the Christ, and BY BELIEVING ye might have life in His name. 

That's the Gospel of God. That is the record of Him who sent Jesus, the Son of God, to die for our sins, and to be risen up again on the 3rd day, as the firstfruits of the promise. And by believing this, have eternal life. Sealed by the Spirit, become a child of God. 

**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: **for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

Anyone, I mean this, anyone who adds requirements to this belief on Christ Jesus for salvation, in any manner, isn't saved, and is bringing a false gospel. Let them be accursed. I say again, anyone who adds *anything* to this record given by God of eternal life in His Son, let them be accursed. It's another gospel. Let them be anathema.

Every damnable heresy that adds to this simple Gospel, that God so loved the world that he gave His only begotten Son, that Jesus is the Christ, that all who believe on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life, seeks to take the glory away from God, cheapen His grace and puts Christ to an open shame, because every damnable heresy seeks to make us the focus, to be special boys who deserve salvation in some way. 

Every single one. 

There are none righteous no not one. All of us deserve death and Hell for our sins. Even if you "turned from your sins," you are still a sinner. Even if you cleaned up your life. Even if you stopped smoking and drinking and fornicating. You still lie. You still know good and do it not. You still have foolish thoughts. You still war with the flesh. It is an impossible standard to put on people to tell them they have to turn from their sins to be saved. And it is unbiblical and a false gospel anyway. 

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.*

What the person who says you have to repent of your sins to be saved actually means is you have to be "as good as they are," or they will doubt your salvation. You have to live up to their standard, or it doesn't count. They are hypocrites. The worst hypocrites, *teaching for doctrines the commandments of men*. They preach against their pet sins and tell others they cannot come to Christ unless they follow these commandments of men. That believing on Christ isn't sufficient, and list vain and doubtful disputations as doctrines, their own inventions of righteousness, *and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.*

They are angry, bitter, they hold their knowledge of the truth in pride, if they have it at all. If they are saved, they preach Christ out of contention. They *give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith*. Turning aside to vain jangling. *Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.*

*This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.*

*For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.*

*Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself. For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's. For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living. But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God. So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God. Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way. I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

Let not then your good be evil spoken of.*

teachings.title: Repentance and the gospel: not "of your sins"
teachings.summary: Argues that adding "of your sins" to repent changes the gospel, and that biblical repentance is a change of heart toward believing God for salvation by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
Generally when the doctrine of repentance comes up, we think of false prophets like Ray Comfort, or John Macarthur, Lordshippers and others who add the teaching of works to justification by faith. 

These vipers are neo-Catholics who deny the glory of God revealed in our redemption, found only in His grace and by the blood of Christ, eternal life in His resurrection, reconciliation and forgiveness, adoption into the kingdom. Heirs to the promise.

They add works of the law to justification and keep people in perpetual doubt of if they are truly saved. It is a means of control and it denies the liberty found in the Lord Jesus. 

There are others, many well meaning believers, who have been raised with false Bible versions, or taught by honest pastors misled by Bible college or extrabiblical reading, into appending "...of your sins" to the word repent. 

This phrase never appears in scripture. 

And, in my experience, these people are straining at a rhetorical gnat and swallowing a camel, by trying to square their trust in salvation by grace through faith, with a vain tradition. They create a semantic trap for themselves, to the detriment of the Gospel. 

They will say that repent of sins actually just means acknowledging you're a sinner **which is** part of biblical repentance. If we can't acknowledge we're sinners in need of salvation, how in the world could we accept the free gift of it?

And God's not going to quibble with them over their misunderstanding of the term or use of it. 

Brothers shouldn't fight each other over pedantic semantics. 

However, the danger of being trapped in that snare of allowing the preaching of men to autocomplete a biblical phrase with something that doesn't appear in the text, comes when you're giving people the gospel. It's sows confusion, and here is how. 

Let's just say someone approaches you online or in real life and says that they are heartbroken. They feel worthless and trapped in sin. They have an addiction or are in a position where they can't break free. They know they are damned, know God is real and have a head knowledge that Jesus might be the answer they are seeking, because the Spirit is working in them. 

And they desperately need help. 

And one comes to them and says, that all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God, there are none righteous. That we're all sinners, deserving death and hell, the good news is Jesus paid that price for us and we only have to believe on Him and be saved. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That we may have peace with God through His son, with the eternal security that, even though we may sin in the flesh, we are sealed by the Spirit unto the day of redemption.

(This obviously is an abridged version of the Roman's road, where we show them from scripture all of these points because faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God, I am summarizing because I am writing to those who have accepted this all to be true and called upon the name of the Lord, Jesus Christ, that they may be healed.)

And say another says to them repent of your sins and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shall be saved. 

The first example is using scripture that is very specific of what you need to believe, to repent towards, that they may be saved. It is good news. They feel trapped and unworthy. They are told that, just as they are God will forgive them in Christ. That none are worthy but God so loved us that He gave His only begotten Son. Leading them to say "Lord, have mercy on me, a sinner," and believe that in Jesus name they are forgiven. 

Jesus said our mission statement as Christians is to preach this good news to every creature. 

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised*.

The second, even if they are well meaning and have the best of intentions to win these people to Christ, actually create more of a problem, because to the unsaved they only hear the first part and see it as the very obstacle they already told you they are struggling with. 

"I have to repent of my sins? What does that mean? Turn from my sins? Which ones? All of them? What if I can't? What if I relapse? What about things I didn't know were sins? Does it just mean willing to give up sin? I wish I could!"

It is bad news. We need Jesus because we are broken. Even the unregenerate man regrets their sin and dreads the looming punishment for it. How does telling them to turn from the sin they are trapped in in order to believe and be saved, save anyone? 

And even if you're saved by faith, if you give this as your gospel, You're going to have people who could have been saved, who desperately needed to hear the truth, discouraged and turned away. 

They may as well have gone to Ray Comfort for the gospel. Gene Kim. Some other reprobate. The Catholic Church. 

We don't get healed that we can come to Christ. We come to Christ so that we may be healed. 

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

I've done it before in past channels and it may have migrated its way to here, but I have literally gone over every single appearance of repentance in the Bible or any deviation thereof, and shown systematically what is being repented from and towards in each case.

This isn't some new doctrine found only in YouTube. This isn't some apostasy that came about in the last century. 

This is the gospel of God as it's taught in the Bible. 

While there may be secondary or tertiary doctrines that you don't like about certain preachers or pastors or soul winners or evangelists or any other saved Christian under the sun who's been saved by grace through faith, or if you've had personality conflicts or past experiences that traumatized you or any other thing other than biblical truth that leads you to doubt that repentance is a change of heart towards believing God that one might be saved in Christ, pray on it. That God may remove the thorns from your heart, so that you may be in better service to Hm and giving the gospel to others. 

Stop slandering people who have successfully and consistently given the gospel and gotten thousands of people saved.

teachings.title: The remnant of Israel and the false gospel of Zionists
teachings.summary: Uses 1 Kings 19:18 to show that in Old Testament days only a remnant of Israel was saved by grace through faith, answering the claim that all of fleshly Israel will be saved in Romans 11.
teachings.text:
**1 Kings 19:18**
*Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.*

The dispensationalist Zionists who claim to be Christian but offer a false gospel for Jews, and another for Gentiles, Make it out as if when Paul writes, *all of Israel shall be saved* that he's talking about Israel of the flesh. 

But as we see under the Old Testament, There were periods where of the millions of Israelites, there were as few as 7,000 people who had called upon the name of the Lord for salvation and were saved by grace through faith. 

The strait is the gate in narrow the way and few there are the find it.

teachings.title: The fruit of the vine and unleavened Passover
teachings.summary: Argues from the Gospels, Exodus 12 and Proverbs 21 that the cup at the Lord's Supper was unfermented juice of the vine, since leaven stands for sin.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 26:26-30**
*And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you,** I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.**

And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.*

**Luke 22:14-18**
*And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God. 

And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves: **For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine,** until the kingdom of God shall come.*

**Exodus 12:19**
*Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.*

Fermentation is prohibited during Passover and the feast that followed. It represents sin throughout the Gospel. The word leavened is the same for fermented. The process of yeasts breaking down sugars. 

**Proverbs 21:31-33**
*Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright. At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.*

Jesus knew no sin. 

Juice of the vine, new. Amen

teachings.title: Dogs and swine: the reprobate and what is holy
teachings.summary: Asks who the dogs and swine are in Matthew 7:6 and why holy things are not to be given to them, tying it to the reprobate doctrine with supporting passages.
teachings.text:
*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.*

**Deuteronomy 23**
*17 There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a **sodomite** of the sons of Israel.

18 Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore, or the price of **a dog**, into the house of the LORD thy God for any vow: for even both these are **abomination** unto the LORD thy God.*

**2 Peter 2:22 **
*But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

**Philippians 3:2 **
*Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.*

For those who don't affirm the Biblical reprobate doctrine and the curse of being a sodomite, choosing instead to think that reprobates can be saved;

What is a 'dog?' Who are the 'swine?' 

Why shouldn't we give to them what is Holy? 

What did God mean by this, including it in the scriptures?

**2 Chronicles 19:2**
*And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, **Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.***

teachings.title: Building on the Rock: the word of God as final authority
teachings.summary: Says that Biblical fundamentalism is building on the Rock, Christ and the inspired, preserved word, and that trusting tradition or newfound manuscripts is building on sand.
teachings.text:
If you don't build your house upon the rock, that is the word of God;  Inerrant. Preserved inspired perfect. And instead are trusting on traditions of men, with changing doctrine, . Newfound translations and scraps of manuscripts turning up in caves, and various religious leaders who list to and fro as the wind blows, clouds without water... If that's you, you're building your house upon the sand. 

*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

All Biblical fundamentalism is simply building upon the Rock, that is Christ and God's word. Both literally in scripture, and in the sense that it is His promise, which we trust by faith. 

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

That we have the whole word, inspired and preserved, that we have been promised so that we may live.

*But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

To be completely furnished to know everything, every doctrine, that we require to live a righteous life unto good works. 

*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

Those that reject these basic tenets of the faith do so by denying that all doctrine comes from scripture. That they reject the idea utterly. 

It's built on sand.

teachings.title: Sodom as an example: reprobation and giving the Gospel
teachings.summary: Uses Sodom as a set-forth example of where unregenerate men end up when given over, and urges that the aim is to give the Gospel to those not yet past saving so they are pulled from the fire.
teachings.text:
**Luke 10**
*10 But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,

11 Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

12 But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

13 Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.*

Again, the lesson of Sodom, *set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire,* serves to show us the extent of unregenerate man's state, once given over to reprobation, and acts as a parable, a byword, as the Bible calls it, to bring people to the kingdom by fear of God's wrath, even as we try to save them with the good news out of compassion, making a difference. 

Sodom is a warning of their fate to those who believe not the truth when it's given.

Jesus Christ Himself, despite all the natural man protests that He "didn't preach hate, only love and unity!" shows here He came to divide. And that those who rejected Him and the Gospel will be worse off than those in Sodom. That if gentile cities like Tyre had heard the Gospel accompanied by the apostles gone out, two by two, performing miracles in Jesus' name, they would have repented towards God, in sackcloth and ashes as the city of Nineveh once did, but these unrepentant Jews were so hardened they refused to believe.

It's not enough to understand reprobation and the bitter fruit it produces in sons of Belial, but to see that it is for the benefit of those seeking truth to gain a better understanding of God's wrath and help through the Spirit to convict them, and accept the Gospel. 

We as saved Christians know how wicked the sodomites are, and the proud filthy dreamers that defend them. But more importantly, we need to reach those who need the Gospel with the truth that God's wrath is real and is revealed to them that they have no excuse. That we may win souls. It is easy in our hate of the enemies of God during their celebration of the pride, declaring their sin, to overlook the number of people in our lives and community that are on the path to perdition, for whom it isn't "too late, reprobate!" Who need the gospel. 

Pulling them from the fire before they become fit to be burned like the reprobate.

My prayer is that we can focus as much or more on giving the Gospel and being a good judge to the fatherless, the number one group headed for reprobation, that they neither are given up or perish in death, but have life everlasting in Christ Jesus. Before it is too late for them.

teachings.title: Pride goes before destruction
teachings.summary: Walks through passages on pride and humility (Proverbs 6, James 4, Isaiah 2 and 3) to show that God hates pride, that a proud people who make room for the wicked are brought low, and that the righteous are kept through it.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Proverbs 16:18**
*Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.*

**Job 33:16-18**
 *Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction, That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.*

**Psalm 10:1-5**
*Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble? The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined. For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the Lord abhorreth. The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts. His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.
*
**Psalm 36:11**
*Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me.*

**Psalm 73:6**
*Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.*

**Proverbs 8:13**
*The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.*

The things God hates are the things we are called to hate, and pride is one of the things God hates most. It is why the sodomites use the term. They defy God by announcing their pride, against His judgments, glorying in the unnatural lusts that fuel their abominations. 

God promises His children that the proud will be destroyed, that we will be protected from their evil and violence, because God will have vengeance on them, He will repay.

**James 4:6**
*But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.*

**1 Samuel 2:3**
*Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.*

**Psalm 12:3**
*The Lord shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things*

**Psalm 40:4**
*Blessed is that man that maketh the Lord his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.*

**Psalm 119:21**
*Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments*

We are called to be humble. To know our place in things. To trust the judgment of God, and do our best to live by His precepts and honor His commandments. His commandments including not giving respect or honor to the proud, but to hate those cursed into their sin. Reprobates. Given up and given over to a reprobate mind. Rejected of God because His judgments are an offense to them in their pride. That they know better than God. 

**Romans 1:32**
*Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

**Romans 2:2**
*But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.*

**Proverbs 16:19**
*Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.*

The push over the past 25 years to normalize queers and to get conservatives to accept them in their "big tent" has worked because of the pride and arrogance of the conservative. Their rejecting of the judgment of God to be tickled by flattery and led away by their own lusts. They divide their spoil with the proud. They join in another man's sin. They yoke themselves to the wicked and become wicked. And in doing so they have been brought low. *For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?* God humbles the proud and brings to ruin men who join with the wicked. 

And those who call themselves by His name, when they are given over to pride, to standing against the judgment of God, they bring swift destruction to their nation.

**Isaiah 2:12**
*For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low*

There are so many verses and chapters and stories in the Bible showing how pride and giving room to the wicked, to sodomites and violence, leads to destruction of the people and their being humbled by the Lord. It is one of the major themes of the Bible. It is inescapable. 

**Isaiah 3**
*For, behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water.

2 The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient,

3 The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.

4 And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

5 And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.

6 When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand:

7 In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.

8 For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

9 The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.

10 Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

11 Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him.

12 As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.

13 The Lord standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people.

14 The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.

15 What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord God of hosts.

16 Moreover the Lord saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:

17 Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will discover their secret parts.

18 In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of their tinkling ornaments about their feet, and their cauls, and their round tires like the moon,

19 The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,

20 The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earrings,

21 The rings, and nose jewels,

22 The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins,

23 The glasses, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the vails.

24 And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty.

25 Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

26 And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground.*

Note the preaching of Isaiah against Judah and the cause of God's wrath and the curse of His judgement against them. That their pride led them there. *Their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of His glory.*..*They declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul!*

To the righteous, who keep their faith in God through this, it shall be well with them. *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.* We shouldn't worry or fear the fall that is coming to our nation for their wickedness and pride. For declaring their sin as Sodom. We will be saved from it, even as we are persecuted for our stedfast faith. 

But woe unto the wicked. They will be rewarded in the manner of their deeds, *receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*

teachings.title: Reprobation and the false gospel of repenting of sins
teachings.summary: Argues that denying the reprobate doctrine leaves Christians unable to explain or guard against open reprobates, and ties that denial to a works gospel that makes salvation depend on reforming oneself.
teachings.text:
The lack of understanding regarding reprobation, and the rejection by God of those who make the truth of God into a lie, is why modern Christians are ill-equiped to deal with the threat of sodomites.  (And I mean saved believers, not just apostates calling themselves Christian. Obviously the false churches can't resist the devil because they are of him)

If you don't believe that sodomites are that way because they have been given up, given over, cursed by God, abominations, conscience seared, never able to come to the knowledge of the truth, fit to be burned, plucked up by the roots, dogs and swine, hard hearted and proud, haters of God, sons of Beliel...then you can't explain who they are and how they behave, identify their threat and defend your family and communities from them. 

You will always be open to their creeping in unawares to lead people to damnation. You will always find excuses for them, because of your hope they may "repent." Ultimately, the denial of the reprobate doctrine is rooted in misplaced empathy and our fleshly nature being contrary to the judgment of God. It's the same impulse as the Pitbull Moms.

This is the evil fruit of the corrupt tree that is the false gospel of "Repent of your sins"-works salvation. The idea that anyone can be saved if they can "repent," or rather reform themselves, turn over a new leaf, clean up their act.

It brings people to believe that regardless of the nature of man, it isn't God's grace that saves but rather being worthy for that salvation. They see their own righteousness as their salvation, and see their own prideful judgment of others, and tolerance for the wicked as a good work. And so, if a sodomite "changes" because these self-righteous "Christians" got them to "repent," they must be super-duper saved. It is hypocrisy and the pride of the holier than thou. 

"Oh, you don't have compassion and love for these poor sinners, the homosexual? You're not a very good Christian! Don't you know we are told to "Judge not," hmm?" It's pride and foolishness.

teachings.title: Biblical parenting and the rod
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that parents should never spank by pointing to what scripture says: that chastening is a loving act, as the Father chastens His children.
teachings.text:
Had a disappointing reaction by a RW poster who seems well meaning, but was in error when he stated that parents should at no time spank their children and how he found it funny that many of his mutuals unfollowed or even blocked him. 

I replied with only scripture regarding what God's word tells us on the subject. He blocked me unanswered. 

Biblical parenting requires a willingness to spank your child when necessary. God (and the very nature of things, our own experience), tells us that it is a loving act, that even God as our Father does to correct us. 

**Proverbs 13:24**
*He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.*

**Hebrews 12:5-11**
*And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. 

Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live? For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness. Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.*

**Proverbs 23:13-14** 
*Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die. Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.*

**Proverbs 22:15 **
*Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.*

When we discipline, it must be with sound judgment and mercy, longsuffering and with grace as God gave us. But it must be a tool that we are willing to use, the Bible is clear. 

**Colossians 3:21**
*Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.

***Ephesians 6:4 **
*And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.*

Just as Christ is the head of all who love Him, the father is the head of the home. Wives should submit, children should obey, but we as men have an obligation too. We represent Jesus in the home, and if we are not using sound judgment, grace, and discernment when we exercise discipline, including the rod, we can turn out children to discouragement and wrath, where they resent God because of you. 

It is an awesome responsibility. 

And mothers, do not undercut the discipline your husband gives out spanking your children. 

**Proverbs 29:15**
*The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.*

When a mother undermines the father, she makes the lesson null and void, leaving the beating meaningless and the child twice worse off than before. And that child will bring you shame. 

**Proverbs 29:17** 
*Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.*

**Colossians 3:20** 
*Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.*

It is the first commandment with promise. 

**Ephesians 6:2-3**
*Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth*.

This is how a Biblical family functions. And the fruit of it is healthy, well adjusted kids and a loving marriage, and parents honored in their old age. God's word is to our benefit. Every time. And in all times. In season or out of season. 

**Proverbs 22:6 **
*Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.*

teachings.title: The church fathers and the canon of scripture
teachings.summary: Explains that the church fathers are not final authorities, that they often disagreed with each other and with scripture, and urges believers to read them for themselves and test everything by scripture.
teachings.text:
And to criticism that I "pick and choose when to use the 'church fathers,'" my point in linking this Twitter thread that demolishes the idea that the cannon of scripture that God gave us and preserved for all time, (sufficiently available to men in every age to bring them to righteousness, and testified as truth in the Spirit) isn't to say that the 'church fathers' are final authorities, but that if your entire theology is based on the traditions of men, you may want to actually know what they said, and acknowledge that they disagree with your modern understandings that you lean so heavily on. 

I don't need brother Polycarp to tell me what the Spirit does.

In short; believe the Gospel. Read scripture for doctrine. Find a good church that preaches the whole word of God and sings Psalms and hymns right with doctrine. 

And if you want to read early writings of first and second century Christians, by all means do so. Just don't rely on other men to tell you what they said, read them yourself. And with everything, search the scriptures to see if what they wrote is so. They were just men and are fallible, after all. But all knowledge and wisdom comes from God, through the Holy Spirit.

The modern internet theologian takes the route of trusting what they are told was the position of "church fathers," when the cited authors often disagreed with not only each other, but with scripture, or agreed with scripture but are contradicted by modern theologies. There is no discernment exercised. 

They place all "church fathers" on the same level, cherry pick what doctrines to take from them, often defend their doctrines by citing men who actually held opposing positions, and never compare spiritual things to spiritual things allowing the Bible to tell them what doctrine should be. Most of the time it's because they are themselves unsaved. And the natural man receiveth not the things of God. They are spiritually discerned.

teachings.title: Faith comes by hearing the Gospel, not by appeals to the world
teachings.summary: Responds to a worldly outreach campaign by showing that faith comes by hearing the word of God, and warns against being embarrassed by the Gospel or trying to win sinners by appeals to emotion or reason.
teachings.text:
I guess the #HeGetsUs campaign is the Hobby Lobby CEO's pet project, and at least going by his church's statement of faith, he believes in Biblical salvation. 

Maybe he sincerely believes that he can reach people about Jesus without actually using the Gospel. Seems like a fools errand. 

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*..

There's a certain embarrassment about that concept, and sharing the Gospel in general that many saved Christians have. They think they have to appeal to the sensual, the fleshly and worldly in order to get sinners to consider Jesus "at least as a great teacher with good things we should all listen to," rather than by the Spirit, using the word of God which has the power to save. 

It may come from a sincere person who doesn't quite get that faith isn't found in an appeal to logic, reason or emotion. It comes from hearing the word. 

It often comes from culturally imbued embarrassment, of wanting to be liked by others and seeing use of the Bible to give people the good news as being "preachy" and "judgey." Not wanting to "scare off people," but really it's just the vanity of wanting worldly people to respect them and their opinion, rather than sharing their faith. 

Some evangelicals believe they have to trick people into hearing about Jesus. That if they do flashy ad campaigns about Jesus the man, the viewers might absorb things about Jesus the Christ and Son of God, by osmosis. 

This is the same impulse that drives turning churches into a Panic at the Disco concert led by effeminate men in skinny jeans only preaching love, and not against sin or from scripture. Thinking if they use fog machines and lasers and uplifting pop music, and not preach hard against sin, they won't alienate people and maybe one might actually get saved. 

But we aren't saved by the flesh. 

*Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain.*

The Holy Spirit has a ministry to the unsaved. 

*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

For unregenerate man is called by the Spirit, led by the Spirit and convicted by the Spirit, and the word of God is spirit and life. 

*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

And so, looking through the materials of the #HeGetsUs campaign, that doesn't have a single appeal from scripture to salvation, it really looks more like a vain attempt to make Christians seem cool, rather than proclaim the truth that saved them. 

But, the Bible says we shouldn't be ashamed of the Gospel. It is the power of God. 

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.* 

And as we know, faith comes from hearing the word of God. 

*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?*

Don't be ashamed to give the gospel from scripture, unapologetically and unashamedly. It is in the word that God's power lay. Not in our anecdotes or testimonials. Not in appeals to the "red letters" on "how to live." But in the surety of the Spirit testifying within us, given by God through His word.

*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

teachings.title: What 'led captivity captive' means
teachings.summary: Shows from Judges 5 that leading captivity captive means taking one's captors captive, and applies it to Christ rising from three days in Hell with victory over death and Hell, not freeing captives from Hell.
teachings.text:
**Judges 5:12-13**
*Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam. Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the Lord made me have dominion over the mighty.*

**Psalm 68:12-19**
*Kings of armies did flee apace: and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though ye have lien among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold. When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon.

The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; an high hill as the hill of Bashan. Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever. The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place. 

Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the Lord God might dwell among them. Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.*

**Ephesians 4:4-10**
*There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men. (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth? He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)*

**Hebrews 2:14**
*Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;*

In case anyone was wondering what "led captivity captive" means, here is the Biblical concept, first defined in Judges 5, as Deborah and Barak sing a victory prayer after they had defeated Israel's oppressors and made those kings and their nations who had enslaved them their slaves. 

In a like manner, Jesus who was captive in Hell for 3 days and 3 nights, rose from the dead, bodily, led captivity captive, as He had victory and took power over death and Hell.

Misunderstanding what that phrase means has led many to believe false teachers who claim it means Jesus freed captives in Hell.

No. He freed mankind from the bonds of death and Hell. He took captive His captors.

teachings.title: Jesus died, went to Hell for our sins, and rose
teachings.summary: Sets out from John 8 and related passages that God is the God of the living, and that Christ died for our sins, went to Hell for three days and three nights, and rose with the keys of Hell and death.
teachings.text:
**John 8:51-59**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death. Then said the Jews unto him, Now we know that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my saying, he shall never taste of death. Art thou greater than our father Abraham, which is dead? and the prophets are dead: whom makest thou thyself? Jesus answered, If I honour myself, my honour is nothing: it is my Father that honoureth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God: Yet ye have not known him; but I know him: and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be a liar like unto you: but I know him, and keep his saying. Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.

Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.

Then took they up stones to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.*

**Matthew 22:31-32**
*But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.*

**Romans 5:6-11**
*For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die. But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.*

**Revelation 1:18**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*

**Hosea 13:14** 
*I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.*

**Hebrews 2:14-15**
*Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.*

Jesus died for our sins. 

God is the God of the living.

Jesus tasted death for all men. While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. 

Jesus was raised from the dead with the keys of Hell and death. That through death He might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil. 

Jesus died for our sins, went to Hell for our sins, and after 3 days and 3 nights, rose again from the dead in triumph. 

His soul was not left in Hell, neither did His flesh see corruption.

teachings.title: Passover and the timing of the crucifixion
teachings.summary: Lines up the Passover week with Christ's triumphal entry, betrayal, crucifixion and resurrection, and argues that letting the Bible set the timing gives three days and three nights rather than the Good Friday tradition.
teachings.text:
I'm not 100% positive, but if today is Passover then we are aligned with the same schedule of events as the Passover of Jesus' crucifixion. 

Saturday, His triumphant entry into Jerusalem, the 10th day of their month, Adar. Tuesday night, the last supper and betrayal by Judas and arrest in the garden of Gethsemane. Today, brought before the High Preists, the lamb without blemish. Slain before the assembled people. Taken down from the cross and buried by 6PM tonight. Eventime. Three days and nights in Hell, three Sabbaths in a row, Passover, the first day of unleavened bread, Saturday. Risen on the first day of the week, Sunday. 

Because our calendar isn't the same as the ancient Hebrews, and the lunar calendar and because they reckon days 6PM to 6PM, not at midnight as we do, it doesn't line up precisely each year.  

One interesting note is that in the Talmud, according to the wicked Maimonides, Jews may never celebrate a passover on a Wednesday. (The timing given in the OT by God through Moses sets a specific date, regardless of timing).

Modern Jews use the Catholic tradition of claiming the Last Supper was a passover seder on Maundy Thursday to throw doubt on the Gospels. That, and the Good Friday narrative make it that the supper wasn't on Passover, and that Jesus would have only been dead one full day, Saturday, and possibly 2 nights under that formula, gives Jews ammunition to argue Jesus didn't fulfill the scriptures. That it was not 3 days and 3 nights, using the Catholic doctrine. 

But of course it's their doctrine that's wrong, and when we allow the Bible to set the timing, we get to see just how the original passover and God's ordinance regarding it, and the other spring feasts, tie directly to Jesus. The foreshadowing of Christ. It is beautiful and perfect.

Another foolish argument comes from people who insist the modern calendar dates 33AD as having Jesus die on a Friday. Of course they are placing a man made calendar over the preserved and inspired word of God.

teachings.title: False gospels of works and salvation by faith, not identity
teachings.summary: Warns that churches teaching a gospel of works are doing Satan's work however much they get right, and reminds that we are saved by faith in Christ as individuals, not by ethnicity, denomination or party.
teachings.text:
I often hear ecumenical people make a big deal about accepting all churches who call themselves "Christian." That we are wrong to point out that these denominations of men that bring a false gospel of works are not only as wicked as the atheists and the Jews, but even more wicked for how they mislead people. 

They say these churches "at least get some of it right" and expose people to Christ and the scriptures, and many like the Lutherans, even pay lip service to salvation by faith alone. So, they say, what is the harm? That we should fellowship with them and save our ire for non-Christians. 

But ultimately, all that bring a false gospel of works, that salvation is either bought or kept by our labors, and not a free gift given by God's grace, paid in full by Jesus' sacrifice, are doing the work of Satan. 

And being of Satan, they will inevitably seek to convince those fooled by their false doctrines into accepting reprobates into their congregation. Setting wolves among the sheep. 

And ultimately, having damned souls with heresy and exposed the innocent to the wicked to be their prey, and making them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves, they will exalt the antichrist when he comes, that those trusting in these religious leaders and their institutions of men will be deceived. 

It is the entire point of the false church of the Whore of Babylon and her harlot daughters. 

If this offends you or makes you angry, consider why. What are you trusting in to save your soul? What God tells us, faith in Christ who died for us and is risen? 

Or following vain traditions of men and your own filthy rags of self-righteousness? 

Is it your identity as a member of a denomination? Or your understanding of being a sinner, deserving death and Hell, spared by the mercy of a loving God?

We aren't saved by our identity. By who we think we are. There are no 'special boys.'

We aren't saved by our genetics, by our ethnicity, by our denomination, by our political ideology, or by the party we belong to. We aren't saved because of anything we do, or deserve. 

We are saved by faith, despite all that. 

We all have individual souls, and are saved or damned based on our free will choice to believe or not. Individual soul liberty. You as a person must believe in your heart that God's word is true. It's not something you can "fake it till you make it." It isn't something you gain from osmosis, being around others who are saved. 

No one can share of their oil, you must prepare your lamp yourself. 

Now nation, family, and all other collective bonds, ordained by God, with roles and responsibilities, are something you can love, cherish and support. But not in place of Jesus and not above Jesus and certainly not as a means of receiving Jesus.

teachings.title: The law of God is perfect: its purpose, grace and judgment
teachings.summary: Argues from a string of passages that God's law is righteous and unchanged, that it shows us our sin as a schoolmaster, and that the old covenant, not the law, was done away in Christ. Closes by asking whether grace is a license to sin (Romans 6) and urging meditation on the law of God.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:*

**Romans 2:11-16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

**Romans 10:4-10**
*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

**Ezekiel 36:25-27**
*Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.*

**Psalm 119:165**
*Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.*

**1 John 5:3**
*For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.*

**1 Timothy 1:9**-**12**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,* For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with *mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

**John 16:7-11**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

**Galatians 3:16-25**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.

Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.

Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.*

**Romans 3:10-28**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. 

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.*

**2 Corinthians 3:5-17**
*Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God; Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth. For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious. Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: And not as Moses, which put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

**James 2:9-12**
*But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law. So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
*
**Psalm 19:7-8**
*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul;
The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;
The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart;
The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;*

**Romans 7:22**
*For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:*

**Romans 8:7**
*Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.*

**Romans 8:4**
*That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.*
 
**1 John 3:3**
*And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.*

Now this is a lot of scripture, and I struggled to pare down to only this, but it's to buttress the point, the argument I make; regarding the righteous nature of God and His law, grace and judgement, and especially His love towards us. 

Having established without controversy that God is love, that because He is love by necessity, He hates sin and the wicked who live by sin, because He is holy. Righteous in all His ways. That He is faithful to His promises and consistent in His judgments. That God is not a respecter of persons. That all who have sinned deserve death and Hell. But He is full of mercy and grace, so that God, because He so loved the world, gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believes on Him shall not perish but instead have everlasting life.

Knowing all this, then what purpose is the law? If all sin (and sin, the Bible says, is transgression of the law), and all have fallen short, deserving death, is God's law just? Is His judgment fair? 

This is an argument many make; "God made us imperfect and without knowing it we sin and damn ourselves. How is that fair? And what about those who never hear about Christ? They don't stand a chance. How is that fair?"

But the Bible tells us that the law of God is written in our hearts. That His wrath is revealed to us by creation itself. That we are without excuse. 

The Bible tells us that whether it was the Hebrews given the perfect law of God inscribed in stone, that they may know His will and the glorious covenant given them that if they kept the whole of the law they would be made righteous; or the heathen that had only the nature of God's law written in their conscience, and the revelation of His judgment by the natural law written upon all creation, all fall short. 

**Hebrews 8:6-7**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

But the fault of the old covenant wasn't in the law, which is perfect, but, the next verse says, the fault was with them. Thus the need for a better covenant;

*Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

So we see that the law wasn't done away with, but the old covenant. Not because God's law was unjust but because we are. That in His mercy He provided us a new covenant. A better testament. The Gospel of liberty in Christ.

And so the law serves His purpose to reveal to us the truth of our condition; that we are all sinners and in need of salvation. The law serves as a schoolmaster. 

And in these later days, the Holy Spirit has been sent to convict the world, that all may know they've sinned by His reproof. 

Because the New Testament isn't that the law no longer is in effect, but that those who understand they are deserving death repent towards God and believe on the Son that they may be forgiven. Redeemed by His blood, cleansed from sin and made righteous. That we will be judged not by our own works, but by Christ's and His righteousness imputed on us that we may be partakers of the promises made. We are condemned by the law but at liberty in Christ. 

God in His mercy extends His grace to all. 

And so, the law stands. Glorious and just. Unchanging. Perfect. And those who walk after the Spirit, the inward man quickened, we delight in His law. We love His judgments. 

But those perishing and those who may be saved by faith but living carnally, after the flesh. Feeding the old man; hate His judgments. They don't wish to consider His law. Because it convicts them afresh, daily.
The unsaved pricked in the heart by the Spirit, the saved chastened by the Father, who scourges His children. 

And so they say things like "that's Old Testament law. It doesn't count any more." Cope. Picking and choosing which of the 600 plus commandments given by God in the Old Testament are invalid based on their own rationalisation. Leaning on their own understanding. 

But it's hard to kick against the pricks.

But we know the immutability of God, that He tells us *I am the LORD, I change not.*

The Bible says; *For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.*

**Hebrews 6:17-18**
*Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed  it  by an oath:  That by two immutable things, in which  it was  impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us.*

**James 1:17**
*Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.*

**Hebrews 13:8** 
*Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.* Amen.

The perfection of God's law hasn't changed. The numerous commandments given that no man has fulfilled, other than the man Christ Jesus who in the flesh knew not sin. 

Be it the hundreds given through Moses, or the 10 originally written in stone, hewn by the hand of God Himself. Or the summation of the whole of the law in two commandments, given by Jesus. The judgment of God stands. 

Yes, the carnal ordinances, dietary laws, diverse washings and ceremonial sacrifices that served as a picture of Christ to come are done away with in Him. The sabbath and the holy days, finished in Jesus. But these were not the same as the commandments by which we come to know sin. 

The single law of Eden existed for the same purpose, that Adam and Eve having received paradise would know sin, and by free will choose to fall and lose everything, that they would be made righteous in faith in God's promise, given by God's grace, and thus glorifying God.

So, what then? If we understand the nature of God, the purpose of His law, the fallen state of man because of our inability to keep all of the law, even one command, the gift of salvation in Christ and the good news of our liberty from death and judgment, are we who believe free to sin? 

Is salvation a license to offend the immutable and perfect law of God? The Bible is clear;

**Romans 6**
*What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

2 God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?

3 Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

4 Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

5 For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:

6 Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

7 For he that is dead is freed from sin.

8 Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

9 Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

10 For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

11 Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

12 Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

13 Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

14 For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
