15 What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

16 Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

17 But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.

18 Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

19 I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.

20 For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

21 What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

22 But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Understanding this; that we are freed from the debt of sin, purchased by the blood of Christ, we become servants of righteousness. We are free from the burden of the law and no longer slaves to sin, if we walk after the new man. To this end we are called to His purpose. 

Our old man will sin. The lusts of the flesh still exist, even as our spiritual new man is at liberty. But we are encouraged to walk in the Spirit that we may better serve our purpose, which He has crafted us for. 

Yes we are at liberty due to the grace and mercy of God. But we must mortify our members, crucifying ourselves daily. Walking in the word. Feeding the new man. Separation. Sanctification. Love. 

And in doing so, glorifying God.

I don't know if I conveyed what I mean very well. The Bible gives us the nature of God, man, the law, salvation and the perfect judgment of God that stems from it all. That's my point. And from this we can draw the conclusion that His law is perfect. It stands today. It serves a purpose in the New Testament, as much as the Old. It existed before Moses. It will be what rules the Millennial Kingdom. It will be the books by which the dead are judged by before the White Throne. 

It is perfectly fair. It is holy. It is righteous. Despise not the law of God, but meditate on it day and night.

teachings.title: Grace cannot be earned
teachings.summary: Explains that grace is the unearned, unmerited gift of God, obtained by faith, and cannot be earned by any rite, action or sanctification.
teachings.text:
BTW the idea that you earn grace, obtain grace by some means of your own, or action, or rite, or through "sanctification" or anything else, shows a fundamental misunderstanding of what grace is.

Grace is the unearned, unmerited, undeserved gift given by God from His mercy and love. 

We don't deserve salvation but it is by the grace of God that we are saved. We obtain that grace by faith, the gift of eternal life. That unmerited, undeserved gift that we don't deserve, because we are sinners. That's what grace is. 
 
It's not a spiritual, magical "force" like Star Wars. It doesn't come in portions. You don't need reups and you cannot earn it. It is the favor of God to redeem you in Christ, despite you deserving death and Hell. It is an expression of His love towards us. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But **if it be of works**, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

teachings.title: Understanding Scripture by the Indwelling Spirit
teachings.summary: Reminds that the saved have the Holy Spirit to give understanding of His word, that no mediator or priest is needed except Jesus, and that the natural man cannot understand it.
teachings.text:
Reminder: the Bible says that if you be saved, that you have the Holy Spirit within you to guide you and give you wisdom and knowledge and understanding of His word. All knowledge comes from the Lord. We have no need for any mediator between God and man except Jesus. We are a holy priesthood. 

You do not need a third party. Intermediary to explain to you biblical doctrines. You do not need a priest, in fact, the New Testament explicitly speaks out against it. The pastor acts as a bishop, a shepherd to their flock. They can lead and guide but the Bible is the final authority. 

Cults tell you that you need a man to explain scripture to you. God doesn't hide His wisdom. There is no gnostic revelation. 

If you struggle understanding the Bible yourself, read it more and pray for wisdom. And if you're not saved by faith alone then you're a natural man and unable to understand it. Simple as.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 4: Righteous, Faithful and Just
teachings.summary: Shows that God is righteous, faithful and perfectly just, that mercy and grace are His gifts, and that His law is perfect, setting up a look at the law and judgment.
teachings.text:
**Zephaniah 3:5**
*The just LORD is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame.*

**2 Thessalonians 1:6-8**
*Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you; And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ:*

**Hebrews 6:10**
*For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.*

**Psalm 11:7**
*For the righteous LORD loveth righteousness; his countenance doth behold the upright.*

**Philippians 3:9**
*And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith.*

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

**Lamentations 2:22-23**
*It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.*

**2 Thessalonians 3:3**
*But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.*

**Deuteronomy 7:9**
*Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations.*

**Isaiah 61:8**
*For I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.*

**Psalm 145:17**
*The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.*

**Proverbs 2:8**
*He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.*

**Psalm 37:28**
*For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.*

**Proverbs 11:1**
*A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight*

**Numbers 23:19** 
*God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?*

**Deuteronomy 32:4**
*He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.*

God is love. God is holy. God is righteous in all His ways. Faithful. True. God is just. 

God, who knows all things and is ever present, who is without sin and in all His works correct, and who reliably and consistently is true, is perfectly just. Without iniquity the Bible says. 

God is perfectly fair in all things. 

God is not a respecter of persons. He shows no favor or bias. He sets covenants with man, offers of peace, callings to partake in His glory. These are made by His mercy and grace. 

Mercy being the withholding of what we deserve; Hell and death. Grace being given that which we don't deserve; Heaven and eternal life. 

And God's law, by which the whole earth is judged, is perfect and fair. 

God's law is glorious. Perfect in its righteousness. 

**Psalm 19:7-8**
*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.*

His law is fair. His balance is just. Because God is love. He is holy. He is righteous. He is exceedingly merciful and His grace abounds. He is longsuffering and patient. The Lord is faithful and true and not slack on His promises. And so His judgment is without error, without iniquity. 

And so, knowing this, we who are called to eternal life through Jesus Christ have faith with which to place our hope. On the Rock of salvation. On the promise of a God who cannot lie. Who extended His hand to us, in His mercy and freely offers this gift of redemption by His grace to the whole world. That all who believe shall not perish but have everlasting life. Amen.

And so, if God's promise to the faithful is sure, then so too His judgment of those who refuse to believe. And since His law is perfect, then those under the law who break it deserve death and Hell. The recompense for sin. 

Having established God's qualities that make Him just and His law perfect, then tomorrow, God willing, we will look at the law and the judgment of the Lord and why His statutes and commandments are still relevant and in effect in the New Testament, contrary to what some may say.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 3: God Is Holy
teachings.summary: Gathers verses on the holiness of God and shows that because He is love He hates sin and is separate from it, and that we are called to be holy as He is holy.
teachings.text:
**Exodus 15:11**
*Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?*

**1 Samuel 2:2 **
*There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.*

**Isaiah 57:15 **
*For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.*

**Leviticus 11:44**-**45**
*For I am the LORD your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. For I am the LORD that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.*

**Isaiah 6:3** 
*And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.*

**Revelation 4:8**
*And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.

***Leviticus 19:2***
Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy.
*
**1 Peter 1:16  **
*Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.*

**Psalm 103:1**
*Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.*

God, who is love, the very essence of love, who because He *is* love, hates our inequities, pride, lying and violence against the innocent, all the sin that we do or invent in our wicked heart. Because of this, God is holy. The Lord is separate from sin. Singular in His perfect ways. Where *we can* love, He *is* love. Where we are called *to be* holy, He *is* holy. 

The Lord God's name is Holy. Rejoice. The angels sing "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty!" Father, Son and Spirit. Each separate and righteous, all one God almighty. 

But holiness is not just righteousness, which is the works of holiness. Like hate of that which is evil is a part of love, righteousness is part of being holy. 

**Psalm 145:17**
*The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.*

Therefore we come to understand the glory of God. He is all powerful. All knowing. Ever-present. There is none like Him, for this He is set apart, and by His love establishes what is evil and wicked, good and true, and thus by His righteousness, He is holy. 

And, the Bible says because He is love, we should love. And because He hates evil, we should hate evil. And because he shows man mercy, we should show mercy. And because He gives to us His gift of salvation by His grace while we were yet sinners, we should show grace to those that sin against us. 

And in doing so, we be holy, for He is Holy.  

Separation from sin is in the acts of righteousness to which we have been called to by a holy God. To be a holy nation. A royal priesthood. To be an holy offering fully acceptable to the Lord our God. 

Bless His holy name.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 2: Hate Is Part of Love
teachings.summary: Shows from John 3:16, 1 John 4 and Romans 5:8 that God is love, and reasons that God's righteous hatred of evil is an expression of His love, so that love cannot exist without hating what God hates.
teachings.text:
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*..

**1 John 4***
7 Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.

8 He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

9 In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.

10 Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

11 Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.

12 No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

13 Hereby know we that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.

14 And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.

15 Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.

16 And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.

17 Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.

18 There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.

19 We love him, because he first loved us.

20 If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?

21 And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.*

**Romans 5:8 **
*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
*
**Ephesians 2**
*4 But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,

5 Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)

6 And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:

7 That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.*

**John 13:34**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.*

**1 Corinthians 13**
*4 Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

5 Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;

6 Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

7 Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

8 Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.

***Deuteronomy 7:13***
And he will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee: he will also bless the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy land, thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep, in the land which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee.
*
**1 John 3:16**
*Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.*

So, having shown yesterday that the Bible says God *hates*. That He hates and abhors and despises men and evil, that He judges and repays the wicked. That he seeks vengeance and recompense, especially for that which is an abomination to Him. 

But the Bible says God is love. In no uncertain terms He is love. God so loved the world He gave His only begotten Son, Who so loved us that He gave His life for us. While we were yet sinners, He died for us. No greater love is there, according to God's word.

So we must consider that there is no love without hating the things God hates. And if the righteous hatred of God is an expression of His love towards us; if judgment, hate and wrath along with charity, grace, longsuffering and mercy, are all part of God, and God is love, then is there contradiction? No, God is without contradiction, for He is holy, and God is love. 

And so, hate is a part of love. 

*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

This is the biblical definition of love. 

And if the love of God is like a light shining through us, His love magnified by us, then, by seeking His holiness, we will also shine the light of His love through what we hate. What we abhor. By hating the evil God hates, by hating His enemies just as we show love to our own. 

Because the hate of God is an expression of His love. It is a subcategory of the qualities of love. It isn't the opposite of love, it is a form of it. 

Our own hate can be misguided, it can be cruel. It can be wicked. It can be seen in envy and strife and unrighteous wrath. But God's is pure. 

Because God loves the world, because He loves His children, the sons and daughters adopted by faith in His grace, He hates that which is against us. His is a perfect hatred and He tells us in His word what the objects of His love *and hate* are. 

And the love of God is righteous, because our God is holy. 

Tomorrow, we will look at the holiness of God.

I'm laying the groundwork for a thesis over the next several days, so I would ask everyone bear with me, for in the end. God willing it'll make sense. I'm sort of working it out for myself to better explain it.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 1: God Hates and God Loves
teachings.summary: Collects verses showing that God loves the world yet hates sin, and explains that true love hates evil, loves enemies with mercy and pleases God rather than men.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 6**
*16 These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

17 A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

18 An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,

19 A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalm 45:7**
*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows
*
**Deuteronomy 16:22**
*Neither shalt thou set thee up any image; which the Lord thy God hateth.*

**Psalm 53:5**
*There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them*.

**Deuteronomy 12:31**
*Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.*

**Deuteronomy 25:16**
*For all that do such things, and all that do unrighteously, are an abomination unto the Lord thy God
*
**Revelation 2:6**
*But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.*


**Amos 5:15**
*Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish judgment in the gate: it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph*.

**Psalm 51:17**
*The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

**Psalm 139***
19 Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, ye bloody men.

20 For they speak against thee wickedly, and thine enemies take thy name in vain.

21 Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?

22 I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.*

**Romans 12:9**
*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

**Matthew 5:44**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you
*
**Proverbs 25**
*21 If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

22 For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.*

**Luke 6:27-38**
*But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you, bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you. And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also. Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again. And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise. For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them. And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same. And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again. But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven: give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.*

It is without contradiction that God loves the world, hates the sinners, despises abominations, expects us to hate those who hate Him, to hate evil in order to love that which is good, to love our neighbors and to show love and mercy to our own enemies, even if it is to spite them. 

This is a fully mature understanding of love that isn't self-directed feel goodism. 

Love is the magnification of the love God shows us in salvation, the love He showed in Christ Jesus. The sacrifice and seeking the profit of others above our own. To serve. And it cannot exist without hating those who hate Him and despising the things God despises. 

**Galatians 1:10**
*For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.*

**John 12:43**
*For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.*

**Colossians 3:23**
*And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men
*
This is God's promise;

**Proverbs 16:7 **
*When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.*

Those who say love is not judging bow down always to the pleasing of men who despise God and His judgment. They call good evil and evil good. They do the will of man not God, because they don't believe the promise that He will overcome our enemies. Man pleasers. Yet they do nothing to show true love, which is prudent judgment, and presenting the truth of God with mercy and grace. Hating evil, cleaving to that which is good.

teachings.title: Guilt, Backsliding and the Good News
teachings.summary: Speaks to those overwhelmed by guilt, pointing to the forgiveness and new life in Christ and the way back for the backslider, and encourages parents of a rebellious saved child to show love with correction.
teachings.text:
A lot of times people can get overwhelmed with feelings of guilt, hopelessness at their circumstance or the damage they've inflicted in other people's lives. The ramifications for their sin and the myriad implications that go along with making it right. 

Old feelings and patterns of behavior that developed in trauma and continue to create it. Things learned as shields to deflect the collateral damage of your sin and the return fire of those around you. 

It's hard to recover when you know you're a piece of s*it and can't see a way out that doesn't involve even greater sin. 

Stumbling blocks. Hardened hearts. Snares and temptations. Pride. Guilt. 

The good news of Jesus Christ is that once you accept that He died for your sins, all of that is gone. Your spirit, dead in sin, is quickened, made alive, born again in a twinkling, and the Spirit of God seals you unto the day of redemption. 

The Bible says your sins are as far from you as East is from West. That God the Father throws them behind His back. He remembers them no more. The peace found in Jesus Christ will fundamentally change you. 

And if you're already saved, but backsliding due to the cares of this world, simply turn back to God in Jesus name and be forgiven. 

There's work to do. We don't have time for you to be weak and lost.

Oh, this reminds me. If you're a Christian parent of a saved child who backslides or rebels, consider the Old Testament. Especially the failures of men twice as righteousness in the faith at their worst than you are at your best. 

Always let your sons and daughters know they are loved no matter what, even in chastisement. Even with the rod. Even with banishing them without the camp. That they always have a way back and know it, terms that are fair, and that it's offered in love. Don't spare the rod, but don't forget mercy and grace.

teachings.title: No Top-Down Denominations
teachings.summary: Shows that New Testament churches are local, independent and pastor-run, and that large institutions of men drift into apostasy; the only universal church comes at the millennium.
teachings.text:
There is no biblical basis for top down denominational structure of a church.

New Testament churches are local, independent, Jesus led, pastor run churches for the very reason that large institutions of men where power is consolidated, always will drift into apostasy and when it does it takes down huge swaths of people. 

An independent church might falter or pick up a strange doctrine, but the people within can leave and often just go across town to another independent Bible believing church.

The only universal church is the one that comes at the millennium. Here on earth there's no such thing. 

That's why God warns us in scripture against the whore and her harlot daughters. There is no based trad denomination out there.

teachings.title: Lent, Fasting and the Gospel of Grace
teachings.summary: Contrasts Lent with Biblical fasting, showing that fasting is private and never a way to earn or keep salvation.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 4:1-3**
*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.*


Lent is the spiritual equivalent of making a New Years Resolution, where you publicly vow to give up something that you probably should anyway and usually fail to keep at it for more than a few weeks. 

The biggest difference is the false expectation of God to give someone grace towards salvation (which He gives freely to those that believe on Jesus Christ) for not drinking as much booze as normal, or giving up chocolates or Twitter.  

And then there is the abstaining from meat, rather than simple fasting in a Biblical way.

**1 Timothy 4:4**
*For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving*

**Matthew 6:16-18 **
*Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.*

Fasting isn't a way to earn salvation and it certainly isn't a way to keep it. It isn't meant as a means to purchase forgiveness or indulgences. It is a spiritual act, which like prayer should be done in private, with the intent of bringing you closer to the Lord. And it isn't done by skipping a meal, dessert or having a veggie pizza and fish and chips instead of a burger.

teachings.title: Faith Upon Faith
teachings.summary: Explains that beyond saving faith there is the faith that hears what God's word says, believes it and obeys, so that faith grows from faith as one trusts what is clearly written.
teachings.text:
There are "other" faiths beyond saving faith. Faith that builds upon faith. For example, the faith to listen to what God's word says and believe it, and implement it in your life. 

When He says to do or not to do something whether it seems foolish to you or not, but there's clear scripture and so you have the faith to obey? You get so many rewards. 

The Bible says with daily reading the wisdom of God will be given to you, that includes things that help you quit sinning, avoid temptation, gain blessings, get opportunities to give the gospel and win people to Christ... You have to have the first faith to have the next faith, and so on, and that's how Faith grows in you; trusting in the Lord and what is clearly said in his word. Living faith to faith.

Every time one of the Old Testament figures puts their faith in something, it is based on something God said to them and their believing it. 

Make sure you don't believe on your own internal feelings about something or what seems right in your eyes, but things that God says in His word.

teachings.title: Making an Idol of the Translation, a Man or an Opinion
teachings.summary: Warns that elevating the KJV translation above the God who gave the word, or following a man or an opinion as an identity, is a form of idolatry.
teachings.text:
It struck me the other day when Ruckmanites were arguing that the KJV, which is the inspired and preserved whole word of God in English, providentially collected and translated at the dawn of English being the lingua franca of the world, and the printing press and universal literacy, was more than that, but itself to be seen as a separate inspiration, given to the translators. Implying the book itself was different and special and thus the preservation of the word to that point, wasn't. That God's word hasn't been preserved for all ages in the manner He saw fit and necessary to save those who would answer the call, but only in 1611 became perfect. 

This makes the translation itself an idol. It is worshiping the created more than the Creator who spake it into existence before all creation, and Whose Spirit overcame the prophets and apostles to reveal it. And the defense of the man or men who promote this idea to the point of infallibility is Idolatry.

All the "I am of Appolos," "I am of Paul," "I am of Catholicism," "I am of Luther," "Calvin," "Hyles," "MacArthur," "Ruckman," "Anderson"... whomever, not necessarily a reflection of the man, but the need by others to make the man or their ideas your identity, is a form of Idolatry too. 

We recognize this form of idol worship in politicians and political movements, ideologies, and it's easy to spot in sin, Mammon, coveting things, but we often fail to see it when talking about the things of God as if they were more than the creature God made for His purpose. 

The clay more than the potter. 

And so, rather than praising God that His word is there for us in our native tongue that we may be easily and thoroughly furnished to good works for Him, we can slip into holding up the carnal, the clay as an idol itself. 


**Colossians 3:5**
*Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry*

**Isaiah 44**

*9 They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.

10 Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?

11 Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; yet they shall fear, and they shall be ashamed together.

12 The smith with the tongs both worketh in the coals, and fashioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with the strength of his arms: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth: he drinketh no water, and is faint.

13 The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.

14 He heweth him down cedars, and taketh the cypress and the oak, which he strengtheneth for himself among the trees of the forest: he planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it.

15 Then shall it be for a man to burn: for he will take thereof, and warm himself; yea, he kindleth it, and baketh bread; yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it; he maketh it a graven image, and falleth down thereto.

16 He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied: yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire:

17 And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.

18 They have not known nor understood: for he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.

19 And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?

20 He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?*

Tangential to this morning's quick study on making things idols; don't make Space**™** an idol, or any other narrative and tradition of man. 

Also, don't make your opinions an idol that need to stand to keep your identity solid and avoid cognitive dissonance. This includes theories on how things are and speculation about what the truth might be. Flat or ball, for example. Fake and gay or real and straight. 

Having an opinion and having fun discussion of it with people who agree or disagree, but keeping that perspective isn't making it an idol.

 Turning it into your identity, is.

teachings.title: Italicized Words and the Preservation of the KJV
teachings.summary: Uses the italicized words of 1 John 2:23 and their witness in ancient manuscripts and early Bibles as an example of God's preservation, and argues that going back to the Greek cannot correct the KJV.
teachings.text:
Funner fact: The last ten words of 1 John 2:23 that are in italics in the KJV (which don't change doctrine but reaffirm the statement being made) were also found in in the Old Latin manuscripts, the Syriac, the Coptic, Armenian, Ethiopic and the Latin Vulgate, Martin Luther's German Bible 1545, the Spanish Sagradas Escrituras of 1569, the Italian Diodati of 1649, and the Cipriano de Valera of 1602. They are included in Wycliffe 1395, in the Greek texts of Beza, Scrivener and Elziever.

The italicized words can also be found in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Psi, C, 33, 614, 630, 1505, 1739 and many other majority text manuscripts, as well as being quoted by Origen, Athanasius, Cyril, Cyprian and Hilary.

God's word was spoken by Him before all creation and preserved by Him for all time, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. 

https://t.me/IFBKJV/3645
  
  Telegram
  
  IFB Independent Fundamental Baptists
  FUN FACT:
The last ten words of 1 John 2:23 in your King James Bible are italicized.

**🔥**5**😁**1

The point is that the italicized words appearing in the King James Bible, which is the preserved inspired word of God in English, is an example of God's *preservation* of that which He inspired, breathed. Spoke. Before the foundation of the world.

I am King James only is because it is the perfect and preserved word of God in English. My native tongue. What a blessing that is. 

But what is important is the content not the container. We should never lose sight of that.

The critical text reading intellectuals who insist that you have to go back to the Greek to get the true meaning of scripture, fetishizing the language or how old the manuscripts are are no different than the Hebrew roots fools who think they have to use yeshua as Jesus's name because it sounds exotic and different. 

If you're a native English speaker, you can find all the doctrine you need in the King James Bible. And there is no other name under heaven but Jesus by which we can be saved. 

So unless you're a native Greek speaker or native Hebrew speaker it's foolishness

But again the point is going back to the Greek can't correct the KJV but neither can the KJV correct the Greek for God's word has been preserved for all time. 

God's preserved word would be the same in Martian if such a thing were possible.

teachings.title: God's Word: Inspired, Preserved and the Living Word
teachings.summary: Shows that God's word has always been revealed and preserved regardless of language or format, warns against men who sow doubt about it and false gospels, and leads into Jesus as the Word of God in Revelation 19.
teachings.text:
*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

**1 Corinthians 2**

*But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.

Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man. For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.*

The Bible says God's word always was, has been revealed in all creation, written in our hearts, shown by the wrath of nature, spoken through inspiration by the prophets, given by inspiration to the same, recorded in different languages via different medium over the ages, preached in different tongues by the power of the Holy Ghost and by the God-given talents of pastors, evangelists and translators, perfect and complete, that no man may have an excuse. Good for doctrine and instruction on righteousness that a man may be thoroughly furnished. That is, completely equipped, to understand the will of God and the faith by which we can be saved. 

The sheep hear His voice. 

It isn't about how it is physically presented, what language it is in, the punctuation or capitalisation, idioms and vagaries of transliteration. The doctrines and spiritual intent remains pure, preserved by God for all time. It is His promise and His testimony. Oral or written in stone, parchment, book or on a screen. Said from a pulpit or at someone's door. Because it is written in our hearts, and given by the Holy Spirit who gives all knowledge and wisdom. 

People get caught up in the worldly details, distracted by pedantic, carnal things. But we are given wisdom by God through the Spirit, revealed in His word that we can live by. Perfect for all time. Preserved by His almighty providence. 

Amen.

This all is important as we move to **Revelation 19**, where we are told one of the names of Jesus is the Word of God. Capital W. 

It is important to understanding that the entire scripture is given as a testimony by God of His promise, fulfilled in Christ. It is that faith in those promises, believing the report of Christ and salvation, redemption in the blood, the resurrection and the kingdom, that grants us eternal life. Since Adam. Since man called upon the name of the Lord. Right through to the end. 

Jesus is the living Word of God made flesh. The Alpha and Omega. Who in the beginning was with God and is God. Slain before the foundation of the world.

If there is a supposed pastor who teaches another Gospel, multiple ways to salvation, then they are accursed. Calling them reprobate is in line with Biblical teaching. 

*As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

This is not accusing anyone who has differences on secondary doctrine or interpretation of more obscure text and prophecy, but literally those bringing a false witness to a false Gospel along with other heresies for the express purpose of leading men astray, creating apostates and worse, while calling themselves men of God. Just as Jesus gave us instruction regarding false teachers;

 *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.*

People get caught up in cults of men rather than spiritual things, and allowing God's word to instruct us, in the Spirit. 

God's word is inspired for all time. Preserved for all time. 

And men who make a living by making merchandise off of those who fall into their snares, by perverting God's word, for coming up with earthly theories about carnal things such as what language a translation is in or how linguistic transliteration may differ, semantics and nonsense, to make people doubt His word and its preservation, are wicked as Hell.

The Greek texts and the KJV agree. If your concordances and margin notes and footnotes show disagreement, it's because they are not the inspired and preserved word of God, not because the source or translation is corrupt. 

If you have to "go back to the Greek" to sell a doctrine to English speakers that you can't sell them on with the KJV, it isn't there.

And if you claim the English is not only different and superior, you agree with the critical text apostates who don't believe in God's preservation of His word, just coming at it from another angle. 

Perfect. 
Inspired.
Preserved.
True.

teachings.title: The Word of God Inspired and Preserved
teachings.summary: Strings together scripture to show that God inspired and preserved His words for all time, available in English in the King James Version.
teachings.text:
The word of God is inspired and preserved for all time. The same since before creation. Perfect. Complete. Preserved. 
God breathed. 
God preserved.

And it is available to us who speak and read English in the King James Version. 

*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.*

*God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.

 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.

As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever.
*
As for God, his way is perfect: The word of the LORD is tried: He is a buckler to all those that trust in him.

*He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.*

*It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by **every** word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.*

The same yesterday, today and forever. Amen. 

And all who say it hasn't been inspired and preserved for all time are calling God a liar.

*The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.*

Amen

teachings.title: Can a Christian Take the Mark of the Beast?
teachings.summary: Answers an interview claiming saved Christians could take the mark or be punished in the Millennium, showing from Matthew 24, Revelation 3, 13 and 14 and 1 Thessalonians 5 that the saved are sealed and cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
In comments, someone posted a video by Kent Hovind, a disgraced former pastor who has some clout still in truther circles for his defense of biblical creation vs evolution. Though much of the rest of his doctrine is a mess., His personal life has left him unqualified to be a pastor, and demonstrated questionable character, but the debates he engages in with atheists over evolution draw in new followers all the time. 

In this video that someone posted, Hovind gives time to a wicked heretic that I won't bother to name, who came to prominence in some evangelical circles nearly a decade ago, promoting a book based on the unbiblical idea that saved Christians could go to Hell during the Millennial Reign. 

Often mocked as "Baptist purgatory doctrine," its promotion exposed many popular very-online pastors as false prophets. 

Hovind begins by saying he "wonders what will happen if a Christian takes the mark" and starts the interview by saying to the viper who authored this heresy "I didn't want to believe it, but having read your book I can't say that it's wrong."

But the Bible can, and does. 

In **Matthew 24:24** says of the end times;

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. *

It's not possible because the saved have the seal of the Holy Spirit upon us, and He lives within us. 

The Bible says in Revelation chapter 13 that the false prophet, who will perform great wonders and deceive many to worship the beast and take the mark; *and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.*

Further, in chapter 14, the Bible says;

*And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

While in chapter 3 of Revelation, Christ promises the saved "*shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.*" 

Those who are saved, whose names are in the book of life CANNOT take the mark. Again, chapter 13;* all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life.*

But further, irrespective of the mark, could backslidden Christians not be taken in rapture after the tribulation, and be present both for God's wrath and punished with Hell for a thousand years? Again, no. 

**1 Thessalonians 5:9**
*For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ.*

We are saved by faith alone, not of works. If someone has believed, the Bible says, they shall not come into condemnation but have eternal life. This is the good news. This is the Gospel. 

This twisted damnable heresy hinges on the behavior of Christians, their works, to save them from Hell, even if it is for "only" the thousand years of the Millennial Reign. It's wicked as Hell, as the viper who promoted it and all the false teachers who gave it an airing will find out.

teachings.title: The Mark of the Beast and the Reprobate Mind
teachings.summary: Explains that taking the mark of the beast does not make a person reprobate; those who take it already were, as a free-will rejection of God and salvation.
teachings.text:
To clarify, taking the mark of the beast won't turn someone reprobate. It means they already were. The decision to worship the beast and take the mark might be the last straw that leads to God giving them up and giving them over to a reprobate mind, damning them. Just as with all reprobates it's a decision of the heart that does it. It's a free will choice to utterly reject God and salvation. The same as those who add to or take away from God's word to knowingly teach a false gospel or who blasphemed the Holy Ghost. It's not so much that the sin itself is unpardonable as it is an act that testifies to their reprobate mind. Their hardened heart. 

They aren't made reprobate because they took the mark, they take the mark because they are reprobate. 

Just as all who are saved who believe in their heart and confess with their mouth that Jesus is the Christ.

teachings.title: What It Means to Overcome
teachings.summary: Gathers the verses on overcoming the world and explains that to overcome, in this context, means to be saved by believing on the Lord Jesus Christ. Posted as preparation for Revelation 2 and 3.
teachings.text:
**John 16:33 **

*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. *

**1 John 5:4**

*For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.
*
**1 John 5:5**

*Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?
*
**Revelation 3:5**

*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
*
**John 5:24 **

*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life*

Synopsis on what it means to "overcome" biblically. Prep for the next two chapters of Revelation where it comes up a lot. TL:DR to overcome means to be saved in this context. To have believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who has overcome Hell and death. The first fruits, leading to the Harvest.

teachings.title: The Scarlet Thread
teachings.summary: Traces the scarlet thread from the hand of Zarah in Genesis 38 through Rahab in Joshua 2 and the genealogy of Matthew 1 as a picture of the blood of Christ.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 38:28**
 
*And it came to pass, when she travailed, that the one put out his hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.*



**Joshua 2:18**
 
*Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee.*

"The Bible also mentions scarlet thread or scarlet yarn as part of the tabernacle’s curtains (Exodus 26:1) and the high priest’s ephod (Exodus 28:6), along with threads of gold, blue, and purple. Scripture does not comment on the significance of those colors in the curtains or ephod, but some commentators surmise that the gold, blue, and purple foreshadow Christ’s glory, heavenly origin, and kingly position, while the scarlet thread represents Christ’s atoning work on the cross through the shedding of His blood."

**Matthew 1** genealogy from Abraham to Joseph, husband of Mary shows the scarlet thread running through the Bible from these instances. And* Judas begat **Phares** and Zara of Thamar; and **Phares** begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram..And Salmon begat Booz of **Rachab**; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse.*..on to Jesus.

The Jews today sell the scarlet thread that represents the blood of the lamb, the sprinkling on the doorpost of Passover, the thread of Rehab, on the judgment seat of the temple in sacrifice, pictures of the blood of Jesus and our salvation. They give it to Kabbalist shabbos goys, Gentiles who have fallen under their away. They sell it on the steps of the Roman wall where their temple was destroyed by God in 70AD, to unwitting Christian tourists in exchange for conning them out of shekels. Making what they claim to be a house of God into a place of merchandise. Blasphemy and corruption.

teachings.title: Does everyone sin?
teachings.summary: Answers from Romans 3:23 and 1 John 2:2 that all have sinned and need Christ as the sole propitiation, and that believers have eternal life that cannot be lost because they are sealed by the Holy Spirit. Quotes 1 John 1:9-10 and 2:1.
teachings.text:
"Does everyone sin?" 

The Bible says *for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God,* and so we need to be saved. We need Christ to be the sacrifice, the sole propitiation for our sin. *And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.* Past. Present. Future. We are forgiven in Christ. The Bible says if we believe, *We **have** eternal life. *Everlasting. That can never be lost or taken away, because by the holy Spirit of God we are *sealed unto the day of redemption.* 

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.*

Amen

teachings.title: Faith cometh by hearing, and rightly dividing the word
teachings.summary: Says critics of biblical fundamentalism take symbols literally while denying plain scripture, and explains that God's word is the means by which the Gospel converts souls however it is communicated. Notes that even believers can fall into traps when they fail to rightly divide the word, as over whether one must call on the Lord's name to be saved.
teachings.text:
I often find people like this who call biblical fundamentalism too literal, failed to understand the spiritual aspect of scripture and themselves take what is symbolic or a picture of other things and draw literal interpretations from them while denying clear scripture that means exactly what it says.

Most aren't saved. 

In this case, the Bible says that Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. The emphasis here is on the scriptures being used as the means of conveying the Gospel to the lost. The Bible has power. God's word is used to convert souls. How God's word is communicated to a person, most commonly audibly, is irrelevant to the fact that it is God's word that brings about faith in a person. Only a fool would take it to mean that the deaf can't get saved. It's just as foolish as saying the mute can't be saved because they can't call upon the name of the Lord. 

Some who are saved fall into similar spiritual traps by not being able to rightly divide the word of God. There's a rift in believers I know over whether you have to actual call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, rather than just believe in your heart. It becomes a semantic and autistic spiral of foolish assertions, and dividing the word of God takes a backseat to silly hypotheticals. 

Anyway, the so-called "doctor of divinity" in this tweet thread is an unsaved vipers teaching that you can save people with your own words, or actions, rather than God's word and Christ's actions. It's wicked and no wonder he makes such a stupid defense of it.

teachings.title: Chastened by the Lord
teachings.summary: Shares being gently but clearly chastised by the Lord over an incidental act, and quotes Hebrews 12:6-8 that the Lord chastens every son He receives.
teachings.text:
I was chastised by the Lord today for something that was an incidental act, that I didn't think anything of at the time, in a way that was mild but clear, bringing me into remembrance of it and realizing I was wrong. 

Amen. 

*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

It really was minor, and the chastisement was more embarrassing than anything else. But it was clear and great.

teachings.title: Romans 9:22-24, vessels of wrath and mercy
teachings.summary: Reads Romans 9:22-24 as one question about God's longsuffering with the vessels fitted to wrath so that the riches of His glory are known on the vessels of mercy. Says not all are Israel that are of Israel, and that God always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.
teachings.text:
**Romans 9:22-24 **

*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

All one question. What if the vessels fitted unto wrath, (Gentiles), He endured with longsuffering that He might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, even us (Jews)? 

They are not all Israel that are of Israel. 

God in His providence always intended to offer salvation to the whole world.

teachings.title: Chanting Christ is King is not being led to Christ
teachings.summary: Warns that chanting Christ is King while trusting in works to be saved leads to perdition, quoting Matthew 7:21-23 and Titus 1:10-11.
teachings.text:
Chanting "Christ is King" and trusting in their works to save them isn't being led to Christ. It's being led to perdition. 

*Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
...
For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

teachings.title: The living water
teachings.summary: Quotes John 4:13-14 and calls it the truest description of salvation Jesus gave: once born again and tasting the living water, nothing else satisfies but the Spirit as a well within.
teachings.text:
John 4:13-14

*Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.*

This is the truest description of salvation Jesus gave. Once you are born again, and taste of the living water, nothing else will do. Nothing else will quench your thirst, but the spring of living water, the Spirit as a well within, which satisfies completely. Amen

teachings.title: Satan was created, and the gap theory is false
teachings.summary: Quotes Ezekiel 28 and teaches that Satan is a created being, not a balance to God, and that the gap theory is a false doctrine since God called His finished creation very good. Traces Satan's fall, Hell prepared for the devil and his angels, and the plan of salvation in the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 28**

*12 Son of man, take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord God; Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.

13 Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.

14 Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire.

15 Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.

16 By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.

17 Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.

18 Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.

19 All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more.*

**Ephesians 6:12**
*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

**Isaiah 14**
*
12 How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

13 For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:

14 I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.*

Keeping in mind who Lucifer is, Satan. That old serpent. 

Knowing that the rulers of this world are given over to him. But it is important to note the Bible teaches that Satan is a created being. Satan was created by God. There was a day where Satan was created. The Heaven and the Earth was created in the 1st day so Satan was created in that first day. 

Some believe the devil is some sort of balance to God, or the Mormons say Jesus 'brother. These are blasphemous statements. Satan is a creature, Jesus the Creator. 

There is a false doctrine called the "Gap theory" that claims, among other things that Satan fell during creation week. That some time, millions of years in fact, passed between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2. And that in those millions of years a world was created, and fell, because of Satan and the 3rd of hosts that fell with him. 

It's a silly doctrine. We know that when God looks at His creation after His work was done, that He found it was "very good." Perfect. Complete. 

Not *very good* *other than the botched world and fallen angels. *

But Satan fell before Eve took of the apple. Iniquity was found in him, and many believe it was the love of man by God that did it. 

When Satan fell, and brought his murderous lie to Eve, casting doubt on God's word, he was attempting to place God in a difficult position with His beloved creation of man. 

We see in **Matthew 25:41** that Hell was created for Satan and the others who rebel with him. 

*Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.*

And knowing his ultimate fate at the judgment of the Lord, earned by his own inequities, he sought to bring down man with him. 

But God, having seen beginning to the end, knowing all things, being the exalted creator, already had a plan of salvation for fallen man. The lamb slain before the foundation of the world. Jesus Christ. And those who called upon the name of the Lord, gave He the power to became Sons of God, given eternal life. Heirs to an eternal kingdom. 

And His beloved mankind turned to a nation like unto the sand, or the stars. Filling up Heaven. Death defeated. Hell and Satan and all unbelieving, cast into the lake of fire, where the smoke of their torment rises forever. 

And Satan's ultimate defeat is known to him. And so, he goes before God, among the sons of God to accuse us, night and day. Like a ravenous lion seeking whom he may devour. Biting at the heel of Christ, who in turn crushes his head.

teachings.title: The natural man and the spirit of the parables
teachings.summary: Quotes Psalm 19:1-7 and teaches that Jesus' parables and figures, such as bread, flesh, blood and the gate, are spiritual and are misread by the natural man who takes them literally, like Nicodemus. Notes that this world will pass away and serves as a schoolmaster to bring us to the truth.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 19:1-7**
*The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun, Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.

His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof. The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.*

**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.*

It's important to understand that all of creation exists to teach us about God, and salvation in Jesus Christ. 

People misunderstand the nature of parables in the Bible. They think that when Jesus uses parables of things we are familiar with, be it sowing seeds and harvesting fruit, or the living water or the bread of life, shepherds and sheep... It is to use the familiar natural things to teach us the spiritual, and it's true. But they don't understand that nature IS this way specifically to serve as that example. That God made all of creation to serve as a living parable. 

Sound. Light. Food. Plants. Animals. Seasons. Marriage. Childbirth. Stars. Sun and moon. Literally everything in creation is there to teach us the ways of God.

The natural man receiveth not the things of God for they are spiritually discerned. 

When Jesus uses the parables He actually set up, from before creation, to be part of His word, they confound those unwilling to hear, unable to see. Hearts hardened, they take His meaning literally, as the thing itself rather than the spirit with which it's meant. 

*It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

And so when He speaks of bread, and eating His flesh, and drinking His blood, and the waters of Life and that he is the gate, that He is the shepherd, that man must be born again to enter the kingdom of Heaven, all of this is Spirit. It is parable. And the things He uses as examples exist so that they may serve that purpose. 

Those who take it literally, carnally, like Nicodemus, are incapable of understanding the spiritual application for all things. 

This world will pass away. Heaven and earth will be rolled up like a scroll. None of this will last and is incidental outside of serving as a school master to bring us to the truth of God.

teachings.title: Reprobate doctrine and the mark of the beast
teachings.summary: Says those who teach that all unsaved people are reprobate often take pleasure in the sins of Romans 1 and want to bring in supposedly repentant homosexuals. Adds that people who see that taking the mark damns a person should also see that someone can spiritually take it today.
teachings.text:
The people who teach the doctrine that all unsaved people are Reprobate, that is given up and given over by God to a natural lusts such as sodomy, almost always believe that because they have felt those unnatural lusts burning within them, or they take pleasure in those who do those things which are not convenient, women leaving the natural use of men, or men with men doing that which is unseemly. Knowing that those who do this are deserving of death, they still take pleasure in them. 

They talk incessantly about bringing in supposedly repentant homosexuals to the church. Those who are crept in unawares as the Bible warns.

I don't know how people can understand that anyone who takes the mark of the beast is damning themselves and is reprobate, but they don't believe in the actual reprobate doctrine. They don't believe that someone now, today, can spiritually choose to take the mark.

teachings.title: The self-righteous and the wedding garment
teachings.summary: Explains that self-righteous people think their good works make them better than others, when the only righteousness we have is His imputed righteousness. Compares the invitation to the wedding party, where those who come in their own filthy garments are cast out.
teachings.text:
The term self-righteous is literally a designation for the smug, prideful people, puffed up, thinking their good works make them better than others, when we are all condemned in sin. When the only righteousness we have is His imputed righteousness, washed in the blood. 

They are self-righteous and think they are better than everyone else and are going to be judged as they judge, and be shocked when they are found wanting.

We have been invited to the wedding party. The wine and meat are prepared. Fatted calf slaughtered. Everything is ready. He's provided us with wedding clothes. Invited both good and bad. 

And some will come not dressed for the wedding, clad in their own garments, which are filthy rags. And they will be cast out into outer darkness.

teachings.title: Do I hate Catholics?
teachings.summary: Says he hates the Roman Catholic organization and its false pagan doctrines but loves Catholics and wants them to repent and believe the Gospel, quoting Paul's desire for Israel in Romans 10:1-4.
teachings.text:
Someone in chat asked if I hate Catholics or just the Roman Catholic Church, and of course it is the organization and its false pagan doctrines that I hate. 

As for Catholics, I love them and would that they repent and believe the Gospel, that they be saved. My feelings are similar to Paul's for the unbelieving Jews of his day:

**Romans 10:1-4**

*Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.
For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.
For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.
For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

teachings.title: Perseverance of the saints is a works heresy
teachings.summary: Objects that the doctrine of perseverance of the saints says a backslider never was saved, which turns salvation into works. Says such teaching produces reprobates who despise God.
teachings.text:
For those asking why; "perseverance of the saints." When their gospel says if you backslidden, you never really were saved, a backwards, works-based "loose your salvation" heresy. 

They are those who believe in vain. Some come to the truth, and put all their faith entirely on Jesus. Most don't, and many become reprobate in the end, damned and with a seared conscience. It's a wicked doctrine of fools. And it has consequences beyond damning its adherents. 

Churches and denominations that create reprobates with works heresy, who despise God, having fallen short, don't wish to retain Him in their knowledge. Who worship the created more than the creator. They're like psychopath factories.

teachings.title: God promised to preserve His words
teachings.summary: Points to Psalm 12:6-7, where God promises to keep and preserve His pure words for ever, as the reason modern versions alter that passage.
teachings.text:
It is clear why modern perversions of the Bible change Psalm 12, where God promises to preserve His word for all time. 

*The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.*

teachings.title: Repent and believe: a walk through the verses on repentance
teachings.summary: Goes through the verses on repentance in the Gospels and Acts, noting beside each that it means to change mind and believe. Concludes that all of them say to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for remission of sins.
teachings.text:
**Mark 1: 14-15**
*Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

Change mind, believe

**Matthew 4:17**
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand*.
- Change mind, believe (same context as Mark)

**Matthew 9: 12-13**
*But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*
-All are sinners, being called to believe 

**Matthew 11: 20-21**
*Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.*

-They didn't believe even with the signs and miracles Jesus did. Even these notorious cities of the wicked would not only have believed, but done so with penance. In addition to believing. 
-Parallel verse Luke 10: 13


**Matthew 12: 41**
*The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.*

- As we've already seen in **Jonah 3:10**, this is physical salvation from God's wrath, which God repents of, *seeing their works *of turning from sin. 
- Parallel passage Luke 11: 32

**Matthew 21: 32**
*For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.*
-Change mind/believe

**Mark 2: 17**
*When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*
- Change mind/believe (righteous don't need to change their mind and believe, but all sinners do)
- Parallel passage **Luke 5: 32**

**Luke 13: 1-5**
- covered in earlier post - they believe some who had died from evil deserved it due to their being greater sinners than those asking Jesus. Holier than thous are just as damned as those men unless they repent/believe 

**Luke 16:27-31**
*Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.*
- Change mind/believe, talks about Lazarus testifying, of persuasion, hearing not the prophets

**Luke 24:46-47**
*And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.*
- Change mind/believe, which is how remission of sins is received (note two separate things being preached)

**Matthew 3: 1-3**
- parallel passage **Mark 1:14-15**

**Acts 20: 20-21**
