*And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house, Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.*
- Change of mind/believe, testimony 
- shows that faith towards=repentance towards 

**Acts:17:29-30**

*Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device.***
***And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent: *
- Change mind/believe, 
- literally changing mind of the ignorance which God had winked at, repent of afore described ignorance of believing in idols

**Acts 26:17-19**
*Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me. Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:*
- change mind/believe, turn to light from dark

Acts 2 deserves it's own post(I have made a post on it at least once)

There's more. They are all the same. 

Repent and believe on Jesus Christ for remission of sins, alone.

teachings.title: You cannot be saved by repenting of sin
teachings.summary: Argues from 1 John 3:4, Jonah 3:10 and Romans 3 that turning from sin is a work and so cannot save, and that biblical repentance is a change of mind toward God and belief. Adds that a saved person should still turn from sin out of love for God, which is not repenting of sin to be saved.
teachings.text:
Periodic reminder that you cannot be saved, you cannot be justified in the sight of God, you cannot receive the gift of eternal life, through "repenting of sin."

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4 - *Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.)*.

The Bible says turning from sin is a work. (Jonah 3:10 - *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.)
*
And we know the Bible says salvation is not of works, least any man should boast. That if sin is transgression of the law, and turning from wicked deeds a work, then adherence to the law is a work of the law, by which no one can be saved.  

This is made clear, in no uncertain terms, in Romans 3: 

*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
*
Note that Biblical repentance is defined as turning from one thing, towards another, be it God repenting of punishment He intended to inflict on a people, Jews repenting of not believing Jesus was the Christ, or repenting of trusting in their dead works or Gentiles repenting of their faith in idols, repentance is always a turning towards a different belief or intent. 

The phrase "repent of sin" doesn't appear in scripture, nor does any similar implied doctrine regarding salvation. What we see over and over is belief, faith, that saved. What is mentioned is turning towards God and belief in His word, and away from whatever contradicts that word that one might believe in, in order to be saved.  

So, based on this, anyone telling you that you must repent of sin, turning from transgression of the law, in order to be saved is preaching a false gospel of works, and cheapening the gift of salvation given by God, paid for by Jesus precious blood, and adding to that perfect and priceless gift our own righteousness, what Paul calls "dung."

We must believe we are sinners in need of salvation to be saved. We must accept that God in His mercy, in grace, gave His Son Jesus Christ to suffer and die for all our sins, and that He rose Him from the dead, to show the promise of eternal life. This is the faith by which we are saved. 

If you are trusting in your ability to turn over a new leaf, to be reformed from sin, even your subjective "willingness" to "repent of sin", or anything else that you might do in order to be saved, other than believe, you're perishing. 

Jesus did it all. Paid it all. While we were yet sinners, we are redeemed in the blood. Clothed in white raiment, the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ. 

Admitting you're a sinner isn't repentance, it's a humbling understanding that we cannot be holy or righteous on our own. The Bible says that the law is a schoolmaster to teach us this lesson. That God reveals it to us in our hearts, our conscience, so that no man has excuse. But this isn't repentance. 

The Bible says that having been saved, and free from the law, our sins erased and at liberty to do all things, even those that edify not, we still should turn from the sin that we did while perishing under the law. Should we continue in sin, God forbid. 

But this again isn't repenting of sin to be saved. It is turning from sin out of love for God.

teachings.title: Do not turn to the right hand or the left
teachings.summary: Uses Proverbs 4:27 to warn against the false either-or choices the devil offers, and points to steadfast faith in God alone as the true path.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 4:27**
 
“*Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil*.”

Don't get caught up in the false binary presented by the beast. Don't go looking at things through the lens of an either or dialectic. 

The devil offers us two choices, and is fine with you taking the greater of two evils, but is equally satisfied with taking the lesser. 

But the Bible says not to walk on the path of evil regardless of which "side" it presents itself as

The true third position is the path of righteousness and steadfast faith in God alone. It is what will save your nation, it is what will deliver you from the wicked. It is the promise and protection of God the Father through Christ the son, sealed by the Holy Spirit.

teachings.title: There is no liberty outside of Christ
teachings.summary: Says true liberty cannot be gained from politics or documents, and that promises of political liberty and exemption from tribulation are a lie bought by the covetous and fearful. Urges turning to the Lord and staying in His word, and notes that a believer threatened with death is being threatened with Heaven.
teachings.text:
I have said it before; There is no liberty outside of Christ. 

There is no liberty to be gained from politics or enshrined in documents or anything else of this world.

The false promises of politically guaranteed liberty, material prosperity and being entitled to exemption from tribulation is the lie sold by the devil himself, and bought by every covetous and fearful dummy. Selling their eternal and holy inheritance and losing their blessings that go along with it for corruptible things of the flesh. Esau selling it for a bowl of pottage.

People desperate for us to 'do something,' terrified of tyranny, confusing discomfort and hardship with true persecution, they hate the idea of doing the one thing we can, turn to the Lord. Stay in His word. They scoff. They talk sedition and rebellion instead, and flock to places where they are insulted and outraged, assaulted and maligned, consuming things created by people who hate them and God.

If you're looking to avoid tribulation and persecution by any means necessary, if you're that fearful and have so little faith, I frankly don't think you're saved. I would say you need to get right with Jesus, but I don't think some of you can in the state of terror you're in.

.

If you truly believed that when they threaten your life, they are threatening you with Heaven, you wouldn't be afraid.

teachings.title: Hail Mary and what grace really is
teachings.summary: Explains that grace is the unearned gift of God, so the idea that Mary was sinless would make her blessings a wage rather than a gift. Says misunderstanding grace leads to the false doctrines of the immaculate conception and perpetual virginity.
teachings.text:
Hail Mary, full of grace. Blessed are thou. 

Grace is the unearned gift, the blessing of God to those who do not deserve it. The idea that Mary was sinless would mean she was as holy as God, and not in need of His grace, as she'd be like unto Him. His blessings would instead be wage, rather than gift. 

The lack of understanding what grace is, being unsaved and perishing, not believing the gospel of reconciliation and grace and so not having been so blessed, being ignorant to His mercies, leaves those who speak blasphemies about Mary wide open to thinking grace is a quality of her's, rather than given of God. And thus the false doctrines of her being conceived immaculate, sinless, a perpetual virgin, who's flesh was not left to perish, etc ..

teachings.title: Talking with God as Father and friend
teachings.summary: Shares how he talks with God the Father and with Jesus all day, and that the fear of the Lord is reverent respect for His authority alongside closeness as a dear friend.
teachings.text:
DB VM starts with a very good point about how our relationship with God the Father should be. I have conversations with God all day, everyday. He and I joke, He points out things and I come to him with my problems, talk about the nature of things and His creation and what things must be like from His point of view, given the examples and parables He sprinkles throughout my day. And talking with Jesus, who's my brother and my Lord, who the Bible says is not ashamed to call me brother, because of the love He showed me, and the grace of God. 

Fear of the Lord is respect for his judgments and His position and authority over creation, and we should be reverent and respectful but He's also our closest and dearest friend. I love God more than my wife, my children, definitely myself and you should too because He loves you that much. 

Anyway I thought it was a really good point, so listen to my friends voice message

teachings.title: Do you believe the record?
teachings.summary: Quotes 1 John 5:10-14 and asks whether the reader believes God's record that eternal life is a gift in His Son alone. Says that to think it can be lost or earned is to call God a liar.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5**

*10 He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
*
11 *And this is the record, that* **God** **hath** **given** **to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son**.

*12 He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

13 These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.

14 And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us:*

Do you believe that record? That salvation is a gift, given by God or eternal life, everlasting, never to die or see Hell, in Jesus, alone. Can't be lost. Can't be earned by other means. Paid for by Christ. 

If you think it can be lost, or must be achieved or maintained by your own works, or that it's not knowable, that you can't have confidence in this gift, then you're calling God a liar.

teachings.title: Witnessing with a meek and blameless life
teachings.summary: Describes how to speak biblical standards from credibility, loving people, crediting God, being honest at work and praying for bosses and coworkers. Notes that people will respect you, ask about Christ, or persecute you, and all three are acceptable.
teachings.text:
I don't have enemies, per se. Normal people like me, toxic people, haters of God run from me. Because I try to love everyone I meet the way I would like to be, by them. Being understanding of their fears and being a rock among them, full of joy and thanksgiving. Being understanding that most people have problems and trauma and are afraid, all the time. Telling them why you are how you are. Crediting God. Glorifying Jesus. 

It pours hot coals on the heads of the enemies of God. They hate it. 

But if you establish your faith and morality in a credible way, not as a kook or needless scold, then you can say true things, upholding biblical standards from a position of credibility and emotional and spiritual maturity, so maybe some listen. 

They might not all agree, but they're going to either respect you, ask more about Christ, or persecute you, and all three are acceptable outcomes. Being blameless makes it easy too. 

Be honest at work, pray for coworkers and bosses. Even the douchy ones. Appreciate what they do, even if it's not up to your standards. Even if you have to correct them constantly. Even if you don't get the credit. 

Labor for God in all things. It pays dividends. It creates pleasant work environments. It emboldens others to speak of their faith. It sends reprobates spiralling.

I openly speak out against fornication, divorce, adultery,porn, sodomy, transvestites,castration and mutilation of children, the corruption of this world. No one laughs. No one really pushes back with more than a "yeah, but this is just how it is" or a halfhearted "we can't go back to the past." No one gets offended because I'm not being aggressive or fearful, but coming from a place of understanding that comes from following God's word. People generally react well to it. The law of God is written in their hearts. They still have a conscience, least they be reprobate.

They've been hardwired to be triggered by certain ideas by linking them with dangerous-seeming individuals. To be afraid when God or the Bible comes up. To be afraid because of those who have given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme. 

Be meek, honest and blameless.

teachings.title: God sees when we go quiet
teachings.summary: Compares a child who goes silent when up to something to a believer who stops praying. Encourages talking to God about sin and bad decisions, with an apology, because he still loves us as a parent loves a child.
teachings.text:
Having adult children, it gives you some perspective on how God feels, sometimes.

You notice that when your kids are up to something they know you wouldn't approve of, they go silent suddenly. The everyday or every other day conversations dry up for a few days.

That's how God sees it when we're not praying to him everyday. He sees right through it

Don't let sin in your life stop you from talking to God about it. Don't let bad decisions you've made go without at least an apology. He still loves you, just as a parent still loves their child. Don't let embarrassment keep you from Him

How many times have you ghosted your own parents who you love, ghosted them for a few days cuz you just don't want to hear it.

Everybody raise their hand

teachings.title: William Tyndale and the English Bible
teachings.summary: Recounts how Tyndale printed the first English New Testament in 1526, with more than 90 percent of it matching the later King James Version. Notes that the Roman Catholic Church had him strangled and burned and burned his first edition.
teachings.text:
William Tyndale translated and published, in 1526, the first-ever mechanically-printed New Testament in the English language. Tyndale’s translations (he produced multiple editions) were so fundamentally correct on doctrine, translation and beautifully translated to English that more than 90 percent of the King James Version that was published nearly 100 years later matched Tyndale's.

The Roman Catholic Church had him strangled and then burned at the stake for the heresies of translating the Bible into English and questioning the authority of the pope. 

In their effort to keep the truth of the true Gospel from the people (and to suppress the anger at the corruption, sexual degeneracy and drunkenness of the English RCC officials) the English Catholic church bought, seized and burned all the copies of Tyndale's first edition.

teachings.title: The Mandela Effect and the wolf and the lamb
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that the Bible was changed from lion to wolf in Isaiah by asking what other animals the passage names. Argues that the preserved word of God can be trusted and that it is more likely outside sources have the wrong memory.
teachings.text:
A few minutes ago, a fren in chat asked me "Name the animal that lay with the lamb in Isaiah," to which I replied the wolf, to his satisfaction. 

But the context of the question lay in the supposed Mandela Effect, which postulates that our reality is malleable, and subject to change, an effect many of us have experienced, sometimes possible faulty cultural memories, other times a creepy certainty that something has absolutely changed, and couldn't possibly be what is now asserted as truth. I am not skeptical of the ME. Some have hit me hard, and lack explanation other than CERN or some other satanic source, rewriting things.

But has the ME struck even the Bible? Is the collective memory of the lion laying down with the lamb overwhelming evidence that it's been changed to "wolf?" 

Is our faith in the inspired and preserved word of God, written before the foundation of the world, containing the ultimate truth misplaced? If this one phrase has changed it would undermine everything Christianity is based on. 

By chance, not long after, I happened to see a post by Vox Day on his blog maintaining that it was always lion and lamb, and citing a couple literary examples with the argument "these guys can't be wrong, they are well read and wouldn't err," basically. 

Which begs the question. 

If ME is real, and we can stipulate that for sake of discussion, wouldn't it be just as likely that the proofs offered of the change, extra-biblcal writings, poetry, stained glass artwork and the like, isn't it just as likely that that's what has changed? 

If God preserved His word, and it was divinely inspired and kept over the millennia, maybe, just maybe it's the secular things that got it wrong. 

Here's a key question to ask those who maintain the Bible is what changed: Name the other animals mentioned in the passage. 

Vox's post concedes that most people don't even know what book the phrase comes from. Because most people don't know anything about the Bible. 

Most saved Christians don't read it cover to cover in their life time. Let alone the natural man that receiveth not the things of God.

Just think about all the false doctrine that is out there, that people swallow Hook line and sinker because they don't know the scriptures in order to compare spiritual with spiritual and prove all things. 

And so, if you were to ask them what other animals are mentioned in the passage,most who insist that it's always been lion with lamb will stare blankly at you. 

Ask yourself. No cheating. Do you know the verses that talk about lambs lying down with predators? Do you know what other animals are mentioned?

Isaiah 11:6-9

6 The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

7 And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

8 And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice' den.

9 They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.

teachings.title: What scripture says about Mary
teachings.summary: States that Mary died a natural death and entered Heaven by faith through grace, the same way as all saved believers. Says every other teaching about Mary is extra-biblical and that a church celebrating it is apostate.
teachings.text:
Mary's body died a natural death and was buried. Her spirit, quickened by being born again in faith through grace allowed her, a sinner, to enter into Heaven the same exact way all saved believers do. 

Every other extra-biblcal heresy regarding Mary is based on grifters and conmen, centuries after her death making up tales. 

Any church that celebrates this heresy is apostate.

teachings.title: The rosary and Mary worship
teachings.summary: Calls the rosary vain repetition and idolatry, noting that its prayers are mostly to Mary and that this is what Jesus and scripture forbid. Says believers who call themselves by the Lord's name yet worship false gods bring a curse on the land.
teachings.text:
This heathen idolatry, vain repetitions and "Mary"-worshiping is as large a reason we are under God's wrath as any pride parade

In case there's any doubt of this blasphemous heresy, note it's origins and the progression of prayers is almost entirely about "Mary"-worshiping. Ten prayers to Mary are said for every one to God the Father. The entire thing was given by a demon appearing in Mary's name. 

It violates scripture, with vain repetitions as the heathen do, thinking they will be heard by much speaking. It idolizes the graven cross and beads as the focus of worship, it is done publicly, with boasting of how devoted its practitioners are to it, as they kneel before idols of "Mary." It is everything Jesus told us not to do, and that scripture forbids. 

The rosery is wicked as Hell

"How many cake-bakers for the Queen of Heaven shot up Jerusalem over the weekend?" 

Again, by calling themselves by the Lord's name and worshiping false gods and idols, they cause the living, jealous God to curse our land and people. So, as they persist they are to blame for much of the tribulation we have in this country.

teachings.title: The day of the Lord is darkness to the damned
teachings.summary: Quotes Amos 5:18 to show that the day of the Lord is darkness and not light for those who desire it without God. Says believers are of the day and the light, and that day and night are a picture of this, a parable of creation.
teachings.text:
In this regard, to the Jews orchestrating the end times, 

**Amos 5:18**

*Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.*

What ends do the damned have on the day of the Lord? They get darkness. Sun and moon and stars. 

We are of the day and of the light.

In fact one of the reasons God created day and night, if not the only reason, perhaps. It's a picture of this very thing at the end. That we understand the night and the day, the darkness and the light.

So we have that understanding when we hear God's word say it, we can picture it, and in picturing it understand what God's saying. The parable of creation

teachings.title: Primary doctrines before prophecy
teachings.summary: Notes people who spend years decoding end times prophecy from the works of men yet do not understand the basic gospel. Says much of prophecy, especially the timing, is fairly easy to understand once first things and secondary doctrines are in place.
teachings.text:
There are people who spend years researching and debating end times Bible prophecy, going through works of men to try and decode the order of things, and yet have no understanding of the basic Gospel of salvation, or any of the primary doctrines of God. 

I have run in to such people repeatedly for decades. They can't accept the truth and insist there are secrets to learn and mysteries to unravel that cannot be answered in scripture, but could be by some obscure work.

While there are some things unclear, seen through a glass darkly, much of it is fairly easy to understand, the timing of things most of all. In the spirit and understanding of first things and secondary doctrines reveal a lot of it. Especially being able to clear up misconception and false teaching and wild theories.

teachings.title: Whosoever believeth: the record of John 3
teachings.summary: Takes John 3:14-18 to show that whosoever believes has everlasting life, meaning never to be lost. Says there is no other means of salvation and that unbelief of this record leaves a person condemned.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**

*14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God*.

If you don't believe that God so loved *the world* that *whosoever, *(that means anyone, anywhere),*  believes *(the only condition required) *will not perish *and *has eternal, everlasting life* (*has*, meaning is then in possession of, *eternal* & *everlasting*, meaning never to be lost because it is forever), then you don't believe the Gospel, and so you are *condemned*. 

There is no other means of salvation. This is the record. 

If this offends you, or you wish to add or take away something to this, you are perishing. Repent and turn towards God.

teachings.title: Doctrines that confine God to time
teachings.summary: Sets John 3, Luke 23:43 and Revelation 13:8 beside the false teaching that confines God to human time. Says the idea that Jesus could not have gone to Hell from the cross, or that Old Testament saints waited in a place in Hell, comes from misunderstanding the spiritual, and that paradise is a synonym for Heaven.
teachings.text:
**John 3
***
11 Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.

12 If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?

13 **And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.**

14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

**Luke 23**
*
39 And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

40 But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

41 And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

42 And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

43 And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, **Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.***

**Revelation 13**

*8 And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of **the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.***

There are many false doctrines of men that constrain God to the human experience of time and space. 

One is the foolish idea that Jesus couldn't have gone to Hell from the cross, while being in Heaven that day to great him. Another is that before the cross, as we reckon time, Old Testament saints were placed in a waiting room in Hell, alternatively called "Abraham's bosom" or "paradise," a word that doesn't appear in the OT, is only mentioned 3 times in the NT, and the only indication of location is "up." (See tomorrow's reading of 2 Corinthians 12). It is just a synonym for Heaven. But all these false doctrines spin out of basic misunderstanding of the nature of the spiritual by those trapped in corruption of the flesh.

teachings.title: Conscience and testing the doctrines of men
teachings.summary: Says the conscience is the law written in the heart and a sign that we need salvation, and that the seared conscience of reprobates is silent. Gives a way to test doctrines of men by comparing them to known scripture, and asks that disagreements over secondary doctrine stay civil.
teachings.text:
I think the idea of angels on your shoulder came from the way people move their eyes when asked a question. People with a conscience, anyway. 

A conscience is the law written in our heart, and something the Bible says is a way God reveals Himself to us. A physical manifestation of our knowing we need salvation for our sin, written on the face of a person trapped in it. That tinge of the heart telling us that Satan is already accusing us of whatever it is, before God, right at that moment. It hits even harder when you're saved and should know better. New man and the Spirit taking over the role the angel of conscience had, and God's rod of correction replacing the devil.

Psychopath reprobates don't have that problem, their conscience seared as scripture says, and so they can lie with a straight face and no guilt. All they have is the devil whispering in their ear.

If you want to understand the things of God, learn His word and then consider the implications of each doctrine, and the patterns that each creates with the others. Just morality and the need for the law to prove to us we need saving, and how it provides the criteria for accepting the testimony of God, regarding Christ, by which we are saved for believing, and then ponder how that has played out in the Biblical history and in your own life...it's awesome

By the way that's a good way to test the doctrines of men. Knowing the scriptures and what they teach, does this doctrine being presented contradict in a plausible way the doctrines you know are true, having tested them to scripture, spiritual with spiritual. 

If it doesn't conflict with clear scripture and established true doctrines, spend time considering it in light of the Bible.

If it does, now it has to explain itself before you go any further on it. The person offering it has to cite scripture supporting it and how it squares with the doctrines of Christ before you should invest anymore time. IMO.

It's ok to disagree on ancillary doctrines, too. But people make it a internet debate and act stupid

teachings.title: Living as the new man so people will listen
teachings.summary: Draws on Paul's second letter to the Corinthians to say that people are drawn to Christ by a believer who lives in the new man with joy, honesty and humility. Describes trying to live in a way approved by God and open to the scrutiny of men, so that others become open to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Just as Paul is writing to the Corinthians in his second epistle to them; if you want to attract people to your cause, in this case, Christ and the ministry of redemption (which should be our primary goal), you have to live in the new man, in joy and confidence, changed by your faith and humble and loving in how you approach people, reflecting the light of the Spirit that's within you. 

The same goes for defending your nation. You can be against something, but it has to be in relation to what you are *for,* and coupled with a living example of why everyone should also be for it.

To this last point, I try, emphasis on try, with the help of the Holy Spirit and staying in God's word, to live in a way that can be approved by God, and can be scrutinized by the conscience of men. (See the study on 2 Corinthians that's ongoing here)

Because I do, however imperfectly, people trust me. They ask me why I am so positive. They know my word is good. My yea means yea. They see me handle tribulation with peace and without fear. They see my charity in caring about them. They see me handle success with humility and meekness, giving glory to God. And to some, it wins them to being at least open to hearing the Gospel. (It repels toxic people, like garlic to a vampire).

I try to live my WN the same way. Unashamed, honest, pro-my family, community and people. So that when I speak against the things being done to us, people listen. When I name who it is doing it and why, they don't freak out, but consider it.

teachings.title: Restoring the joy of salvation
teachings.summary: Uses Psalm 51 to encourage believers who are overcome by the world, worry and fear. Says it is fixed by turning back to God in faith and prayer, and like David singing praises and sharing the good news.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51
**
*12 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

13 Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

14 Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

There's many our guys who are believers, living right, and still overcome by the world. Relationships with family,  being vexed by the wicked conversations of the world, work and money, inability to find a girlfriend, let alone find and keep a wife, caught up with fear and constant worry, often for good reason and rationally so, but for the joy of Jesus and the knowledge that He's overcome all, and we through Him have as well. But sometimes that fades, and the world and the old man creep in. 

But it is fixed by turning towards God, in that first faith and prayer to build upon it. 

And like David, sing praises unto the Lord and share with others the good news that's healed you, so it may others. Amen

teachings.title: Saved Christians forget they were sinners
teachings.summary: Observes that many Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after salvation. Says most believers go through backsliding and that real maturity admits sin and shows grace to others.
teachings.text:
I think a lot of Christians, especially online (but even before there was an internet believe me), but a lot of Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after they've been saved. The average span of zealous devotion in the faith is something like 3 years. It generally takes the old man about 3 years to push his way back after one receives the new man.

Some people remain cast away for the rest of their natural life, even though they have that eternal reward waiting. Many eventually mature and come to understand the awesomeness of the gift they've been given. But most go through some form of backsliding, or falling away. 

The cares of the world come for us all in different ways through different means, and the devil is like a ravenous lion seeking whom he can devour. 

But, most Christians will portray themselves as having always been perfect in their ways. They may admit to a sinful past as part of a testimony to how much they've changed, but it's rare they'll admit their own sins. It takes a kind of maturity in Christ and in faith to be able to. 

I mean, when you ask them they'll all admit of course I'm a sinner, but few really mean it because we all want to look good. But you can tell when someone has had a sincere repentance from whatever had taken them away from their love of the Gospel.

teachings.title: Patience with God and the saints under the altar
teachings.summary: Uses the martyrs crying out under the altar in Revelation 6 to answer those who want action now. Says believers should trust God's timing and vengeance, be thankful they are not yet suffering real persecution, and be patient.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 6**

*9 And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held:

10 And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?

11 And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.*

There are many Our Guys, who, frustrated by the world, provoked and angry at the state of things and the direction we are headed in, who express impatience with those of us who profess Christ. That we should *do something!* That it's not enough to turn to God and pray for our people and live a Godly life, trusting in Him. That vengence is His. 

They complain that God is too long suffering for them. "When oh Lord?!" they cry out. 

They turn to false hope in politics. In red pilling enough people. In telling coworkers about the Holohoax when we are borrowing tools. In supporting movements, listening to podcasts, buying merch, being paypigs. Some even advocating violence and riot. They cannot put their trust in the long-suffering God who has promised them His wrath on the workers of iniquity, and eternal destruction in an unquenchable fire. 

And then you look at these saints, the dead in Christ who were slain for the word, and who plead with God to pour out His wrath on the wicked, and who are told to rest a while more as the season comes full, and they do. 

The suffering of those far out strips anything that we have to complain about. These are people beaten imprisoned and beheaded, stoned shot and killed in the name of Jesus Christ. People who lost all their loved ones, who were dispossessed of all their earthly belongings, who suffered and were scourged and died. And as they cried out for the Lord to take vengeance, they still waited patiently for His perfect timing.

Comparatively we have it easy. In relation to them we haven't suffered it all. The petty things that afflict us are nothing compared to the protection and blessings that the Lord has provided most of us in our lives. 

We should learn to be a bit more patient with God. Real persecution will come. Great Tribulation is at hand. But in the meantime we should be thankful that we aren't experiencing it yet.

teachings.title: Prove all things with scripture
teachings.summary: Says pride keeps people from accepting doctrine shown from scripture, and that believers should know the word by reading it daily rather than relying on other people's theology. Urges reading the whole Bible and then reading it again.
teachings.text:
A lot of people have pride keeping them from acknowledging doctrine from scripture when shown, because it would mean their lazy, Reddit Christianity is exposed. Admitting they were fooled, and accepted what they're taught, rather than comparing and proving all things taught with scripture. Directly. By knowing the word, reading it daily in the spirit, not reading someone else's theology, or listening to someone else tell you what it means, or googling and cherry picking isolated verses to justify your dogma. Deboonking instead of letting God just tell you. 

It's such a snare for so many. 

Read the entire Bible. And then read it again.

teachings.title: The birds were gleaning
teachings.summary: Tells how birds that kept pests out of his garden were eating his peas, and how the Spirit reminded him of gleaning and that the ox that treads out the corn is not muzzled. Ends with his frustration gone and praise for God's garden.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 19:9-10**

*And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest. And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am the LORD your God.*

***Deuteronomy 24:19-21**

*When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands. When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.*

Keep this in mind.

So this year the garden has been very good to us, we've been blessed with healthy plants and few diseases. The harmful insects have been kept to a minimum thanks to so many birds nesting in and around the chicken coop. We added some birdhouses last year, and so far this year they have been phenomenal in keeping harmful bug population to almost zero.

The peas did exceptionally well this year, and produced over 6 gallon bags of pods of big, delicious sweet peas. Normally the plants have died off by this point but, despite the heat and the drought like conditions, several of the vines are still healthy and producing, and there are even new flowers forming daily as it crawls across the trellis. It's providing noontime shade for my massive cukes and cherry tomatoes.

I had harvested the last big batch about a week and a half ago, and I was letting the stragglers develop before taking them as well.

But then I began to notice discarded pea shells all around the bush of vines.

The same day I noticed a baby chipmunk run across the yard away from the peas.

Of course I assumed that was the culprit. I set traps and threw mothballs throughout the yard coffee grounds, peppermint spray. 

The traps never triggered, and the pea pods kept falling, chewed open and hollowed out.

Naturally I redoubled my efforts and, still, no joy. More and more dead pods littering the ground.

So today I stopped and just watched for a while, a little frustrated, and asking God for protection from the vermin. To extend the hedge.

As I'm praying, talking to God, I see that the birds, the same birds who all year have been keeping the harmful bugs away from my plants, feasting on peas. 

They took out an early infestation of Denver potato beetles. I found maybe three Beatles one day crushed them, and then watched birds decimate them over the next week.

Beetles that attacked my squash and cucumbers last year, did not make a reappearance and a white fly infestation at my cabbage was swiftly dealt with. 

It was those same birds, coming through my pea patch and eating all my peas.

God said to me "they're gleaning." The Spirit reminding me of the practice, bringing all things into remembrance. A laborer gets its reward. *Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn.*

And, just like that my Elmer Fudd frustration disappeared.

Of course this means next year I probably have to net them early.

Easily 10' high and climbing. The cuke is going up the tomatoes and beans going up that.

This is God's garden.

teachings.title: Finding a church
teachings.summary: Gives two directories of KJV Independent Baptist churches and his own criteria for choosing one: the Trinity, deity of Christ, salvation by faith alone, KJV only and soul winning. Lists things to avoid, such as contemporary music, Lordship salvation, women leaders and Ruckmanite teaching.
teachings.text:
Quite a few people have come into my chat or in others, asking about finding a church to go to, so as to not forsake the assembly, and maybe find a church home.

And

teachings.title: Primary doctrine and incidental opinions
teachings.summary: Says a belief is not Biblical doctrine unless scripture clearly spells it out, separating primary doctrines such as literal creation from secondary matters like the exact age of the earth. Urges not becoming dogmatic over the firmament or other worldly things, and hearing sound doctrine from preachers who hold the gospel of grace alone.
teachings.text:
Just because you believe something about the world to be true, doesn't make it Biblical doctrine. It actually has to be clearly spelled out in scripture, and even then other than the Gospel and a few primary doctrines, there's interpretation of secondary and tertiary doctrine that's open for discussion and then there are things people try to get the Bible to comment on that it simply doesn't. 

Literal creation is a primary doctrine. Biblical age as determined by generations is secondary. Earth being precisely 6,482 years old is interpretation that has Biblical basis, but is incidental, bearing no real importance in our spiritual walk, and good faith people of faith can disagree. 

Too many place their own beliefs of incidental and worldly things far to high in the order of importance.

Many, many, many of the people in our circles, especially young men who are aimless, lost, broken by trauma, or babes in Christ and culturally Christian but not quite there yet, need to hear hard preaching on sin and practical application of Biblical truths to their spiritual life and walk with Christ, from preachers who adhere to the Gospel of salvation by faith alone, in grace alone, plus nothing, minus nothing. 

And that preacher's idea or opinion of worldly things differing from your own shouldn't be a hindrance from hearing sound doctrine of spiritual things. 

If it is, you need to reevaluate what's important to you.

My preference for Easton's definition of Firmament in the Bible, over Nave's or Smith's, or even Webster's, doesn't make it doctrine. Simple as. 

It could just be the expanse, the reach of the heavens. "Firm" being in the word doesn't make it solid, even if I believe it to be. 

Don't project your opinions of the worldly onto scripture and become dogmatic in things that are ultimately not important. 

Sons of Belial, Jews and reprobates, being liars and leading persecution and engaging in subversion is true, because the Bible tells us so, explicitly. We don't have to prove they lie about the shape of the earth, or space, or age of creation, etc to prove they lie. Examples are simply signs to read, and the truth to ponder and wonder about.

teachings.title: The shape of the earth is not Bible doctrine
teachings.summary: Says neither the flat nor the globe view is Biblical doctrine and that doubting someone's salvation over it is wrong. Warns that wonder at world events must not outrank a relationship with God, and that nothing is known for certain apart from Christ and him crucified.
teachings.text:
The shape of the earth isn't Biblical doctrine, and both FEs and globers claims that it is are foolish. 

And suggestions that either view isn't saved, based only on whatever preferred theory they have about it is uncalled for. Not only uncalled for, but an indication that you think belief in the shape of the earth being round or flat is part of the Gospel, and so it casts doubts on your own salvation. Don't do it. 

And, as always, this *not* an invitation to try and prove your view is the real biblical one to me.

If your wonder at what's going on all around you in the world is more important than your spiritual relationship with God, your priorities are wrong and you need to get right with Jesus.

This goes for fears and cares of this world. They should be an incidental distraction or a sign of the times, to observe. Not your religion.

And if you think you know for certain anything other than Christ and him crucified, you're a fool.

teachings.title: Luke 21 and the so-called three snares
teachings.summary: Answers a preacher's claim of a secret doctrine of three snares in Luke 21:34, showing that the snare in verse 35 refers back to the day of the Lord. Explains the order of events from Matthew 24, the signs, and why believers who watch will not be caught unawares.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:33-36**

*33 Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

34 And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so **that day** come upon you unawares.

35 For as **a snare** shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

36 Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.*

This caught my attention scrolling through Telegram, and because I wasn't certain what he was talking about by these so-called "three snares," I watched a little bit of the video. 

Wiles claims that Luke 21:34 seems as if it is a non sequitur, that Jesus in talking about the end times throws this bit about surfeiting, drunkenness and cares of this life in to his preaching, and that these are the secret "three snares" that all Christians must avoid if they want to go to heaven when Jesus'second coming is here. 

Rick Wiles and his co-host, Doc Burkhart further say they've never heard anyone else who claims to be an end times prophecy expert mention this doctrine Wiles "discovered." And they chastise viewers who don't "buy and read books" that could explain the "mysteries of Revelation" to them. He then hocks the second edition of his own book. 

That's all within the first 5 minutes. 

(Just to be clear for those wondering, surfeiting is a word that means being full of something that you've overindulged in)

When we turn to the actual chapter and verse in question, we see that the snare that is referred to in verse 35, refers back up to "that day," meaning the day of the Lord. The second coming, after the tribulation in those days, where the dead in Christ are risen and called up into the clouds, followed by the living who are saved at that time, caught up with Jesus, and the wrath of God begins being poured out for the next three and a half years. 

Jesus has just finished telling the apostles exactly the order of events, and how it will play out. We see the same account in Matthew 24. Jesus tells them, and us, that we will know that the time is growing close. We will see the signs. His coming will not be a surprise to those of us who are paying attention and who are studying his word and praying because all of those other things will have come to pass leading up to it. There are three and a half years of Great tribulation on Earth with the Antichrist and the persecution of the saints. He tells the parable of the fig tree, to draw a comparison to how you know what season it is based on these observations. Jesus warning about not being so full of the cares of this world, caught up and drunkenness, caught up in a form of worldly gluttony, so that we are able to pay attention to those signs and, that's not be caught unawares. Because it's to the unsaved that his coming will be like a thief in the night. That carnal Christians who are backslidden and not keeping their mind towards God, will also be taken by surprise, potentially.

Wiles turns this into some kind of weird works-based doctrine that if you're unhealthy, be it gluttony, drunk or a worry wart, you won't get saved when Jesus returns.

teachings.title: Repent means a change of mind, not turning from sin
teachings.summary: Says repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief to believing God's word, and that turning from sin is something everyone tries for many reasons, none of which save. Uses Jonah 3:10 to show God repented and the phrase repent of sin is not in the Bible.
teachings.text:
Repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief in something to justify us before God, or turning from unbelief to believing His word. It's a changing of mind. I don't know anyone who is counting on their sin to justify them or bring them to righteousness, so repenting of sin in this context is foolish.  

Everyone, saved and unsaved feels regret and shame for their sin and, when conscious of it, tries to turn away from specific sins, whether through conscience sake, guilt, trying to work their way to self righteousness, trying to please others, to avoid punishment or consequences of their sin, etc ... 

The reprobate doesn't turn from sin out of guilt or to please God, but often will to avoid tradeoffs and mitigate consequences and risk. A reprobate may quit smoking, drinking, abstain from more vile affections for fear of jail. 

Everyone turns from sin at various points in their lives. 

We have things like New Years resolutions, diet and weight loss industry, screen time monitoring apps, aids to quit smoking, swear jars,  #NoNutNovember, appeals to "common decency," etc...all expressions of God's law written in our hearts bringing us to try and turn from the harmful and wicked things we do, for a variety of reasons and motives, selfish and selfless. 

None of that saves. 

Only faith in the risen Christ and belief in the promise of God that Jesus is the sole propitiation for all sin can save us.

*But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them;
I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land*

**Jonah 3:10**

 *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Now this verse is not about spiritual salvation, it is about the physical salvation of the city of Nineveh who God had sent Jonah to be a prophet unto them and get them to repent of their wicked ways or he was going to destroy their city and kill all of them. Of course Jonah objects because they're not Israelites and he doesn't think that they deserve a warning then of course God corrects him on that but that's a story for a different time, what's interesting here is that we both see that repentance, or turning away from sin is viewed as a work by God, AND it shows that repenting cannot always mean "...of sin," because we see God who cannot sin repenting of the destruction he was going to visit on them having seen their good works 

So in one verse you have evidence that repenting of sin is a work, and that repentance does not always mean of sin, because God does it.

By the way this is the closest verse you can find in the Bible where repent of sin, or turning from evil ways, is mentioned. 

The phrase "repent of sin* doesn't appear anywhere in the Bible. And the concept relative to salvation appears nowhere in any of the Gospels or the Acts of Apostles or any of the Epistles. Where the term repent or even turn away, appear, it's always explicitly spelled out what they need to repent from, and turn towards believing God.

teachings.text:
**Fun fact**: Of 105 instances of the term "repent" or "repentance," contained in the authorized translation, the KJV, the modern versions eliminate its use in 46 verses.

Curiously, it is fairly consistent when they choose to change scripture. The NIV and other other corrupt Bible transitions eliminate the 35 different times God is said to "repent" in scripture. Essentially removing from scripture the idea that God can repent. The only rationale one can draw from that is they know the idea of a sinless God repenting undermines their subversive, heretical claim that "repent" automatically means "turn from sin." They also remove other instances such as Exodus 13:17 and Matthew 27:3, which complicate the false works-based doctrine that they are trying to teach. 

It is impossible to come to any other conclusion than that is the agenda behind their selective censorship of the term from any instance that undermines their wicked doctrine.

teachings.title: What reprobate doctrine explains

teachings.text:
Reprobate doctrine explains who they are, what their traits are, how they get where they are, what they're willing to do, and scripture tells us what as a nation we are to do with them. Twice-dead, conscience seared, dogs, abominations, deserving death, their blood be upon them.  

It's a spiritual state as much being a born again Christian, saved by faith, or an unbelieving sinner, damned at death if they don't repent and believe on Jesus Christ alone.

Reprobate Doctrine is God giving you the who, the what and the why. Even the how, as far as creeping into a church unawares, etc. It gives examples in government, in false prophets, in nations turning from God. Individual people such as Judas. Sodomites in general. Antichrists who deny Jesus. 
The when is always, and waxing worse in the later days. 

You can't fight them if you think you can save them or that their strange lusts and unnatural affections are normal sin.

teachings.title: Reprobate doctrine and false religion
