teachings.text:
You don't have have to understand the reprobate doctrine to be saved, but it's hard to deny it if you are. 

False religion that teaches there is no such thing as reprobation, that sodomites and pedophilia are "normal sin" and if you "repent of it" you can go to heaven get basic salvation wrong, damn their followers and so it's no wonder they don't teach the biblical doctrine that explains these sons of Belial.

teachings.title: God repented: the Bible's own definition of repent
teachings.summary: Quotes Jonah 3:10 to show that repent means a change of mind, and that God repenting of the evil He said He would do cannot mean turning from sin. Says the Bible defines itself.
teachings.text:
**Jonah 3:10**
 
A*nd God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Here we get the biblical definition of repent, God changing His mind, AND the acknowledgement that "turning from their evil ways" ie "Repenting of sin" = works.

The Bible defines itself.

In before spergs conflate physical salvation of nations, in the world with eternal salvation of individual souls in the Spirit.

teachings.title: Perfect contrition is a work, not grace
teachings.summary: Says believers confess to God knowing grace is never lost, and that working to maintain grace makes grace no more grace. Calls the act of perfect contrition a loophole that rests on the sinner and not on the blood of Christ.
teachings.text:
This is so wicked. We confess our sins to God knowing He's forgiven them already, that we have eternal grace that's never lost or taken away, in Christ Jesus. 

Working to maintain God's grace makes grace no more grace.

In fact, this work, this "act of perfect contrition," is simply a license to sin while disobeying the Gospel. A get out of jail free loophole that has nothing to do with Jesus. It requires the sinner to be 100% honest, 100% contrite, about 100% of their sins, that depends on the sinner alone, not the blood of Christ.

teachings.title: Answering the works-salvation reading of Matthew 7 and the rich young man
teachings.summary: Answers a Greek Orthodox argument that those who listed their works in Christ's name were relying on faith alone. Points out the text condemns the very doctrine of works for salvation.
teachings.text:
This is from Greek Orthodox Church of America. They legitimately are arguing that the people in Jesus teaching, telling Him all the works they did in His name, were relying on faith alone to save them. The exact opposite of what's being taught by Christ. 

They cannot see the discrepancy. They do not have the ability to. 

Note that this is not Cherry picked out of context, but condemns precisely the doctrine they are defending, works for salvation.

Here again, shortly after conceding that scripture says by the deeds of the law are no men saved, they cite this story of Christ testing a rich young man who lied and claimed was sinless, and was exposed when he refused to give up his wealth to follow Christ. 

As the Bible says, *As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.*

teachings.title: What repent means: Acts 26:20
teachings.summary: Shows from Paul's testimony in Acts 26 that repent means to turn from false beliefs and turn to God, and that works meet for repentance follow salvation. Distinguishes knowing one is a sinner from repentance, and says faith alone saves.
teachings.text:
To be explicitly clear so no one can misunderstand:

We must turn from false beliefs regarding righteousness, and turn to believing God's report, obeying the Gospel, by trusting in Jesus Christ alone as the sole propitiation for our sins. This is what the Bible says **repent** means. 

But before we repent and believe, we have to first recognize we are sinners in need of salvation, damned without Christ. 

This is *not the same* as repentance, although it could be *the reason* for repenting. 

Knowing you're going to Hell and that God is offering you a way out is sufficient to bring many to repent and believe. Knowing God is just and not a liar is also sufficient to bring one to turn from the unfruitful and believe. 

According to the Bible, all men know the law written in their hearts, that they are sinners and worthy of death, and in need of salvation. *That they have no excuse. (Romans 1:20-21).
*
I hope that clears it up for everyone.

In Acts 26, Paul gives his testimony to Agrippa. 

Many false teachers point to this chapter, and verse 20 specifically, where Paul says that after his acceptance of salvation in Christ, he began his ministry and "*shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.*"

What the subtle false prophet will do here is rhetorically ignore the clear meaning of the complete thought "repent and turn to God," remove the "and," and count on people not understanding what "do works meet for repentance" means. 

Repent means turn from. Nothing more or less. In this verse the context is clear: turn from whatever is keeping from believing God and turn towards God. Period. There is no mention of anything else here. If you were believing on something else to justify you, being a good person, worshipping idols and dead gods, turning from sin... anything else, turn away from that, repent, and turn to God. Not towards God. But fully turn to God instead.

AND, which as a conjunction here implies "then" rather than cumulative, do works meet, meaning worthy of, that aforementioned repentance. 

We are called once saved to do works worthy of that salvation. Reading Paul's epistles we see that is consistent with everything he wrote. Exhortation and edifying to act as one having repented and believed, and by faith been saved.

I would love to move on but this heresy persists and is spread by many in error, because false prophets appeal to our natural man nature that our salvation is in ourselves, in our hands, that we can maintain salvation by being self-righteous, that it's not a free gift from God.

BTW read all of Act 26, and see what Paul's testimonial of his own conversion entailed. He describes his false belief as a Pharisee, his persecution of those who had believed on Christ, that it was his thought, within himself to do these things. He believed he was right, in other words. And then he saw the light:

*13 At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

14 And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

15 And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

16 But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

17 Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

18 To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

19 Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

*Paul in his own testimony says he had believed one way, sees the light believes Jesus' word, and now believes on Him. Biblical repentance.

Further he explains his ministry to the Gentiles, to turn them, which is the meaning of repent, from dark to light. From Satan to God. For what purpose? So they would have to "repent of their sin" to be saved?  Or in turning to light, to God, be saved and *have forgiveness of sins and inheritance *of those who have also been saved, *sanctified *by the same faith Paul has. Not by their "turning from sin" but by their faith in God.

This is the Gospel. Anyone preaching another is accursed. Period. No matter what else they may get right, if they do not get this correct they are false teachers.

Now again I stipulate that man is by nature one who seems to square circles and close gaps when faced with seemingly conflicting ideas, to bring them into harmony. 

Because of this, many believers who have accepted Christ unto salvation and then are exposed to preaching that tells them that they must repent of their sins in order to be saved, again a concept that doesn't exist in the Bible, will automatically in their own mind, take that to mean "admitting their are a sinner and regretting their sins," which all saved Christians would likely say was part of their coming to belief. 

But it was their faith that saves them, not acknowledging they need salvation, not regretting their sin. But believing Jesus died and was raised again so that God can give us the free gift of forgiveness and eternal life. 

There can be several reasons one accepts God at His word, but it is that acceptance, turning from not believing to trusting Him, that saves.

And so those who mentally put "of your sins" after "repent," and think it means acknowledge/regret, are in error, but not to the point of it being damnable heresy. Not at all. They are taking a biblical concept, applying the wrong word to it based on ignorance and hearing it said by so many, and just assuming that's what it means. 

But those who preach that we must turn from sin to be saved or to keep eternal salvation, that it is a necessary step, where our actions factor in to salvation, are teaching a damnable heresy of works salvation, and they should be rejected.

teachings.title: The virtuous woman of Proverbs 31
teachings.summary: Reads Proverbs 31:10-31 as the Biblical model of a virtuous woman who keeps her house and also works. Says single and newly married men often hold a distorted view of what a good woman is like.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 31:10-31**

*10 Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

11 The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.

12 She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

13 She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

14 She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

15 She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.

16 She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

17 She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.

18 She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.

19 She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

20 She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

21 She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.

22 She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.

23 Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.

24 She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

25 Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

26 She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.

27 She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

28 Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.

29 Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.

30 Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

31 Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.*

This is the Biblical model for a virtuous woman. The trad wife blueprint. 

Notice that she takes care of the house and has a side hustle or more, to the benefit of her household (rather than some megacorp). She has her own honor, keeps the fruit of her labors and loves the Lord.

It's not that women didn't work at all. It's not that they were just a passive, submissive combo of an easy bake oven, real doll, birthing chamber, nanny cam and Roomba.  

They were industrious for their house and themselves. They crafted. They had market gardens. They bartered and traded. They built up a reputation based on their own merits and labors. That's the ideal as much as cooking the meals and raising and educating the children.

I think unmarried or newly married guys in our thing have a distorted view of what a good woman is like, and their roles. Especially over time as children grow.

teachings.title: Faith without works in James 2
teachings.summary: Explains that James 2 is not about salvation but about faith that offers nothing to people in need. Urges believers to help those around them and not to be respecters of persons.
teachings.text:
Oh yeah, I remember what I was going to say. 

Even sincere Christians can fall into this trap, by the way. The thoughts and prayers and proselytizing, rather than helping is exactly what James to is talking about when it says that faith without works is dead. It has nothing to do with salvation it has everything to do with this tendency to spout off or passively "care," and offer nothing substantial to people in need, now.

**James 2**
*14 What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

15 If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

16 And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

17 Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone
*
Be mindful of allowing your faith to be of no use to anyone, but instead help people around you in need. Bring it alive. And don't be a respecter of persons. Condescend to the lowly. Be a good judge to the fatherless.

teachings.title: Matthew 24:22 and the pre-trib rapture
teachings.summary: Reads Matthew 24:19-22 and asks why the days would be shortened for the elect if the saved were raptured before them. Calls the pre-tribulation rapture a false doctrine, while saying he does not believe the tribulation is here.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 24**

*19 And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!
20 But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day:

21 For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.

22 And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened*.

The context is obvious with the current situation, although this is meant for the jews and days of vengence against them. But since they're creating the conditions for the end times artificially, it makes sense it's artificial milk that's run dry. 

BTW vs 22 lays the Dispy "pre-trib" rapture out flat. Why should the days of tribulation be shortened for the saved if they're raptured before it happens? Foolish false doctrine.

To be clear, I do not believe we are in the tribulation, but any appearance to the contrary is entirely intentional. IMO

teachings.title: Once saved always saved: proof texts
teachings.summary: A run of passages for the security of the believer: kept by the power of God in 1 Peter 1, Galatians 5 against adding a work, Hebrews 13:5 and Deuteronomy 31:6 on never being forsaken, and 1 John 5 on eternal life given in the Son.
teachings.text:
**1 Peter 1:4-9**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath **begotten us again** **unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,** **To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,
Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.** Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:
That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:
Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory:
Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.*

Anyone who says we are not saved unto everlasting life, with eternal security, is a liar and is damned. If you're caught up in this false teaching, repent and believe the word of God.

**Galatians 5**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

2 Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

3 For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

4 Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.

5 For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith.

6 For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love.*

If you are counting on your own ability not to sin, you are a debtor to the whole of the law and Christ is of no effect. You are fallen from grace. Not in the sense that you've lost your salvation, but that you've never had it. 

You can substitute anything in the place of circumcision in this chapter. Baptism, repenting of sin, going to church... anything, and once you add any condition to the grace and faith in Christ to your belief for salvation (or maintaining salvation) you now are a debtor to the WHOLE of the Law. "*If you offend in one point," *in commission or omission, you are damned. *Christ is become of no effect unto you.*

"Repent of sins" or "you can lose your salvation" are damnable heresy because no one can repent of all sin, and no one saved by faith alone can lose it. Anyone giving these as part of their "gospel" is a false teacher who isn't giving people a "lively hope," but an impossible task.

Literally there were people at the church of Galatia convinced that they needed to do *something *in order to be saved. They added a work to the Gospel, and Paul head to write to tell them that in doing so they made the Gospel of no effect. The same impulse rules men today that make them unable to believe that God would give them eternal life with no strings attached, and the delusion they place themselves under to maintain that false belief keeps them fallen from grace.

Ok, one more swing at this dead horse:

**Hebrews 13:5** 
*Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.*

**Deuteronomy 31:6**
*Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.*

How can you be content with what you have, be strong and without fear, if you believe God the Father will abandon you? How can you call Him a liar when He says He will never leave or forsake His children?

I think one of the most toxic things about the current culture of illegitimacy and divorce we are mired in, that all of us have experienced either directly, as children or in our families, makes people suspicious of unconditional love, and unable to grasp a heavenly Father who won't abandon His sons

Ok, one more proof text for OSAS. Don't miss it, or you might be calling God who cannot lie a liar:


**1 John 5**
*7 For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.

8 And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one.

9 If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son.

10 He that believeth on the Son of God **hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.

11 And this is the record, that God hath given to us **eternal** life, and this life is in his Son*

teachings.title: Fear is a sin: step away from what feeds it
teachings.summary: Advises walking away from online content that leaves a believer afraid or anxious, since anything that does not edify one's service to God is a sin to engage in. Warns against becoming loyal to the source that sells the fear.
teachings.text:
I don't know who might need to hear this, but if any of the things that you're finding online, be it political, conspiracy theory stuff, White identity stuff, great reset / great replacement, w e f Black Rock and whatever else... If it leaves you more afraid, if it gives you anxiety and controls your thought patterns and behaviors, rather than entertain and amuse, inform, edify or give you a like-minded community to belong to, stop engaging in it. 

If the fake and gay gets too real and hard for you, you're better off walking away. Being simple about evil as the Bible says. If something isn't edifying you and your ability to serve God, then engaging in it is a sin. Fear is a sin.

I confess sometimes the food stuff gets me and I want to be sure I can feed my family, but a lot of the spiritual aspect of growing my own food has taught me to fear a lot less and to trust God a lot more.

Also if that fear makes you become fiercely loyal to whatever source of information is feeding that fear to make merchandise of it? To become the content you consume? Defending it like a junkie protecting his dealer?

Step away for a while. There's nothing you can really do online anyway and they're selling you fear wraped in false hope.

teachings.title: Romans 13: Paul obeyed authority in faith
teachings.summary: Notes that Paul wrote Romans 13 under Roman rule and obeyed authority unless it conflicted with God. Points to Paul staying in the Philippian jail to win the jailer, who is told only to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ.
teachings.text:
And Romans 13 is written 250yrs before that satanic, judaized death cult was founded by Satan, and Paul in the spirit says ALL authority, whomever it is under - state, family, community, employment, all, is to be obeyed unless it conflicts with a higher authority, God being ultimate. 

Catholics not create false doctrine challenge, impossible

FFS the Romans were in charge and persecuting Christians when he wrote that. They had Paul under house arrest, chained to a guard. 

Paul trusted God and obeyed authority, in faith.

Paul could have escaped the Philippian jail after the divine earthquake, but he stayed to get the jailer saved in Acts 16:25-31

*25 And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

26 And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.

27 And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

teachings.title: The New Testament church: local, independent and Jesus-led
teachings.summary: Describes the churches the Apostles planted as local, independent and led by a pastor, with one Gospel and doctrine from Scripture alone. Notes that sects adding to the word crept in and sought control, yet never extinguished the true faith.
teachings.text:
Biblical churches planted by the Apostles were local, independent, Jesus-led, via a pastor aka a bishop or bishopric. Elders of the church sent evangelists out to start new independent churches, and members were sent out as the priesthood of believers to win souls locally. 

They had one Gospel, the doctrine came directly from scripture and had no hidden or extra-biblical offices, rites or oral tradition that wasn't also found in scripture. 

Heretical sects who added to the word of God crept in and demanded regional control for political ends, and were rebuked and turned out by some, and accepted by others. And as much as those sects gained power and persecuted the believers, hid the knowledge of truth, and enslaved followers with the chains of works, they never could extinguish the true faith. #TrailOfBlood

teachings.text:
If abortion is made illegal without men being responsible for both the mother and child that results from fornication, you have not solved the problem, you've just slightly shifted the immorality calculus.

Here's the thing; by a man's fornication you don't just make the child, but you make the woman a mother. 

Polygamy, despite what Mormons might say, isn't condoned by God in the Bible. But what is suggested by God's law is the man, by engaging in fornication, or adultery, that results in a child is now on the hook for providing for both the mother, and the child. 

There's no getting around that.

Making abortion illegal is all fine and good but it was only allowed to proliferate because men had absolved themselves of these responsibilities that come from their sin

teachings.title: 2 John: abide in the doctrine of Christ
teachings.summary: Walks through 2 John by question and answer: the truth that dwells in us, the commandment to walk in love, and the deceivers who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh.
teachings.text:
2 John is written to whom? "all they that have known the truth"

And what is it that dwells within us? For how long?

For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever

And what commandment should they walk in?

And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.

What are deceivers doing? 
For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist.

Do the deceivers have both father and son? 
Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son.

If someone comes in to your house (or chat) not bringing the doctrine of Christ, what then? 
If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed

Why?
For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.

So then what are the dangers of not doing that?
Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

Is this epistle about salvation or about tolerating false prophets and in doing so, being partakers of their evil and undoing works and losing rewards (the payment God gives the saved for their work Romans 4)? 

Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

teachings.title: All evil in 1 Timothy 6:10
teachings.summary: Quotes 1 Timothy 6:10 and shows that modern versions change "all evil" to "all kinds of evil", which lets teachers say "all" does not mean all elsewhere.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 6**
*10 For the love of money is the root of **all** evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows
*
ESV (Evil Satanic Version) changes it to "all kinds of evil" and that allows special boys claim "all kinds" doesn't mean all, and so other places all is used, that it means "Not all." Then they mumble something about the Greek, because they don't believe God when he promised to preserve His word, because they don't believe God when he says "whosoever," the world, "every," and "all." 

Seriously, that's how they rationalize it.

If your doctrine requires you be multilingual, calls God a liar, you should rethink it. 

"My looking at Strong's where a alcohol drinking, tattooed, earring wearing walking pedophile-physiognomied false prophet told me too", is not better than the 50 odd translators of the KJV and those before them, Bishops and Tyndale's, the other 4 attempts that led to the 1611 authorized, *refined like silver 7 times.* 

It's not.

 It's foolish.

teachings.title: Man's choice in the Bible: free will against Reformed theology
teachings.summary: Points to the first commandment in the garden, the freewill offerings and the choices of the Old and New Testament as proof that man has a choice to believe. Answers the Reformed use of Proverbs 16:9 and sets Titus 2:11 against it.
teachings.text:
"What must I do to be saved?" 

Repent, change your mind about what you place your trust in, and believe on the Lord.

"Sorry, I don't have free will. Gonna have to see if God makes me. Thanks anyway, arminian!"

**Genesis 2**

*15 And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

16 And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

17 But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
*
Special boys "show me in the Bible where man has a choice! One verse!" 

Literally the first interaction God has with man is giving him one.

A simple bible study on the choices made by man throughout the Old Testament and New, and their consequences for not believing the Lord dispels the notion that there is no free will. The fact that God puts emphasis on sacrifices being free will sacrifices, pointing to Jesus and our choice to believe in His, should be sufficient. But it's the point of the entire Bible. 

Random example pop to my head, the book of Judges where "every man did that which was right in his own eyes" is the theme. That's them choosing to do what's right in their own eyes rather than in God's.

If Reformed Theology was simply **Proverbs 16:9,** it wouldn't be damnable heresy. 

*A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps*

Instead that's the Motte and Bailey they fall back to when their false doctrines are attacked, "So you're saying the Lord doesn't direct man's steps?"

What will also often happen to these reformed special boys, when cornered with verse and logic, is they will demure, saying "oh I'm not a strict five point" or whatever and back down from whichever unsupported view that's been exposed, to maintain whatever other view isn't being discussed currently. Like arguing with a liberal, it becomes nailing Jello to the wall.

The calvinist giving their version of the "good news" is like a timeshare condo pitch that says "good news, you may have won a free weekend at one of our resorts..." It's just so obviously gross.

**Titus 2:11-12**

*11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to **all men**,

12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;*

teachings.title: God is not the author of evil
teachings.summary: Gathers James 1:13-14, Ecclesiastes 7:29, Jeremiah 19:5 and Romans 1:30 to show that God does not tempt or devise evil, and that men invent it. Answers the claim of total depravity that ascribes every wicked thing to God.
teachings.text:
**James 1**
*13 Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: 14 But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.*

**Ecclesiastes 7**
*29 Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions*.

Jeremiah 19
*5 They have built also the high places of Baal, to burn their sons with fire for burnt offerings unto Baal, which I commanded not, nor spake it, **neither came it into my mind:***

Romans 1
*30 Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, **inventors of evil things,** disobedient to parents*,

James White is a reprobate. His damnable heresies require him to ascribe to God every wicked thing White and his fellow sons of Belial come up with. They believe in "total depravity" and call all men reprobate, because that is what they are. 

**2 Peter 2**
*1 But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction*.

teachings.title: Free will and the Calvinist "and"
teachings.summary: Says false doctrines are held by trading one false either/or for another instead of taking the Word as it is. Argues that denying man's choice denies the point of Scripture, and that Lordship and Reformed answers always add "believe AND...".
teachings.text:
What they do is position themselves within a theological false binary and endlessly rationalize their (false) positions based on what other (equally false) positions are, rather than just accepting the Word as is. 

When poked, they will invariably argue you're the opposing binary. It is a red-blue mentality applied to religion. It's how theological traps work (and all similar false binary rhetorical traps, too)

And because they can't escape from these prebuilt either/ors to see their own error, they can't reach understanding.

This is especially true in those who think they are clever special boys, because the snare is designed to hook their pride, and the larger their pride, the more entangled they become.

What those who deny man's free will in choosing to perish or accept God's word cannot explain is why, if it is His will who be given faith, (rather than God's will being "*all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth*"), why did He create all of Scripture as His testimony, and make spreading the Gospel, the Good News of that promise, the means of propagating salvation, "from faith to faith?" To having witnesses that His word is true?

They can't explain why there was His law in the garden, even one commandment, that Adam and Eve should have choice. That the entire OT is presenting the lineage of choice for both inheritance and blessing. Denying the will of man, denies the entire point of the Word, and ultimately that belief on that word is what saves us.

As for Reformed Theology and Lordship, they claim that their "surrendering to Lord Jesus," to make themselves "slaves to Him," (rather than servants, because slave denotes not having a choice), they aren't actually trusting in Him alone. They are trusting their corruptible flesh to perfectly obey, and instead of showing complete faith in God, putting it all on themselves.

That's not even getting into the blasphemy of claiming God dictates all manner of wickedness and sin, being an absolute sovereign of the world. (Reprobate James White claimed pedophiles rape kids because it is God's will, for example).

When asked how to be saved it's always "believe AND..." It is the "and" that damns them.

teachings.title: Wisdom by the word and the rod of reproof
teachings.summary: Quotes Proverbs 1:22-28 and John 16:8-12 to show that God grants wisdom by His word and by reproof, and that the Holy Ghost both gives wisdom and reproves.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 1:22-28**

*22 How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?

23 Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.

24 Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;

25 But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:

26 I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;

27 When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.

28 Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:*

God grants us wisdom by His word and by the rod of reproof. The Holy Spirit is the person of God who both gives wisdom as He gives reproof.

**John 16:8-12**

*8 And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

9 Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10 Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11 Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.

12 I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.*

When the Holy Spirit talks to you, have an ear to listen. That comes from prayer and reading and reflecting on God's word throughout the day.

teachings.title: Jesus the author and finisher of our faith
teachings.summary: Reads Hebrews 12:2 to show that Jesus is the Word of God, the author of what we believe and its finisher. Warns against reading the verse as Christ giving the ability to believe rather than the Gospel we have faith in.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 12**
*2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.*

Jesus is the Word of God. He is the author of what we believe on, and its finisher, having come as promised to do God's will.

Some, misguided by heretics see this verse as Christ literally giving faith, the ability to believe, rather than giving us the Gospel we have faith in. It's foolishness.

teachings.title: The Spirit reproves the world of sin: because they believe not on Me
teachings.summary: Reads John 16:7-11 and notes the KJV word is reprove, not convict, and that the sin named is not believing on Jesus. Warns that the newer versions' wording opens the door to repent-of-your-sin works salvation.
teachings.text:
**John 16:7-11**

*7 Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.

8 And when he is come, he will **reprove** the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

9 Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10 Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11 Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged*.

Public Service Announcement: In false new age versions, they use "convict" rather than the precise term, "reprove" in this verse, so they can insert the false doctrine of "repent-of-your-sin" works salvation. Don't be fooled!

When Jesus says the Holy Spirit will reprove for sin, note what the sin is; not believing on Him.

teachings.title: No limbo: Old Testament saints were saved by faith
teachings.summary: Shows that Adam and all Old Testament saints went to Heaven by faith in God's word, and that Limbo and purgatory are inventions. Points to Christ as the lamb slain before the foundation of the world and the blood on the mercy seat.
teachings.text:
No they didn't. "Limbo" is an invention of the RCC. 

Saved Christians know that Adam, and all OT saints, went to Heaven, the same way we do; faith in God's word. Jesus went to Hell to pay the price for all sin, Adam's to yours, and beyond. He freed the saved in the Old Testament the same way He's freed us. With His blood. 

Repent and get saved today! It's a free gift from God, and no institutions of man can give it to you, or deny His grace to you.

The Bible says that Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. That He was "foreordained before the foundation of the world." All believers were called upon to "inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The notion of Limbo comes from unsaved false prophets, like Clement of Alexandria, who not understanding simple salvation, sought to rectify the ways of God to the feeble understanding of a natural man, stating that "it's not right" that the Patriarchs, "should be condemned without trial," when the wages of sin has always been death. Natural man questioning God's judgement is the source of most heresy. 

The scriptures teach us that there are none righteous, "no not one," and that since the first generation of man, we have been justified by faith alone calling upon the name of the Lord. 

Heaven and Hell. Those are the two choices before every man. There is no limbo. There is no purgatory. There is no working your way to righteousness. There is only the blood of the lamb on the mercy seat. The burnt offering of Christ. Amen.

teachings.title: The Antichrist deceives the lost, not the saved
teachings.summary: Corrects the idea that saved Christians will be deceived by the Antichrist, from 2 Thessalonians 2: those deceived are those who received not the love of the truth. Adds that name-only Christians are likely to be his biggest supporters.
teachings.text:
This is a category error. Those being deceived aren't saved Christians. The Antichrist does not deceive believers, but those who dwell in inequity. 

**2 Thessalonians 2**
*7 For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.

8 And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:

9 Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,

10 And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.

11 And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:

12 That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

Of course, this doesn't mean Evangelicals and Catholics and other sects that are ostensibly Christian, but in name only, can't be deceived. In fact, they are highly likely to be, as they aren't believers on Christ and saved by faith. If anything, they will be the biggest supporters of the Antichrist when he gains power.
